articles.title: ‘Closed, but not locked’: Inside Israel’s secret villa for girls fleeing violence and abuse
articles.summary: Removed from their homes, sometimes without clothes, bags or phones, dozens of girls and young women find refuge each year at a confidential shelter in southern Israel, where they learn to rebuild trust and experience life without fear
paragraphs: Removed from their homes, sometimes without clothes, bags or phones, dozens of girls and young women find refuge each year at a confidential shelter in southern Israel, where they learn to rebuild trust and experience life without fear

Two years have passed, but Sarah still remembers the day she arrived at the shelter. She was 16, and nothing could have prepared her for finding herself in a villa in southern Israel, cut off from the outside world and unable to contact her family.
"It was a slap in the face," she recalls. "It was incredibly hard for me. I just wanted to get out of there."
'She went home, they beat her again and confined her, and she came back to us a second time.' Inside the secret villa
(Photo: Shira Kadri-Ovadia)

Deep down, however, Sarah, whose name has been changed to protect her identity, knew that leaving home was inevitable. She had found the strength to seek help herself after people she knew became aware of the abuse she had suffered at home, which had placed her in serious danger. They were the first to help her recognize that what was happening to her was not normal.
Once she reached out for help, events unfolded rapidly. She was removed from her home without her parents' knowledge and taken to the emergency shelter.

"The moment there's a danger, it has to happen immediately," explains Aviv, director of the shelter, which is operated by the nonprofit organization Yachdav on behalf of Israel's Welfare Ministry. Like the girls in her care, Aviv does not disclose her full name, fearing that she could be followed and the shelter's location exposed.

Sarah remembers barely speaking during her first days at the shelter, afraid that anything she said might be used against her. Today, she recognizes that this was something she had learned in the home where she grew up. Even when members of staff were kind to her, she immediately became suspicious.
"I assumed that if someone did something nice for me, I'd have to give them something in return later," she says, alluding to the patterns she had grown accustomed to.
It took weeks before she realized that the help she was receiving came without conditions and began to trust those around her.
"I felt that she genuinely cared about me," Sarah says of the social worker who eventually broke through her silence. "That she was doing it wholeheartedly."

Sarah is one of dozens of girls and young women who arrive at the villa each year. The facility accommodates individuals from across Israeli society whose lives are endangered by violence, severe neglect or domestic abuse. Others arrive after experiencing violent and dangerous intimate relationships.

Like Sarah, many struggle to adjust during their first few days. "One day they're suddenly uprooted from their lives and brought here," Aviv says. "Usually without a change of clothes, without bags and quite possibly without their phones. Their lives change in an instant."
Aviv understands their distress. "Sometimes they come into my office crying and asking, 'Why is he outside and I'm in here?'" she says.

The person they are referring to could be a father, an uncle or a boyfriend. "This week, a girl asked why she had to pay the price. Why had the person who hurt her been released from custody while she had to stay here?"

What do you tell her? "That it's incredibly frustrating, but sometimes it takes time to establish sufficient grounds for an indictment. And that while it might feel like the end of the world right now, it's better to spend two or three difficult months in a shelter and then be able to live safely."
The shelter operates under strict confidentiality. Its name and the city in which it is located cannot be disclosed, only that it is somewhere in southern Israel.

Girls arriving at the facility are asked to surrender their mobile phones to prevent the location from being tracked. Any telephone conversations with family members take place under staff supervision.

Across Israel, various emergency facilities provide accommodation and assistance to at-risk youth. What distinguishes this shelter is that its location is kept secret even from the girls' families, much like shelters for women experiencing domestic violence.

"When professionals determine that a girl is in danger and needs a protected environment, she'll come here," says Inbar Simon Sharabi, who works in emergency services at the Welfare Ministry. That can happen in the middle of the night, on weekends or during holidays. Staff members are available around the clock to receive new arrivals.
'We have 14-year-old girls who arrive here unable to read or write'
Some girls come directly from hospitals, where they have been treated for injuries inflicted by family members.

"One girl came to us after her mother decided she'd had enough of her not waking up on time in the morning, so she poured hot water over her," recalls Limor Ziv, who founded the shelter and directed it during its early years. She now oversees addiction services at Yachdav.

In some cases, the immediate danger comes not from threats made by relatives but from severely risky behavior, including alcohol and drug use and unhealthy relationships. Staff members work to interrupt these patterns before they escalate further.

"These things don't happen in a vacuum," Ziv says. "A girl doesn't just find herself in situations where she's putting herself at risk. It usually begins with things happening at home, followed by difficulties functioning at school. Night becomes day and day becomes night."
That, she explains, can lead girls into contact with people on the margins of society and criminal elements who exploit their vulnerabilities.

"They pick them up effortlessly, tempting them with things they're missing at home: 'Come on, I'll take care of you. I'll buy you a pair of jeans.' The way to stop that is to separate them from that environment."

Telephone conversations with family members are supervised not only to protect the shelter's location but also to ensure that contact with the outside world does not undermine the therapeutic process.

"Our role during those conversations is to protect the girl and make sure the conversation doesn't go in a direction that could harm her," Aviv says. "For example, we make sure she isn't being pressured to change her account or withdraw a police complaint."
Some conversations, she adds, involve emotional manipulation, with relatives telling girls that they want them to come home but insisting that they first withdraw their complaints.
'I would have stayed longer.' The secret shelter in southern Israel
Ultimately, however, the decision remains with the girls themselves. "This is a closed facility, but it isn't locked," Aviv says.

Unlike secure residential facilities operated by Israel's Youth Protection Authority, where young people are sometimes placed under court orders, the shelter exists to provide protection. Not every girl is willing to accept it.
"We had a girl whose mother would tell her during every phone call, 'We miss you, we want you to come home, we won't hurt you anymore,'" Ziv recalls.
"There were endless promises until she asked to return. She went home, they beat her again and confined her, and she came back to us a second time."
Officially, the shelter accommodates girls and young women ages 14 to 24. In practice, some arrivals are even younger, occasionally just 12 years old.
"They've been through extremely difficult experiences in their lives, and the trauma is evident," Aviv says.

The facility has 18 beds and accommodates approximately 70 girls and young women annually. Roughly half come from Israel's Arab community and half are Jewish. Another shelter elsewhere in the country serves girls from the Arab community exclusively.

In some cases, girls face threats connected to so-called family honor. In others, they experience severe domestic violence disguised as discipline or a parenting philosophy. Ziv still remembers girls who arrived with serious physical injuries resulting from brutal punishments.

The shelter has operated under strict confidentiality for 25 years. Its earliest residents are now adults, but the violence and danger have not disappeared, and new generations of girls continue to arrive.

Having watched generations of girls and young women pass through its doors, Ziv says major events that have transformed Israeli society over the years have also affected its most vulnerable populations.
The consequences of broader social upheavals, she says, tend to become apparent inside the shelter within a year or two.
(Photo: Shira Kadri Ovadia)
Following Israel's 2005 disengagement from Gaza, for example, several girls arrived after their lives had become destabilized and they had found themselves in dangerous circumstances.

During the shelter's early years, some residents came from families that had immigrated to Israel from the former Soviet Union. "Their mothers and fathers weren't at home, leaving them without a parental presence, and they drifted to the margins of society," Ziv says.
Following periods of terrorist attacks, staff encountered girls suffering from post-traumatic stress.

In recent years, against the backdrop of war and continuing instability, Simon Sharabi says the circumstances facing the most vulnerable girls have become increasingly severe, as have the experiences they bring with them to the shelter.

By late morning, pots are already simmering in the villa's kitchen in preparation for lunch. Elsewhere, the girls sit at classroom desks, each working on a different assignment with a teacher employed through HILA, an educational program for young people outside the mainstream school system.
The educational disparities are considerable. "We have 14-year-old girls who arrive here unable to read or write," Aviv says. "Others are capable of sitting their high school matriculation exams."
The daily schedule is packed and the rules are clear: six cigarettes a day for those who smoke, six meals and designated times for showering and studying.
"Everything is carefully regulated and structured to help them establish a routine," Aviv explains. "At the shelter, we want to help them rebuild their everyday habits," Ziv adds.

The rules and structured schedule are designed to support a far more important objective. "They often come from environments where nobody really saw them or took an interest in them," Ziv says. "Here, we're trying to give them a different experience, one in which their strengths are recognized and they feel seen."

It is not an easy process. Many girls arrive emotionally overwhelmed and distressed, experiencing panic attacks and outbursts of anger. But learning that they can express those emotions without being rejected is itself part of their recovery.
"Girls who haven't necessarily experienced love or acceptance can express difficult emotions here and discover that they're still embraced and loved," Aviv says.

The villa has seen countless girls come and go over the years. Their stays are intended to be relatively short, usually lasting a few months. "It's like an emergency room," Aviv explains. "An opportunity to stop, calm down, get away from their surroundings and understand what's happening."

During their stay, residents undergo assessments to determine which type of residential or therapeutic setting would best meet their needs afterward. At the same time, municipal social services departments seek to work with the families they have left behind.
At the end of this period, a decision is made about their future. Some will be able to return home, while many others will move to residential educational or care facilities.

Sometimes, girls remain at the shelter longer than recommended because no suitable placement is available. In other cases, residential facilities are reluctant to accept girls who continue to face threats to their safety. Occasionally, parents refuse to cooperate, delaying the placement process.
Sarah also remained at the shelter for an extended period until a suitable placement was found for her. She watched other girls arrive and leave, but she was in no hurry to follow them.
"I would have stayed longer," she says. "The shelter really felt like home."

articles.title: בלי שחמאס התפרק מנשקו: ישראל בדרך לאשר את התוכנית לעזה
articles.summary: תוכנית הפירוז בעזה צפויה לצאת לדרך עוד לפני פירוק חמאס מנשקו • מפקד חיל הים של איראן שהראם איראני: איראן מתכננת סדרה של פעולות צבאיות לפריצת המצור הימי האמריקאי • עדכונים שוטפים
paragraphs: 16:29 - צה"ל על אירוע התקיפה סמוך לכפר אל מועייר: זהות הפצועים היא שני אזרחים ישראלים ושני פלסטינים. הארבעה נעו ברכבים עם לוחיות זיהוי ישראליות
16:20 - הקואליציה בראשות סעודיה הודיעה שיירטה טיל שנורה מהחות'ים בתימן לעבר עיירה בדרום סעודיה
14:54 - הקואליציה בהובלת סעודיה הודיעה שיירטה שני טילים ששוגרו על ידי החות'ים בתימן לעבר האזור הדרומי במדינה
14:31 - תקרית חמורה בבנימין: רעולי פנים תקפו עובדים של חברת החשמל, אחד מהם נפצע קשה
עובדי חברת החשמל של מזרח ירושלים שהגיעו הבוקר (שבת) לטפל בתקלה באזור הכפר אל-מוע'ייר שבבנימין - הותקפו בידי רעולי פנים. אחד מהעובדים במצב קשה, ושניים נוספים במצב קל. לפי ההערכות, התוקפים הם יהודים.
העובדים הגיעו למקום בעקבות תקלה שנגרמה ככל הנראה בידי פורעים יהודים בימים האחרונים. הם הותקפו בידי כמה רעולי פנים, שנמלטו מהאזור. העובדים מקבלים טיפול רפואי בשטח.

"בעקבות דיווח שהתקבל לפני זמן קצר בחשד לתקיפת עובדי חברת החשמל על ידי רעולי פנים, עת שעבדו בתיקון עמוד חשמל בכפר אל-מוע'ייר שבאזור בנימין ואליו הוזעקו כוחות צה"ל ולוחמי מג"ב איו"ש, נפתחה חקירה במחוז ש"י", נמסר מהמשטרה. לקריאת הכתבה
13:02 - הקואליציה בהובלת סעודיה מדווחת שיירטה טיל בליסטי ששוגר על ידי החות'ים לעבר האזור הדרומי של המדינה
12:09 - דיווח בפייננשל טיימס: צבא ארה"ב סיכל לפני שבועיים חדירה של שישה כטב"מים לבסיס חיל האוויר לייקנהית' במזרח אנגליה, ששוהים בו כוחות אמריקאים

על פי הדיווח, איראן חשודה במעורבות בתקרית, אך טרם נמצאו לכך ראיות חד-משמעיות. הכוחות האמריקאים הפעילו אמצעים נגד כטב"מים והצליחו להדוף אותם אך אף אחד מהכטב"מים לא נתפס, ולכן לא ברור אם נשאו חומרי נפץ או אמצעי מודיעין.
11:18 - כוחות הביטחון סיכלו הלילה כמה הברחות מסיני באמצעות בלונים, שכללו בין היתר 15 רובי קלשניקוב, טלפונים ומעל ל-100 ק"ג של סמים

10:08 - סוכנות הבריטית לפעולות סחר ימי: חמושים פשטו והשתלטו על אוניית משא במרחק של כ-120 ק"מ מיילים ימיים מדרום-מערב לאזור בלחאף שבתימן. הדיווח של הסוכנות מסתמך על דברי רב-החובל של הספינה. בצל האירוע ניתנה הנחיה לכלי שיט אחרים באזור לנקוט משנה זהירות
08:47 - מפקד חיל הים של איראן שהראם איראני: איראן מתכננת סדרה של פעולות צבאיות לפריצת המצור הימי האמריקאי
08:43 - בלי שחמאס התפרק מנשקו: ישראל בדרך לאשר את התוכנית לעזה

ישראל צפויה לאשר בימים הקרובים התקדמות משמעותית ביישום תוכניתו של נשיא ארצות הברית דונלד טראמפ לרצועת עזה - עוד לפני שחמאס התפרק מנשקו. מחר (א') צפוי הקבינט להתכנס ולדון בעדכון הצעת ההחלטה הנוגעת לסיכומים עם מועצת השלום, וביום שני צפוי מנכ"ל המועצה, ניקולאי מלדנוב, לצאת בהצהרה לתקשורת על ההתקדמות בתוכנית. לקריאת הכתבה

04:11 - פיקוד המרכז של צבא ארה"ב, סנטקום, פרסם הודעת בדיקת עובדות שבה הפריך שלוש טענות של מפקד צבאי איראני: השתלטות אמריקאית על שתי מכליות נפט איראניות, פגיעה איראנית בנושאת המטוסים "אברהם לינקולן" במהלך מבצע "Epic Fury", וגביית 2.5 מיליון דולר מכלי שיט העוברים במצר הורמוז. בסנטקום הבהירו כי נושאת המטוסים לא נפגעה, לא נגבית אגרת מעבר במצר וכי שלוש הטענות שקריות
03:07 - ארגון רופאים ללא גבולות (MSF) פרסם הודעה בעקבות חיסול שני מחבלי חמאס, שלפי צה"ל עבדו במקביל כמאבטחים במרפאה של הארגון בעיר עזה
"אנחנו המומים וזועמים בעקבות הריגתם של שניים מעמיתינו, ששימשו כשומרים, בתקיפה ישראלית על אחת המרפאות שלנו בעזה. מדובר בפגיעה ישירה ב-MSF, שמעלה ל-17 את מספר עמיתינו שנהרגו ברצועת עזה", נכתב בהודעה.
עוד נכתב בהודעת הארגון כי "המתחם שלנו סומן בבירור בלוגואים של הארגון, ומיקומו הועבר לצה"ל והיה ידוע לו". בצה"ל הדגישו מנגד כי התקיפה לא כוונה לבית חולים ולא נגרם נזק לתשתיות רפואיות במרחב.
02:21 - שר ההגנה הסעודי ח'אלד בן סלמאן עמד בראש משלחת הממלכה שהשתתפה בישיבה השנייה של הוועדה האסטרטגית לעניינים מדיניים וביטחוניים של ברית ההגנה של מכה, שנערכה באיסלאמאבאד, בירת פקיסטן

במהלך הישיבה נדונו דרכים לחיזוק שיתוף הפעולה בין מדינות ברית ההגנה של מכה, באופן שיתרום לקידום האפיקים המדיניים והביטחוניים של הברית ולהשגת ביטחון ויציבות. כמו כן, נסקרו כמה נושאים וסוגיות בעלי עניין משותף, ואושרו החלטות והמלצות שהופיעו בסדר היום.
01:09 - צה"ל חיסל אמש את המחבל אחמד ספיאן מוחמד עלי אבו חצירה ואת המחבל מעאד יוסף עליצבח, מפקד חוליית ארטילריה בזרוע הצבאית של ארגון הטרור חמאס

השניים עבדו במקביל כמאבטחים במרפאה של ארגון רופאים ללא גבולות (MSF) - דוגמה נוספת להיטמעות של חמאס בארגונים בין-לאומיים. בצה"ל מדגישים כי בניגוד לנטען, התקיפה לא בוצעה לעבר בית חולים ולא נגרם נזק לתשתיות רפואיות במרחב. "לאורך המלחמה ובעת האחרונה בפרט, המחבלים קידמו מתווי טרור נגד כוחות צה"ל ואזרחי מדינת ישראל ופעלו לשיקום יכולות ארגוני הטרור ברצועה, תוך הפרה שיטתית של הפסקת האש", הדגישו בדובר צה"ל.

לתשומת לבכם: מערכת גלובס חותרת לשיח מגוון, ענייני ומכבד בהתאם ל קוד האתי המופיע בדו"ח האמון לפיו אנו פועלים. ביטויי אלימות, גזענות, הסתה או כל שיח בלתי הולם אחר מסוננים בצורה אוטומטית ולא יפורסמו באתר.

articles.title: זוהרן ממדאני הזהיר מהגירעון - ואז העניק לעובדיו העלאות שכר בכמעט מיליון דולר
articles.summary: לפי ה"ניו יורק פוסט", ראש עיריית ניו יורק העניק מאז תחילת השנה לעובדי לשכתו העלאות שכר בסכום מצטבר של 850 אלף דולר, בצל גירעון תקציבי של 5.4 מיליארד דולר וביקורת על התנהלותו
paragraphs: לפי ה"ניו יורק פוסט", ראש עיריית ניו יורק העניק מאז תחילת השנה לעובדי לשכתו העלאות שכר בסכום מצטבר של 850 אלף דולר, בצל גירעון תקציבי של 5.4 מיליארד דולר וביקורת על התנהלותו
ברקע הביקורת, הודיעה החודש העירייה כי תוכנית ההוצאות תפחה ביותר מ-3 מיליארד דולר ל-129.2 מיליארד דולר, וכללה קיצוצים של 429 מיליון דולר בלבד.

articles.title: High-security prisoner used soap to escape despite being handcuffed and chained to officer
articles.summary: Exclusive: Inmate from HMP Manchester now back in custody after 13 hours on the run A prisoner from one of England and Wales’s most dysfunctional high-security jails is believed to have used soap to help escape from officers while visiting a hospital for treatment. The 36-year-old detained at HMP Manchester managed to slip away despite being cuffed and chained to an officer, sources told the Guardian. He is believed to have lathered his metal cuff with liquid soap and slipped his hand out while being given privacy to use a bathroom. Continue reading...
paragraphs: A prisoner from one of England and Wales’s most dysfunctional high-security jails is believed to have used soap to help escape from officers while visiting a hospital for treatment.

The 36-year-old detained at HMP Manchester managed to slip away despite being cuffed and chained to an officer, sources told the Guardian. He is believed to have lathered his metal cuff with liquid soap and slipped his hand out while being given privacy to use a bathroom.
After 13 hours of freedom and a short pursuit on foot, the offender was detained and arrested by Greater Manchester police officers.

The incident has sparked a formal inquiry by the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) and comes amid an increase in escapes from jails in England and Wales. This is the second time this year that a prisoner has escaped after attending a Manchester hospital.

Marwan Jumaa, a 20-year-old Sudanese national deemed to be a risk to himself and others, was serving an indefinite secure hospital sentence for attacking two women. He escaped after being transferred from his secure hospital facility to North Manchester hospital for medical treatment in July.
Mark Fairhurst, the national chair of the prison officers’ union, the POA, demanded that more officers should escort offenders from category A and B prisons to hospitals.

“This incident highlights the risks that officers face when escorting prisoners to and from hospitals. There should be a minimum of three officers on every hospital appointment instead of two under current rules,” he said.

The number of prisoners escaping from custody has steadily increased over the past three years. In 2025-26, 14 people escaped from custody across England and Wales, compared with 12 the year before, and nine in 2023-24.
HMP Manchester, once known as Strangeways and which houses category A and B prisoners, has been said to have some of the worst conditions across the England and Wales estate.
The category B prisoner escaped on the evening of 20 November after two prison officers accompanied him to a local hospital.
According to prison escort regulations, category B prisoners must wear “double handcuffs” – where both wrists are restrained close to each other and a prisoner is cuffed to a member of staff.

Subject to risk assessment, the double cuff can be adjusted to a single cuff and a ratchet chain when privacy and hand movements are required, such as when using the toilet or shower. This allows the prison officers to give an offender privacy in a room or cubicle while still being attached to an officer with a chain, which can be more than a metre long.

Sources said that the prisoner had been placed in a single cuff and chain but had escaped from his cuff while using a bathroom. Police were alerted at 8.30pm and searched for the man overnight. He was located at 9.30am on Saturday, and was detained and arrested after attempting to flee on foot.
The internal MoJ investigation will focus on whether safety procedures were carried out at all times and if the man was handcuffed properly.
A spokesperson for Greater Manchester police said: “We received a call shortly before 8.30pm on Friday 20 November that a 36-year-old man had absconded from lawful custody whilst at hospital.

“Officers deployed and utilising specialist resources conducted a full search over the course of the evening and into the morning. The man was safely detained at around 9.30am on Saturday 21 November following a short foot chase and further arrested on suspicion of escaping lawful custody. He has been transported back to custody.”

Prison sources said the escape of a prisoner held in a high-security prison was still relatively rare. In September 2023, Daniel Khalife, 23, sparked a high-profile search when he broke out of HMP Wandsworth by clinging to the underside of a food delivery truck. At the time he was being held on remand for spying charges.
Last year, an escaped prisoner tried to flee armed police by ramming them with his getaway car. Jay Bennett, 33, was serving a nine-year sentence when he absconded from HMP Sudbury in Derbyshire.

An official report into HMP Manchester conducted earlier this year by the prisons watchdog found large quantities of drugs flown in by drones, an obvious rat infestation and violence against prisoners and staff.

The report by Charlie Taylor, HM chief inspector of prisons, said the jail was “in a precarious state”. In 2024, he invoked an urgent notification, which automatically triggers ministers to intervene in the jail’s management.

A Prison Service spokesperson said: “This individual is now back in custody. We have launched an investigation into this incident and any prisoner who is unlawfully at large faces extra time in prison.”

articles.title: ‘I didn’t know who to help first’: Airstrike on Myanmar wedding kills at least 20
articles.summary: Witnesses tell AFP that Myanmar's military struck a house hosting a wedding in the country's east, killing at least 20 people and wounding dozens; most of the victims were women and children, with several people still missing
paragraphs: Witnesses tell AFP that Myanmar's military struck a house hosting a wedding in the country's east, killing at least 20 people and wounding dozens; most of the victims were women and children, with several people still missing
At least 20 people were killed in a Myanmar military airstrike on a house hosting a wedding in the country's east, witnesses told AFP on Saturday.

The strike hit a village near Moe Bye, a town on the border between Shan and Kayah states. Images from the scene obtained by AFP, which had not been independently verified, showed at least six people killed in the attack.
The aftermath of a deadly airstrike in Myanmar
A representative of Nway Oo Yaung Chi, an organization assisting displaced people in Myanmar, said 21 people, including five children, were killed and more than 40 were wounded.
The organization's chief said rescue workers struggled to transport the wounded to hospitals because of the large number of casualties and a shortage of vehicles.

Myanmar has been engulfed in civil war since a military coup in 2021 ousted the government of Nobel Peace Prize laureate Aung San Suu Kyi. More than 100,000 people have since been killed on both sides of the conflict, according to human rights organizations.
The military controls Moe Bye, while opposition forces operate in surrounding villages. The area has seen intense fighting.
A witness to the strike described the devastation and chaos at the scene as survivors struggled to rescue the wounded.
"I was in shock. I didn't know who to help first. An injured woman told me to get the children out first," he said.
"Several people are still missing, including my niece. I couldn't find her."
The witness said most of the victims were women and children. He also provided AFP with footage showing a man fleeing the scene carrying a baby and a young girl searching for her parents.

articles.title: "הגיעו לפתע והכו באלות" | תיעוד: פורעים יהודים תקפו עובדי חשמל, 4 נפצעו
articles.summary: פורעים תקפו את העובדים, תושבי מזרח י-ם, בעת שתיקנו עמוד חשמל. צה"ל עודכן על קיום העבודות, אך לא נערך בשטח "כי מדובר בעובדים ישראלים". כוח מג"ב היה רק בסמוך - ולא דווח על עצורים: "הכוחות קפצו מיד, החשודים ברחו". אחמד המהנדס נותר בהלם: "הם ניקבו צמיגים ושברו שמשות. התשתית משרתת את כולם"
paragraphs: רעולי פנים יהודים תקפו הבוקר (יום שבת) פועלים ערבים-ישראלים ופלסטינים במהלך עבודות לתיקון עמוד חשמל בכפר אל-מועייר שבאזור בנימין, בשטח C, וארבעה עובדים נפצעו. שניים מהעובדים שהותקפו, גם באמצעות אלות, הם תושבי מזרח ירושלים, והשניים האחרים פלסטינים; אחד מהם פונה לבית החולים עם חבלות בראש ובידיים, והיתר נפצעו באורח קל וטופלו בבית חולים ברמאללה.

בתיעוד מהמקום נראה אחד העובדים מצלם את הפורעים מתנפלים - ככל הנראה על עובד אחר - כשהוא מסתתר מאחורי רכב. לאחר מכן התוקפים מבחינים בו, ואחד מהם רץ אליו כשהוא אוחז במוט; העובד צעק "למה? מה עשינו?" - והוטח אל הקרקע. הפורעים גם ניפצו שמשת משאית ששימשה לעבודות. אחמד, מהנדס שהוגדר כ"איש הקשר" בשטח, שעובד גם כן בחברה ששלחה את הפועלים, שחזר: "העובדים טיפלו בתקלה בקו מתח גבוה, כשלפתע הגיעו מתיישבים, תקפו אותם באלות, שברו את שמשות כלי הרכב וניקבו את הצמיגים".
פורעים יהודים רעולי פנים תקפו עובדי חברת החשמל

לטענתו, אחד העובדים נפצע באורח קשה. "מדובר בתשתית חשמל שמשרתת את כלל התושבים באזור, לא רק את הכפרים הפלסטיניים", אמר אחמד, "היא מספקת חשמל גם לתאורת הכבישים, למצלמות ולתשתיות נוספות באזור. בסופו של דבר הם מגיעים ופוגעים בקווי חשמל שמשרתים את כולם. לפני כמה ימים, באותו מקום, פגעו בתשתית וגרמו להפסקת חשמל בכפר שלם. בעקבות התקיפה שלחנו צוות נוסף לטפל בתקלה. כל כלי הרכב נפגעו ונלקחו לתיקון".

צה"ל ידע על קיום העבודות, אך לא נערך בשטח כדי לאבטחן. רק כשעתיים אחרי התקיפה, דובר צה"ל מסר תגובה ראשונה שלפיה "בהתאם להערכת מצב וניתוח החיכוך הפוטנציאלי, מספר צוותי מג"ב היו פרוסים במרחב השטח, למניעה וסיכול אירועי פשיעה, אלימות וטרור, אך לא היה כוח צמוד לנקודת האלימות שזיהה את האירוע. הכוחות קפצו מיד בקבלת הדיווח, אך החשודים ברחו לפני הגעת הכוחות. מדובר בעבודה שתואמה רק מול חלק מהגורמים הרלוונטיים. מאחר ומדובר בעבודה של ישראלים, לא הועלתה דרישה לאבטחה צמודה והייתה אבטחה מרחבית. האירוע מתוחקר בצה"ל.

"מפקד פיקוד המרכז ביצע הערכת מצב משותפת עם מחוז ש"י, מפקד אוגדת איו"ש, ראש המנהל האזרחי, מפקד מג"ב איו"ש ונציגי שב"כ, בה סוכם על פעולה מהירה ונחושה בשיתוף כל כוחות הביטחון לאיתור החשודים ומעצרם. צה"ל מגנה בתוקף את האירוע ורואה בחומרה כל גילוי אלימות. מדובר בתקיפה מכוונת ואלימות חסרת הבחנה, כלפי חפים מפשע. מעשים אלו פוגעים פגיעה קשה במדינת ישראל ובדמותו של צה"ל, בארץ ובעולם, עומדים בניגוד מוחלט לערכי צה״ל ומסבים נזק כבד למאמצי הביטחון והלגיטימציה".

לאחר מכן פרסם צה"ל הודעה נוספת שבה ביקש "לחדד" את הדברים. בהודעה זו נטען כי "רק לאחר הפצת ההודעה, בניגוד לדיווח הראשוני, התקבל עדכון בפיקוד המרכז ובמנהל האזרחי כי זהות הפצועים היא שני אזרחים ישראלים ושני פלסטינים. הארבעה נעו ברכבים עם לוחיות זיהוי ישראליות. כפי שנאמר, האירוע מתוחקר".

המשטרה מסרה כי נפתחה חקירה במחוז ש"י, וכי בעקבות הדיווח על התקיפה הוזעקו למקום כוחות צה"ל ולוחמי מג"ב איו"ש. "כוחות משטרה וחוקרי מערך הזיהוי הפלילי של מחוז ש"י נכנסו לזירה באבטחת כוח צה״ל והחלו באיסוף ממצאים, ראיות וכן גביית עדויות", נמסר מהמשטרה. "חקירת המקרה נמשכת".
בחברת החשמל הבהירו כי "עובדי חברת חשמל לישראל לא פעלו הבוקר באזור בנימין ולא נפגעו באירוע האלימות המדווח".
התקיפה מצטרפת לאירוע אלימות נוסף שהתרחש בלילה בכפר קראוות בני חסאן, שבמהלכו פורעים נכנסו ליישוב והציתו רכב.

articles.title: Costa Rica bars UN rapporteur on Palestinian territories from entering the country
articles.summary: Francesca Albanese, leading critic of Israeli abuses in Gaza and West Bank, barred on ‘national security grounds’ Costa Rica barred entry to the UN special rapporteur on the Israel-occupied Palestinian territories, Francesca Albanese, earning the ire of the UN human rights chief. Albanese, an Italian national, went to Costa Rica to receive an honorary doctorate from the University of Costa Rica. She was stopped at the airport in San José and not allowed to enter the country, and was transferred to a hotel before she travelled to Mexico on Saturday. Continue reading...
paragraphs: Costa Rica barred entry to the UN special rapporteur on the Israel-occupied Palestinian territories, Francesca Albanese, earning the ire of the UN human rights chief.

Albanese, an Italian national, went to Costa Rica to receive an honorary doctorate from the University of Costa Rica. She was stopped at the airport in San José and not allowed to enter the country, and was transferred to a hotel before she travelled to Mexico on Saturday.

The UN human rights office said that Albanese was stopped from entering the country on “national security grounds”. Costa Rica’s migration office said that its decision was made after she was subject of an “alert” over alleged ties to terrorism.

The UN high commissioner for human rights, Volker Türk, said that he was “deeply concerned” by the decision to deny Albanese entry. “This is difficult to reconcile with Costa Rica’s longstanding commitment to human rights,” said Türk.

Albanese shared a picture on X of an airport bench and her suitcase, where she was meant to stay the night. “Second night in the airport. Guarded by security at every step. Uncomfortable chairs. Noise. Bright light,” Albanese posted.

Albanese, who acts as an independent expert appointed by the UN human rights council, has been outspoken on Israeli abuses in Gaza and the West Bank. She has drawn ire from Israel and its allies for being one of the first, most prominent officials to accuse Israel of committing genocide in Gaza – a claim Israel denies.

The US placed sanctions and revoked the visa of Albanese for her work on Palestine in the summer of 2025, cutting her off from the global financial system. The sanctions make daily life a struggle for Albanese, who has no access to western banks or credit cards.

Albanese called for an investigation into whether her denial of entry into Costa Rica was connected to the US sanctions, in remarks she made remotely at the ceremony for the acceptance of her honorary doctorate.

Costa Rica’s government, headed by the rightwing president, Laura Fernández, is close to the Trump administration and has cooperated with it on security and immigration issues. The government has also intensified its ties with Israel.
Israel’s envoy to the UN, Danny Danon, praised Costa Rica for its decision, accusing Albanese of using her UN position to spread propaganda against Israel.
On Saturday, Albanese was expected leave Costa Rica for Mexico, with the Italian embassy in Mexico working in advance of her visit to ensure there are no obstacles to her entry into the country.

articles.title: Afghanistan explosion kills 10 students and injures more than 100, official says
articles.summary: A spokesman for Afghanistan's interior ministry says the blast was caused by carelessness at an explosives depot nearby.
paragraphs: At least 10 students have been killed and 110 others have been injured following an explosion near a school in Afghanistan, a spokesperson has told the BBC.
The incident happened on Saturday morning in the Anderseir area of Asadabad, the capital of Kunar province, the spokesperson for the Taliban government's interior ministry said.
Posting on X, Abdul Mateen Qani said that according to initial investigations, the blast was caused by "negligence and carelessness" at an explosives depot belonging to nearby mining companies.
An investigation into the incident was ongoing, he added.

The province's culture and information director Sami ul Haq Bayan said the blast took place in a house near Shagai Middle School in Asadabad as explosives were being prepared for mining and blasting rock, reports AFP.
The Associated Press also cites the official saying up to 15 wounded people remain in hospital, while the rest have been discharged after treatment.

articles.title: US Army detonation of 4,500 kg. lead-azide in Iowa had near-zero environmental impact, EPA claims
articles.summary: According to initial lab results from 88% of post-detonation samples taken by the EPA, measurable concentrations of lead in soil, water and drinking supplies were no higher after the blast.
paragraphs: Lab results from the first soil and water samples collected after the US Army detonation of an aging stockpile of lead-based explosives in Iowa found negligible levels of contamination attributed to the blast in surrounding areas, the US government reported on Saturday.
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) posted its readings online three days after the Army blew up nearly 5 tons (4,500 kg.) of highly volatile lead azide stored in 68 degrading plastic drums.

The orchestrated demolition was carried out in two simultaneous explosions at an Army munitions depot in the tiny farming town of Middletown, Iowa, about 150 miles southwest of Des Moines, the state capital.

According to initial lab results from 88% of post-detonation samples taken by the EPA, measurable concentrations of lead in soil, water and drinking supplies were no higher after the blast than levels found in samples taken beforehand.

In a statement posted on X/Twitter on Saturday, the EPA said the first lab results indicated the Army's "controlled detonation ... did not result in an elevation of lead in the water bodies that act as drinking water sources" and that there were "no detection of lead in drinking water sources taken after the detonation."

The EPA said its teams had collected more than 1,600 air, water, soil and dust samples after the detonation, roughly the same number taken before the blast, and that 187 homes and other structures were assessed, including schools, playgrounds, churches and daycare centers.
Zero levels of airborne lead present in 30 hours post detonation

Residents living closest to the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant were evacuated in advance of Wednesday's detonation as a precaution, while others sheltered in place inside their homes to avoid exposure to any lead dust emitted from the blast.

Immediately following the detonation, the Army and EPA said emission monitors had detected zero levels of airborne lead in the surrounding region, and an all-clear notice later in the day advised residents they were free to resume normal activities.
The EPA said on Saturday that its air monitoring operations recorded "0.0 µg/m3 readings" of airborne lead for 30 consecutive hours after the controlled detonation.

Army officials attributed the favorable air testing to an array of containment measures designed to muffle the blast and prevent toxic dust from being spewed over homes, crops and livestock beyond the detonation site.

Independent experts welcomed Wednesday's initial air quality readings but said atmospheric sampling was of limited value and that the real measure of lead fallout would come from sampling of water, soil, and structural surfaces, the analysis of which would take longer.
Lead exposure can cause a range of health problems, particularly in children, in whom it can interfere with cognitive development. Once it settles in the environment, it does not break down.
Detonation followed days of public rancor

The "controlled, mitigated detonation" was conducted after days of public rancor and legal wrangling over the disposal plan, which US officials said was far safer than waiting for the chemicals to eventually blow up on their own.

The Army said that by the time an inspection of the stockpiled barrels in March found them to be on the verge of spontaneous explosion, it was too late to safely move the containers or to chemically neutralize them.
Critics, however, suggested that the situation reached crisis proportions because of inept management of the stockpile and poor planning.

Environmental groups filed suit challenging an emergency permit the EPA granted the Army to carry out the detonation, and US President Donald Trump intervened on Monday to order the Army to hold off on the operation until the courts approved it.

Later that same day, the 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the EPA's permit and lifted an earlier injunction it had imposed on the demolition, clearing the way for the Army to proceed two days later.
Following the blast, residents of the area expressed a mix of relief that toxic exposure appeared to have been minimized, and skepticism about the government's level of transparency.
Army projections before the blast had shown that lead dust could settle on surfaces as far as 40 miles southwest of the detonation site, extending through southeastern Iowa into northern Missouri.
US and Iowa agriculture officials also estimated that 350 farms might be affected by lead fallout based on weather forecasts.

The Environment and Climate Change portal is produced in cooperation with the Goldman Sonnenfeldt School of Sustainability and Climate Change at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev. The Jerusalem Post maintains all editorial decisions related to the content.

articles.title: US regulators eye kratom as overdose deaths mount
articles.summary: Kratom advocates say a ‘critical distinction’ should be made between natural and chemically enhanced versions of drug The US government is paying more attention to kratom after the apparent overdose deaths of young people, but advocates say the synthetic drug hurting people is not the same as the supplement and users should be aware of the difference. But chemical dependency specialists and law enforcement figures warn that the distinction may not be enough to curb an increasing number of fatalities and treatment center admissions for synthetic and semisynthetic kratom derivatives rather…
paragraphs: The US government is paying more attention to kratom after the apparent overdose deaths of young people, but advocates say the synthetic drug hurting people is not the same as the supplement and users should be aware of the difference.

But chemical dependency specialists and law enforcement figures warn that the distinction may not be enough to curb an increasing number of fatalities and treatment center admissions for synthetic and semisynthetic kratom derivatives rather than natural kratom leaf.

Signs of a growing issue around kratom and kratom enhanced with the 7-OH alkaloid are beginning to emerge. Three weeks ago, the US telehealth provider Quick MD released a study showing that the substances now account for more than half of its new addiction treatment patients, a five-time increase from 10% in 2024 to 50%.
“In September, 55% of our new addiction treatment patients sought help for kratom or 7⁠-⁠OH dependence,” said Ryan Lissack, chief executive officer of QuickMD. The company is now advertising on TV.

The US Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) recently issued two notices recommending that 7-OH, or 7-hydroxymitragynine – one of the major psychoactive ingredients in kratom – should be placed under federal controls while legislation has been introduced to effect stronger controls.

The notice came less than a month after Ole Miss college students Aidan Hamilton, 18, and Robert Strang, 20, were found dead in separate incidents with packages of concentrated kratom-related products discovered at both scenes. Federal prosecutors have said the two students “died of conditions consistent to overdoses”, though toxicology results are still pending.

Promoted as a wellness product that’s often sold in corner stores and gas stations, kratom is a mild opioid derived from the leaves of Mitragyna speciosa (a tropical evergreen tree native to south-east Asia). It’s sold in various forms, including powders, teas, capsules, tablets, extracts, gummies, and raw or crushed leaves.
Enhanced kratom is the latest drug to register as a concern for health authorities and law enforcement.

“Any opioid, synthetic or semi-synthetic, has the potential to be addictive,” says Patrick Trainor, director of the narcotics investigation and drug control unit at the Pennsylvania attorney general’s office. “Any opioid that’s being sold as a wellness drug is of concern.”

A 2023 Tampa Bay Times investigation found that more than 580 people in Florida have died from kratom-related overdoses during the past decade. The paper notes that most of the deaths were caused “by a fatal mixture of kratom and at least one other substance, but 46 people overdosed solely on the herb”.

The National Poison Data System found that between 2015 and 2025 kratom exposure reports surged 1,200%. Estimates of how many people use kratom and 7-OH products in the US vary. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention estimates there around 5 million “lifetime” users. The American Kratom Association puts the number at 11 million to 16 million, with retail sales estimated at $2.2bn in 2024.

Trainor, a former DEA agent who worked on drug interdiction in Philadelphia’s notorious Kensington area, notes a primary concern with kratom is that “it’s being sold from retail locations, there’s a lot of misbranding, or misrepresentation, to what the potency is. People might think they’re taking a legal dose but that may not be the case.”

While kratom is not approved for use in a medical environment, it’s often used to moderate opioid withdrawal symptoms. A development with this use is that the increasing strength of the kratom products containing 7-OH means it can create new chemical dependency issues while trying to solve existing ones.
“For people who are dealing with substance abuse disorder, kratom has potential to get people sick,” Trainor says, using a street term for drug withdrawal symptoms.

This is happening as some harm reduction medications – including the opioid dependency management drug Suboxone – are becoming harder to obtain because of strict distributor caps and dispensary policies.

A study by UC Berkeley found that despite the relaxation of prescribing guidelines, harm reduction drugs such as buprenorphine, one of the ingredients in Suboxone, is only carried by four in 10 US retail pharmacies, and that access is more limited in Black and Latino communities.
The Trump administration has voiced support and showed effort to limit the chemical compounds found in enhanced kratom.
“These are potent opioids being manufactured and sold in consumer products, often under labels that obscure their true risks,” the US attorney general, Todd Blanche, said in August.

The US Food and Drug Administration has said it has observed “a proliferation of products containing 7-OH, and has “serious concerns” about products containing the alkaloid, calling it an “emerging public health threat”. Last December, the agency said that the US Marshals Service seized 73,000 units of 7-OH products – valued at roughly $1m – from three firms in Missouri.

The American Kratom Association has called for a “critical distinction” to be made between natural leaf kratom and chemically enhanced opioid products and welcomed efforts by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the Department of Justice to distinguish between them.

“The DEA and the Department of Justice deserve recognition for addressing the critical distinction between dangerous, chemically manipulated opioid products and natural kratom leaf,” said Mac Haddow, senior fellow on public policy for the association, in a statement last month.
The distinction, Haddow added, “is essential to protecting consumers without imposing an unjustified ban on lawful botanical products”.

The Manhattan addiction specialist Dr Andrew Tatarsky said the concerns around kratom maybe misplaced. “We demonize the drug because we don’t want to deal with all the other complexities over why people may be vulnerable to overuse,” he said.

Tatarsky said he and his colleagues in the field were not seeing “significant or rampant problems” with kratom. “But 7-OH is a potentially problematic substance that people should be cautioned and educated about.”

Kratom/7-OH dependency issues have begun showing up in rehabilitation centers. Dr Mohammad Sarhan, medical director of the Caron treatment center at its Florida campus, said the practice treats kratom and 7-OH as different substances.

“Kratom offers a mild opioid stimulant effect whereas 7-OH is a highly potent opioid. Patients using kratom we consider ‘other substance use disorder’, but people who say they’re using 7-OH we consider and treat it as a standard opioid use disorder.”

Kate Appleman, chief clinical officer at Caron’s Pennsylvania campus, said she equated the kratom and 7-OH distinction to the way cannabis had evolved from a drug with a small percentage of THC, its active psychoactive ingredient, to one that might contain up to 90%.

“Cannabis is something natural in nature, but when you start to change the components of it, it’s very different,” she said. “Kratom is very similar. People think it’s natural, it’s legal, but when you start to look at the way it gets manufactured, that’s the part that makes it even more problematic.”

From an addiction standpoint, Appleman pointed out, the brain doesn’t know the difference between fentanyl, heroin and OxyContin, and kratom because it affects the same receptors in the brain. Caron has started stand-alone relapse programs for people who have had recovery from heroin or alcohol but relapsed on kratom.

“We hear stories from patients that kratom is more potent than they had anticipated and they have the same symptoms of addiction as they do for heroin and alcohol. Their life is unmanageable, they have withdrawal symptoms and cravings – everything that is standard with having a substance use disorder.”

Sarhan noted that patients being admitted often express a sense of betrayal and embarrassment at becoming dependent on a product that is sold next to energy drinks. “They say, ‘How dangerous could it possibly be? The packaging said it was botanical, plant-based, all-natural – nothing on the label said it was an opioid.’”

Signs that a new era of opioid dependency is approaching are hard to miss. Los Angeles county officials have linked six fatal overdoses to 7-OH, while the San Francisco department of public health reported the city’s first-known adult fatal overdose involving a semisynthetic kratom-derived opioid in September.

The California department of public health issued warnings stating that 7-OH and kratom-derived products are illegal to manufacture or sell for consumption in the state. Eleven states have made it illegal, while Massachusetts and North Dakota have issued temporary bans.

According Sarhan, it’s a “maybe” on whether Kratom could be considered an epidemic, a characterization typically identified and declared by public health agencies. Since it was not scheduled as an illicit substance, Sarhan said, there were regulatory issues. “If it comes off the shelves, does it become an illicit substance? Are people going to switch to an illicit substance or seek treatment? I don’t know. But whatever it is, we’re still early on.”

articles.title: Sakana AI’s CEO says its homegrown models are about more than Japan’s national security
articles.summary: Sakana AI aims to strengthen Japan’s industrial competitiveness with homegrown AI models.
paragraphs: Sakana AI, a Japanese AI startup, last month revealed plans to develop its own foundation model. The move has drawn attention for its potential impact on Japan’s defense and cybersecurity sectors as well as concerns about reliance on U.S. and Chinese technologies.

Sakana AI’s co-founder and CEO, David Ha, told TechCrunch that its upcoming foundation model, Sawara, is part of the company’s broader goal of supporting and strengthening Japan’s industrial and manufacturing sectors using AI. In addition, Ha noted rising cybersecurity threats and stressed the need for domestic AI alternatives for sensitive applications, particularly if access to foreign models becomes limited.

“When we started planning for this model, of course, we had physical AI, manufacturing, and industry in mind, and we still do. This is our long-term vision,” Ha said. “But short-term, I think Japan has a real need for security-related capabilities as well.”
Sakana will begin working on Sawara this month, aiming to train and release a smaller-scale model in early 2027, followed by a larger version.

The project comes roughly five months after Sakana launched Fugu, an AI orchestration system that ropes in other large language models, including those developed by U.S. AI labs, to assemble AI agents according to the task at hand. The Tokyo-based startup has also built Namazu, a Japanese-focused language model that fine-tunes existing open-weight models from Meta and DeepSeek to better understand Japanese language, culture, and business needs, including translation, political questions, and AI agent tasks.

“We cannot simply use open-weight models as-is in Japan for enterprises because they’re usually biased towards their creators,” Ha said. “They may refuse to answer questions about Japan or Japanese politics […] they may give Japanese people answers they don’t want to hear.”
However, Ha acknowledged that developing a domestic foundation model alone will not fully eliminate reliance on foreign AI technology.

“The only thing [left] for us to become a full-stack company is the pre-training, Sawara,” Ha continued. “We plan to apply the [Sawara] technology in industry and manufacturing. We’ll train both a small and a large model next year. The small model should be particularly useful for on-premises solutions. Japan needs on-premises deployment capabilities.”

While Fugu incorporates OpenAI’s models, Ha noted that foreign AI models are not enough for certain applications. For example, in cybersecurity, Japan requires that customized models be deployed on-premises.

“Japan will continue to use U.S. systems, but it also wants domestic alternatives,” Ha said. “People often point to Palantir and other systems. I have a great deal of respect for companies such as Snowflake, Palantir, and Datadog. But for national defense, Japan will want its own systems.”

Sakana signed a research contract with Japan’s Ministry of Defense in July to explore how AI could help analyze and integrate information from multiple sources, and it has also worked with the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, on systems for detecting disinformation.

Sakana’s work with Japanese government agencies has shaped its approach to developing Sawara, Ha said. Unlike commercial customers, government agencies often have stricter requirements, including the ability to audit training data, customize AI models and deploy them on-premises.
“Those lessons helped us plan how to develop and deploy Sawara. I think similar requirements exist in many governments,” he said.

While enterprise customers can use a combination of Fugu, Namazu and AI models developed overseas, Sakana’s government-related work currently focuses on two main areas: disinformation detection and analysis, and multimodal systems that integrate data from different government sources.
Sakana’s expansion into developing its own foundation models comes amid speculation about a potential IPO following reports by Nikkei and Bloomberg earlier this month.
But Ha said the company doesn’t have any near-term plans to go public.

The reported timing and potential valuation were speculative, Ha said, adding that he did not know when the company might pursue a listing, though he expects his startup to eventually go public in Japan itself.
“We have a gravitational pull to eventually IPO in Japan,” Ha said.

Ha sees Sakana’s future growth tied to the global expansion of Japanese manufacturers. Rather than focusing on selling its models, the company wants to help local companies use AI to become more competitive globally.

“We want to strategically work with the government and Japanese industrial base, make them competitive,” Ha said. “We want to go abroad, go international together with manufacturing and industrial sectors.”

articles.summary: עדים סיפרו לסוכנות הידיעות AFP כי צבא מיאנמר תקף בית שבו התקיימה חתונה במזרח המדינה, הרג לפחות 20 איש ופצע עשרות. אחד העדים סיפר: "פצועה אחת אמרה לי לחלץ את הילדים קודם. רוב הנפגעים הם נשים וילדים. כמה עדיין נעדרים, כולל האחיינית שלי"
paragraphs: עדים סיפרו לסוכנות הידיעות AFP כי צבא מיאנמר תקף בית שבו התקיימה חתונה במזרח המדינה, הרג לפחות 20 איש ופצע עשרות. אחד העדים סיפר: "פצועה אחת אמרה לי לחלץ את הילדים קודם. רוב הנפגעים הם נשים וילדים. כמה עדיין נעדרים, כולל האחיינית שלי"
לפחות 20 בני אדם נהרגו היום (שבת) בתקיפה אווירית של צבא מיאנמר - שכוונה לעבר בית שבו התקיימה חתונה, במזרח המדינה. כך סיפרו עדים לסוכנות הידיעות AFP.

בסוכנות הידיעות דווח כי בתמונות מהזירה, שטרם אומתו, נראו לפחות שישה הרוגים בתקיפה, שהתרחשה בכפר ליד מואה בייה, עיר שממוקמת בין מדינות המחוז שאן וקאיה. נציג של עמותת "Nway Oo Yaung Chi", המסייעת לעקורים במדינה, הצהיר כי 21 בני אדם נהרגו, בהם חמישה ילדים, ויותר מ-40 נפצעו.
ראש הארגון אמר כי "נקראנו למקום כדי לחלץ אנשים אחרי שמטוס צבאי תקף אותנו שוב. זה היה קשה מאוד עבורנו להעביר את כל הפצועים לבית החולים, כי יש הרבה מאוד קורבנות אך יש לנו מעט מכוניות".

מיאנמר הידרדרה למצב של מלחמת אזרחים מאז ההפיכה הצבאית ב-2021, שבה הודחה ממשלתה של כלת פרס נובל לשלום אונג סן סו צ'י. מאז, לפי ארגוני זכויות אדם, יותר מ-100,000 בני אדם נהרגו בשני צדדי הלחימה. הצבא שולט על העיר מואה בייה הסמוכה לאזור התקיפה, בעוד שכוחות האופוזיציה פועלים בכפרים הקרובים.

עד לתקיפה על החתונה, שהתקיימה באזור שבו מתקיימת לחימה עצימה, אמר כי הבחין לבדו ב-17 גופות. "שמעתי קול של מטוס שטס קרוב מאוד, אבל לא חשבתי שהם יפציצו את האזור שלנו", הוא סיפר. העד הסביר כי לאחר שחזר לביתו, "שמעתי פיצוץ וראיתי הרבה עשן במקום שבו המטוס תקף".

העד הוסיף: "הייתי בהלם, לא ידעתי למי לעזור קודם. אישה פצועה אמרה לי להוציא את הילדים קודם. כמה אנשים עדיין נעדרים, כולל האחיינית שלי. לא מצאתי אותה". הוא ציין בנוסף כי "רוב הנפגעים הם נשים וילדים", ומסר ל-AFP תיעוד שבו נראה גבר נמלט מהמקום כשבידיו תינוק, וכן ילדה קטנה שמחפשת את הוריה.

articles.title: Iraq, Iran hold security talks as Tehran warns Baghdad against becoming Trump's puppet
articles.summary: Al-Hajjaj said the delegation was discussing issues of “strategic importance and high sensitivity,” including border control and other matters of mutual interest between Baghdad and Tehran.
paragraphs: Al-Hajjaj said the delegation was discussing issues of “strategic importance and high sensitivity,” including border control and other matters of mutual interest between Baghdad and Tehran.

An Iraqi security delegation held high-level talks in Tehran on counterterrorism, smuggling, border security, and broader security cooperation between the two countries, Iraq's ambassador to Iran Yasser Abdul-Zahraa Al-Hajjaj announced on Saturday.

In a post on X/Twitter, Al-Hajjaj said the delegation was discussing issues of “strategic importance and high sensitivity,” including border control and other matters of mutual interest between Baghdad and Tehran.
Al-Hajjaj added that the meeting was intended to explore more “prospects for security cooperation between Baghdad and Tehran.”
Khamenei advisor warns Iraq against becoming a tool of Trump's policies

Earlier on Saturday, Mohammad Mokhber, a senior adviser to Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei and former interim president following Ibrahim Raisi's death in 2024, warned Baghdad against allowing its borders to be used by “enemies of Islam.”
“Sharing a common destiny with our neighbors is a fundamental principle” of Iran's foreign policy, Mokhber wrote, adding that Iran had stood by Iraq during its “darkest days.”

He said the relationship “requires Baghdad to remain vigilant on border issues” so that Iraq would not become “a tool in the hands of the enemies of Islam” or an “instrument for carrying out the policies of US President Donald Trump.
'Strait of Hormuz shall remain closed until Iran’s conditions are met'

Iranian Army Commander-in-Chief Maj. Gen. Amir Hatami said the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until Iran's conditions were met, according to a report by Tasnim News Agency, a state-affiliated Iranian outlet.

In remarks marking the Army's Strategic Naval Force Day, Hatami praised the navy's role in closing the strategic waterway and said it was “prepared to make the ultimate sacrifice to defend the country’s territorial integrity and the unity of a powerful Iran”

According to Tasnim, Hatami said Iran's navy, alongside other branches of its military, confronted what he called the world's “arrogant powers” in the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf of Oman and exposed their “weakness and desperation” in the critical waterway.
“The Strait of Hormuz shall remain closed until Iran’s conditions are met,” Hatami’s statement ended.
