articles.title: בניר עוז החליטו: הבתים שנשרפו בטבח יועברו לאתר הנצחה מחוץ לקיבוץ
articles.summary: שלוש שנים לאחר הטבח, בקיבוץ ניר עוז התקבלה החלטה - מהקשות ביותר לאחר השבעה באוקטובר. חברי הקיבוץ הצביעו היכן להציב את אתר ההנצחה לאירועי הטבח, והדעות - מעורבות: "רוצים להנציח - בדרכים אחרות"
paragraphs: שלוש שנים לאחר הטבח, בקיבוץ ניר עוז התקבלה החלטה - מהקשות ביותר לאחר השבעה באוקטובר. חברי הקיבוץ הצביעו היכן להציב את אתר ההנצחה לאירועי הטבח, והדעות - מעורבות: "רוצים להנציח - בדרכים אחרות"
51% ממשתתפי ההצבעה הכריעו כי יש להעביר את הבתים השרופים ואת השאריות שלהם שנותרו אל מחוץ לחצר המשק, ולהקים את אתר ההנצחה ליד בית העלמין. ההצעה התקבלה ברוב של 38 חברים מול 32 שהצביעו נגד.

האפשרות השנייה שהועמדה כהצעה, שקיבלה קולות רק של 32 חברים, היא לשמר במקומם את רוב "בתי העדות", ולהקים במתחם חיצוני מיצב ממ"דים בלבד. ההצעה כללה גם את בית משפחת ביבס, אותו הוצע להשאיר ולעבור יישום כמוקד מורשת חי. א' הוסיף: "מי ששב לחיות כאן, לא רוצה להשאיר בתים הרוסים אלא להנציח את הזיכרון בדרכים אחרות".

"אני מבין את אלו שהתנגדו לכך", אמר א', אחר מחברי הקיבוץ ששמו שמור במערכת. "יחד עם זה, אנשים רוצים לחיות כאן ומאד קשה ולא נעים לחיות לצד בתים שרופים והרוסים. בתי העדות יועתקו לאתר ההנצחה, וכאן ישאר ציון כדי להסביר את מה שהתרחש ולהזכיר".

החברים מונים מספר סיבות לקבלת ההחלטה. לצד רצון לחיות בלי בתי העדות מול העיניים, הם גם לא רוצים שהקבוצות הבאות לבקר ולראות את הקיבוץ יסתובבו ביניהם כאילו הם מיצגים. עוד ציינו, כי לא יתכן שחברים המתגוררים מחוץ לקיבוץ, יחליטו איך האתר יראה והיכן יוקם, כשבמקום החיים הנוכחי שלהם לא נמצאים.

articles.title: ‘Collision course’ with Israel: The senator leading the progressive challenge to Chuck Schumer
articles.summary: Once backed by Israeli-American billionaire Haim Saban, Chris Van Hollen now accuses Netanyahu's government of ethnic cleansing in Gaza and seeks to restrict arms sales to Israel; backed by Bernie Sanders, Elissa Slotkin and Hollywood stars, he is challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate leadership
paragraphs: Once backed by Israeli-American billionaire Haim Saban, Chris Van Hollen now accuses Netanyahu's government of ethnic cleansing in Gaza and seeks to restrict arms sales to Israel; backed by Bernie Sanders, Elissa Slotkin and Hollywood stars, he is challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate leadership

In 2016, when Chris Van Hollen was running for a U.S. Senate seat representing Maryland, Haim Saban, the Israeli-American billionaire who has described Israel as the only political issue that interests him, contributed $100,000 to his election effort. Van Hollen pledged his "absolute commitment to Israel's security."

A decade later, Van Hollen is seeking to lead Senate Democrats after becoming one of the most outspoken critics of Israeli government policy in Congress. His opponent is Chuck Schumer, the highest-ranking Jewish elected official in American history, who has described himself as a "guardian of Israel."
Sens. Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen. Democrats secured a sweeping electoral victory but now face an internal battle over the party's direction
(Photo: Finn Gomez/Getty Images North America/AFP, Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images North America/AFP)

The leadership contest followed the Democrats' sweeping victory in this month's midterm elections. The party flipped nine Republican Senate seats and is expected to hold a 56-44 majority beginning in January, alongside a substantial majority in the House of Representatives. Yet Democrats now find themselves facing their first contested Senate leadership election in more than three decades.

On Tuesday, December 1, Democratic senators will vote by secret ballot to elect their leader, who will guide the party's opposition to President Donald Trump over the next two years while also seeking opportunities for cooperation with his administration. Fifty-five caucus members are expected to participate, with 28 votes needed to win. Van Hollen says he has secured more than 15 votes and claims momentum is on his side. Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats for nearly a decade, says he is confident he will retain his position.

The contest has extended well beyond the corridors of Congress. Hollywood stars Robert De Niro, Jane Fonda and Marisa Tomei, all Democratic Party donors, expressed support for Van Hollen this week. They were preceded by Mark Ruffalo, the Avengers star and one of Hollywood's most vocal critics of Israel.

Ruffalo criticized Schumer over what he described as "deep-seated religious beliefs and loyalties," prompting Anti-Defamation League CEO Jonathan Greenblatt to demand clarification about which religion and loyalties he was referring to, suggesting the remarks invoked the antisemitic trope of Jewish dual loyalty.

Ruffalo stood by his comments, citing a 2018 speech Schumer delivered at the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) conference about the Torah and the Jewish people's connection to the land of Israel. Ruffalo argued that religious beliefs should not determine Palestinian rights.

The actor also shared a petition opposing Hakeem Jeffries' appointment as House speaker, which attracted more than a million signatures. That campaign similarly focused on Jeffries' support for Israel and his relationship with AIPAC. The petition failed to achieve its goal, and Jeffries won his party's House leadership vote by a wide margin.
Despite his emerging image as a progressive challenger and calls from his supporters for new blood in the Democratic Party, Van Hollen is himself a product of the political establishment.
Van Hollen with Benjamin Netanyahu and Lindsey Graham in 2019. He once described America's alliance with Israel as unbreakable
(Photo: Amos Ben Gershom/GPO)

At 67, he is only about eight years younger than Schumer and has spent nearly a quarter-century in Congress. He has held party leadership positions, overseen fundraising operations for Democratic congressional candidates and worked closely with former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and the Obama administration.

For years, Van Hollen was regarded as a methodical, cautious establishment politician. Now, he is challenging the system he helped build. Last year, he described Democrats who refused to support Zohran Mamdani in New York as "spineless."

Until recently, Van Hollen had considered running for president in 2028, but abandoned the idea when he announced his challenge to Schumer. This week, he clarified that he would not seek the White House even if he lost the Senate leadership race.

As Senate majority leader, he promises to challenge Washington's status quo, address the cost of living, expand access to health insurance, curb the influence of billionaires and cryptocurrency companies and reform the Senate's filibuster rules.

Under existing rules, most legislation requires 60 votes in the 100-member Senate to overcome a filibuster, effectively giving the minority party veto power over much of the legislative agenda. Although the rule has endured for decades, it can be changed by a simple majority.
Van Hollen's life story begins far from Maryland politics. Christopher Van Hollen Jr. was born in 1959 in Karachi, Pakistan, to an American family whose life revolved around diplomatic postings.

His father was a diplomat who served as U.S. ambassador to Sri Lanka and the Maldives. His mother, Edith, was a Russian-language specialist who worked for the CIA and later in State Department intelligence, including in a senior position dealing with South Asia.

Van Hollen grew up in Turkey and Sri Lanka, attended boarding school in India and graduated from high school in Massachusetts. Childhood friends described him as a rebellious, liberal teenager who would sneak into the girls' dormitories. Van Hollen himself acknowledged that academic achievement was not his highest priority.

He has said that his childhood taught him to examine American foreign policy through the eyes of people living in other countries. After earning a philosophy degree from Swarthmore College, he studied public policy at Harvard University and later law at Georgetown University.

During a summer vacation, he traveled with friends to Alaska, where they slept in the woods and hitchhiked in search of work. Van Hollen found employment cleaning salmon at a fish processing plant before operating a forklift and unloading catches from fishing boats. He used his earnings to buy a motorcycle and also learned to play poker during that period.

He met his wife, Katherine Wilkens, during his first week at Harvard. They married in 1987 and raised three children, Anna, Nicholas and Alexander, at their home in Kensington, a quiet Washington suburb.

Katherine later recalled that her father had warned her that Chris was "too good a person for politics" and that her role would be to protect him. She keeps a thick binder filled with favorable newspaper clippings about her husband.

Early in his career, American media portrayed him as a reserved politician who would rather go jogging with his 10-year-old son than sit down for a promotional interview. The family spent vacations camping outdoors, and even after entering Congress, Van Hollen continued driving a battered, decade-old Toyota Corolla. The family minivan had accumulated approximately 170,000 miles. Asked whether his children were embarrassed by his cars, he replied: "Of course."

Even before entering elected politics, Van Hollen was involved in documenting war crimes in the Middle East. In 1988, while working as a staff member for the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, he traveled to Turkey with colleague Peter Galbraith to interview Kurdish refugees about Saddam Hussein's chemical attacks. Their findings helped advance sanctions against the Iraqi regime.

In 1990, Van Hollen was elected to the Maryland legislature, where he advocated gun control and environmental protection. In 2002, he defeated Mark Shriver, a member of the Kennedy family, in the Democratic primary before beating popular Republican incumbent Connie Morella in the congressional election.

One of his former legislative colleagues' favorite stories involved an evening at a restaurant in Annapolis, where John Pica, a former lawmaker and lacrosse star, challenged those present to an arm-wrestling contest. Van Hollen was the only one to accept, defeating Pica within two seconds to the amusement of his colleagues.

In May 2022, while serving in the Senate, Van Hollen suffered a mild stroke and was hospitalized for several days. He announced that doctors expected him to make a full recovery without lasting damage and subsequently returned to work. In November of that year, he was elected to his second Senate term with nearly 66% of the vote.
In 2002, Van Hollen described himself as a "longtime friend and strong supporter" of Israel, saying he would not interfere should Israel decide to defend itself against a potential Iraqi attack.

During the Second Lebanon War in 2006, he criticized Israeli military strikes, drawing anger from pro-Israel supporters. However, during Operation Cast Lead in 2008, he again supported Israel's right to act against rocket fire from Gaza.
Van Hollen last month: 'The US shares responsibility for the atrocities in Gaza'

During the 2016 Democratic Senate primary, he was regarded as the more favorable candidate among pro-Israel donors, including Saban, compared with his opponent, Donna Edwards. Upon entering the Senate in 2017, he described Israel as America's greatest ally in the Middle East and characterized the relationship as "unbreakable."
Benjamin Netanyahu has been a central target of Van Hollen's criticism as his positions have evolved.

Van Hollen opposed the annexation of territory in the West Bank, demanded an investigation into the death of Palestinian-American journalist Shireen Abu Akleh and clashed with the Biden administration over its Gaza war policy.

Even before the war, in June 2023, he met Netanyahu in Jerusalem alongside several other senators and raised allegations of settler attacks against Palestinians in the South Hebron Hills. According to Van Hollen, Netanyahu said he was unfamiliar with the incidents and promised to investigate.
"He never got back to us," Van Hollen recalled.

Following the October 7 massacre, Van Hollen acknowledged Israel's right to defend itself and demanded the release of the hostages. As the war continued, however, he became increasingly critical of Palestinian civilian casualties and restrictions on humanitarian assistance.

In January 2024, he visited the Egyptian side of the Rafah crossing and described the humanitarian aid delivery system as dysfunctional. In July that year, he boycotted Netanyahu's address to a joint meeting of Congress.
Van Hollen visiting the Rafah crossing in August 2025. He co-authored a report alleging US complicity in ethnic cleansing
(Photo: AP Photo/Mohammed Arafat)
Van Hollen, right, alongside Egyptian Red Crescent personnel at the Rafah crossing

Van Hollen accused Netanyahu of prioritizing his political survival over the interests of Israeli and American citizens and claimed the prime minister had assembled Israel's most extreme coalition in an attempt to avoid a possible prison sentence.
He subsequently backed an initiative by Sen. Bernie Sanders to condition military assistance on compliance with human rights standards and block arms sales.

Following another visit to the Gaza border region and the West Bank with Sen. Jeff Merkley in August 2025, the two published a report accusing Netanyahu's government of pursuing a policy of ethnic cleansing against Palestinians in Gaza and arguing that the United States bore partial responsibility.
Van Hollen also said he agreed with organizations and scholars who concluded that Israel's actions in Gaza met the legal definition of genocide.

Since then, he has promoted measures to block arms transactions, called for restoring funding to the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA), demanded investigations into the deaths of American citizens in the West Bank and recently led an initiative to remove provisions from defense legislation expanding military and intelligence cooperation with Israel.

In a May opinion piece published in The New York Times, Van Hollen warned that conditions in the Palestinian territories could ultimately lead to Palestinians being expelled or living under what he described as an apartheid system.

He suggested that if efforts to achieve a two-state solution failed, Washington might have to consider alternative political arrangements. He argued that Democrats had failed to advance a two-state solution because they had been unwilling to use America's leverage over Israel.

Van Hollen called for one final effort to preserve the two-state solution, arguing that permanent apartheid or the expulsion of Palestinians would result in continued oppression, regional instability and Israel's international isolation.
He also outlined his vision for U.S. policy toward Israel should a Democratic president be elected in 2028.

Under his proposal, the next Democratic president would recognize Palestinian statehood, subject to conditions including free and fair elections. Until a different agreement was reached, Washington would consider Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, Palestinian territory.

Van Hollen also called for ending American taxpayer-funded assistance to Israel, applying the same weapons procurement conditions imposed on other countries and withholding offensive weapons unless Israel committed to a defined timetable for ending the occupation and implementing a two-state solution.
He advocated reinstating and expanding Biden-era sanctions against individuals and organizations deemed to threaten security and stability in the West Bank.

Van Hollen acknowledged that reviving the two-state solution would be extraordinarily difficult and would put Washington on a "collision course" with any Israeli government opposed to Palestinian statehood. He anticipated substantial domestic opposition, particularly from AIPAC, and urged Democrats to resist that pressure.
He also warned that Democratic primary voters in 2028 would scrutinize the records of lawmakers who had supported weapons transfers to Netanyahu's government.
The differences between Van Hollen and Schumer also extend to Iran.

Van Hollen supported the 2015 nuclear agreement negotiated by the Obama administration. Schumer, one of the few Democrats to oppose it, argued at the time that the deal would grant Tehran sanctions relief without permanently blocking its path to nuclear weapons.

Today, Van Hollen accuses Netanyahu of drawing Trump into a war against Iran and strongly opposes funding military operations against the Islamic Republic. He has pledged that if elected Senate leader, he will seek to block funding for further offensive operations against Iran.
"Netanyahu said he had been waiting 40 years to do this, and finally he found in Donald Trump a president who was stupid enough to agree to it," Van Hollen said.
During his leadership campaign, Van Hollen has repeatedly highlighted Schumer's opposition to the 2015 nuclear agreement, although Schumer later opposed Trump's decision to withdraw from it in 2018.
Van Hollen has also criticized Schumer's close relationship with AIPAC and the lobby's involvement in Democratic primaries against progressive candidates.

Michigan provided a prominent example. Schumer backed Rep. Haley Stevens, while Van Hollen supported Abdul El-Sayed, an Egyptian-American physician and epidemiologist who refuses to recognize Israel as a Jewish state and opposes American military assistance to Israel.

AIPAC and affiliated groups spent approximately $30 million supporting Stevens, but El-Sayed won and is set to become the first Muslim U.S. senator in January. El-Sayed was subsequently among the first to urge Van Hollen to challenge Schumer.

Alongside El-Sayed, Van Hollen's publicly declared supporters include Sanders, Merkley, Minnesota Sen.-elect Peggy Flanagan, Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin and former Rep. Donna Edwards, whom Van Hollen defeated in the 2016 Senate primary.

Slotkin's endorsement is particularly notable. A Jewish former CIA officer and moderate Democrat, she previously received AIPAC's support and for years presented herself as a strong supporter of Israel's security.

She continues to emphasize her support for Israel as a Jewish and democratic state and for defensive systems such as Iron Dome. This year, however, she voted to block sales of bombs and other offensive weapons to Israel, arguing that supporting Israel does not require supporting Netanyahu.
Slotkin explained her endorsement of Van Hollen by citing the need for a new generation of leadership, rather than necessarily agreeing with all of his positions.
On the other side are several prominent Democrats, including Pennsylvania Sen. John Fetterman, who has remained a staunch supporter of Israel throughout the Gaza war.

Fetterman argued that Van Hollen's prominence stemmed largely from his "hostility toward Israel," which he said had made him a progressive star. He warned that Van Hollen's election as Senate leader could cross a personal "red line" within the Democratic Party.
His remarks have raised speculation that he could leave the party, although the Democrats' substantial Senate majority would limit the immediate impact of such a move.

Angela Alsobrooks, Maryland's other Democratic senator, has also announced that she will support Schumer, citing a previous commitment. The Jewish Democratic Council of America (JDCA) backs Schumer, while the liberal pro-Israel advocacy organization J Street has remained neutral.
Schumer, who celebrated his 76th birthday this week, faces significant challenges despite his party's electoral success.

He represents an older generation of Democratic leadership, which critics accuse of being insufficiently confrontational toward Trump. In March 2025, he angered Democratic activists by helping advance a Republican government funding bill to prevent a shutdown. His critics argued that he had surrendered one of the few sources of leverage available against the president.
Meanwhile, progressive Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has been mentioned as a potential challenger to Schumer in New York's 2028 Democratic Senate primary.

Some longtime Democrats have already suggested that Schumer announce his retirement at the end of his current term to avoid repeating what critics regard as Joe Biden's mistake of remaining in power when voters were demanding change.

Trump himself joined the criticism this week. The president has repeatedly referred to Schumer as a "Palestinian" because of his criticism of Netanyahu's government, criticism that Schumer's progressive opponents consider insufficient.
"It will be very difficult for me to work with Chuck Schumer if he becomes Senate majority leader," Trump wrote on Truth Social, describing him as one of the worst leaders in history.

articles.title: The Netanyahu trial: Distinguishing between criminal liability and public scrutiny - analysis
articles.summary: A plea bargain could resolve Netanyahu’s criminal proceedings, but it cannot settle the broader question of what the public expects from those who govern it.
paragraphs: The judges in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s criminal trial asked the attorney-general on Wednesday to rethink how the case should proceed.

Attorney-General Gali Baharav-Miara said the court’s comments would be examined, and reiterated the prosecution’s willingness to pursue an agreement. Netanyahu’s lawyer, Amit Hadad, called for mediation through the court.

But, reaching a plea bargain would involve more than deciding which charges remain: A conviction could also affect Netanyahu’s ability to hold public office. That is where moral turpitude, or kalon, becomes central.
First, though, it’s critical to be precise about what happened on Wednesday.

The judges did not acquit Netanyahu or remove any charges. They urged prosecutors to reconsider the entire Case 4000 count against him, questioned whether the conduct alleged in Case 2000 constitutes an offense, and sought a way to bring Case 1000 to a conclusion. They stressed that these were their impressions so far, and not a verdict.

In Case 4000, their concerns went beyond the bribery charge, which they had already twice urged prosecutors to reconsider. This time, they also questioned the basis for the breach-of-trust accusation.

They doubted whether they could rely on former Communications Ministry director-general Shlomo Filber’s account of Netanyahu’s alleged instruction to favor telecommunications company Bezeq. They also questioned whether prosecutors had proved unusual responsiveness to coverage requests at Walla, and whether Netanyahu knew of that treatment at the time.

The prosecution alleges that Netanyahu exercised public authority over matters affecting Bezeq while receiving a personal benefit through Walla’s handling of coverage requests. The alleged conflict was between his duty to make regulatory decisions in the public interest, and his personal interest in that media treatment. That explains why doubts about whether the treatment was established, and whether Netanyahu knew of it, matter to the breach-of-trust accusation as well as the bribery charge.

The distinction also carries over to the possible implications for fellow defendants Shaul Elovitch, Bezeq’s former controlling shareholder, and his wife, Iris. A doubt about what Netanyahu knew concerns his state of mind, but a doubt about whether the alleged unusual responsiveness was proven concerns the relationship that the prosecution holds existed.
Those are different questions, even within the same alleged exchange, but the judges expressly limited their remarks to Netanyahu and did not reach conclusions about the Elovitches.

In Case 2000, they raised a different problem: whether the conduct described in the indictment amounts to a criminal offense. The case concerns Netanyahu’s discussions with Yediot Aharonot publisher Arnon “Noni” Mozes about favorable coverage, in exchange for measures restricting rival newspaper Israel Hayom. They said prosecutors should have an opportunity to explain their legal argument before the court decides how to proceed, so that question remains open.
Resolution of Case 1000 could have critical impact on other cases

In Case 1000, however, the judges did not express comparable doubts. They said most of the evidence was before them and sought a way to reach a decision. The gifts case concerns benefits Netanyahu allegedly received from wealthy businessmen and steps he allegedly took to advance businessman Arnon Milchan’s interests. If negotiations focus on that case, the details of what Netanyahu would agree to admit would be critical.

A plea bargain would require the two sides to agree on the facts he would admit – and the charges it would resolve. Those admissions could allow the court to convict him without hearing the remaining evidence on those charges. The facts he admits would still have to establish the offenses.

The two sides could also recommend a sentence together, agree on a sentencing range, or leave each side free to argue for the punishment that it considers appropriate. The judges would decide the sentence and would not be bound by the parties’ recommendations.

Mediation is one way to try to reach those agreements. Both sides must consent, and it ordinarily takes place before a judge different from those hearing the evidence. The mediator helps them work through their differences, although neither an agreement or deal are guaranteed.

Prosecutors could drop charges against Netanyahu without requiring him to plead guilty to anything else, and an agreement with Netanyahu would not automatically end the proceedings against the other defendants.
Question of moral turpitude yet to be addressed
For Netanyahu, however, an agreement leading to a conviction would still leave the question of moral turpitude to be addressed.

Kalon concerns the moral gravity of the offense in its circumstances and its implications for holding public office. It is a legal determination, distinct from the broader judgment voters make about a politician’s conduct.

The rule for a serving prime minister is explicit. Under Basic Law: The Government, the court convicting him must determine whether the offense involves moral turpitude. If it does, the Knesset may remove him by a majority. If it does not, his tenure ends when the judgment becomes final – after any appeal has been resolved or the deadline for appealing has passed – and the government is deemed to have resigned.

That is why dropping bribery would not, on its own, settle the matter. If Netanyahu were convicted of breach of trust while serving as prime minister, the court would still have to decide whether the offense indicates moral turpitude.

The lawyers could agree on the position they present to the court, or disagree and argue their respective positions, but the decision would remain the judges’. A plea agreement could not remove that responsibility.

This is familiar ground. Moral turpitude was a major point of contention during the 2022 negotiations. Reports at the time described a possible agreement dropping Case 2000 and the bribery charge in Case 4000, while retaining fraud and breach-of-trust offenses in Cases 1000 and 4000. Netanyahu publicly denied having agreed to moral turpitude and said he would remain in politics. Those talks did not produce an agreement.

On Wednesday, Baharav-Miara maintained that an agreement would have to reflect the nature of the alleged conduct and offenses. Her willingness to discuss one does not indicate which terms she would accept.

The prosecution’s own guidelines require any plea agreement to be consistent with the public interest. The guidelines identify difficulties in presenting evidence and proving guilt among the considerations relevant to that decision.

Netanyahu’s declaration on Wednesday night that “the trial has collapsed” went beyond what the judges said; they had not delivered a verdict. But their doubts should not be brushed aside as technical obstacles to a guilt that has somehow already been established.

Because it has not. The prosecution must prove an offense beyond reasonable doubt, and Netanyahu does not have to prove his innocence. If the prosecution fails to meet that threshold, the court must acquit him of the charge.
Public opinion of Netanyahu to remain an issue beyond court proceedings
What the public makes of established conduct is a separate question.

What is proved or disproved in a courtroom does not automatically tell us everything about a person’s fitness to govern. Voters and political partners can ask whether conduct reflects the judgment, integrity, and restraint they expect from a prime minister, but they still have to distinguish what has been established from what has not.

This becomes particularly important when the legal dispute is about whether conduct constitutes a crime at all, because something can fall outside a criminal prohibition and still warrant public criticism. Criticism, in turn, cannot take the place of proof.

The same care is needed when judging the prosecution. An acquittal would not, by itself, prove that the case was fabricated, or that the trial was pointless. Nor would it shield the decisions that led to the trial from examination.

The charges brought, the handling of the evidence and the length of the proceedings can all be questioned. Neither an indictment nor an acquittal will answer every question about how the case was conducted.
The court must decide criminal liability, and the public still has to decide what it expects from those who govern it.
A plea bargain could resolve Netanyahu’s criminal proceedings, but it cannot settle that broader question.

articles.title: ‘Disaster’ unfolding as Sydney fire ant outbreak partly blamed on ignored biosecurity recommendations
articles.summary: Farmers’ Federation president says Australia ‘can’t even keep [illicit] cigarettes out of the country … let alone some of these difficult-to-detect pests’ Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Years-old recommendations by Australia’s biosecurity watchdog have been ignored or not acted on by successive federal governments, increasing the risk of an invasive pest outbreak such as the fire ants discovered in Sydney this week, according to experts. Environmentalists and biosecurity experts warn the large colony of red imported fire ants are a warning sign that the…
paragraphs: Years-old recommendations by Australia’s biosecurity watchdog have been ignored or not acted on by successive federal governments, increasing the risk of an invasive pest outbreak such as the fire ants discovered in Sydney this week, according to experts.

Environmentalists and biosecurity experts warn the large colony of red imported fire ants are a warning sign that the country’s quarantine system is too slow-moving, underfunded and overly concerned with agriculture.
The nest was found in Auburn and is the second outbreak of the invasive species in Sydney this year after they were discovered at the Enfield intermodal logistics centre on 23 September.
Both sites are industrial areas dealing with imported goods.
On Friday, the New South Wales government introduced a biosecurity control order focusing on the 500-metre area and extending a radius of 2km from the Auburn detection site epicentre.

More than 4,800 businesses and 2,400 residences covered by the order will be compelled to protect the zone when transporting high risk material – for instance, appropriately treating, checking, and covering loads.
The NSW agriculture minister, Tara Moriarty, said on Wednesday that the Auburn outbreak was “different to what has occurred in the past and is seemingly the result of infested imported goods”.
“Our government is boosting our on-ground resources and establishing a taskforce to focus on tracing the supply chains that have led to this occurring,” she said.
But experts say there have been years of warnings about Australia’s biosecurity, often not acted on by the federal government, that might have made a difference in halting the ants’ spread.

The policy director of the Invasive Species Council, Carol Booth, pointed to a 2021 review by the inspector general of biosecurity of the controls for the Khapra beetle, which made recommendations to improve the entire quarantine system.
The south Asian beetle is the second-highest identified national priority plant pest, due to its risks to the grain industry.

At the time, the inspector general made 13 recommendations, including that the department “improve its level of regulatory agility”, “with an expectation of response time frames of days or weeks, not months or years” due to the rapidly evolving risk of outbreak.
It also criticised the federal government for not acting when the risk of the beetle arriving was first identified in July 2020.

“This delay is an illustration of the department’s continuing regulatory immaturity,” the inspector general found, suggesting either a poorly defined risk assessment process or an overly cavalier attitude to risk.

Four years later, nothing had been done about the recommendation to improve response times. An October 2025 review of the report by the inspector general found that all but one of the recommendations were still open.
Booth said the recommendation was particularly significant because biosecurity risks to Australia were endlessly evolving and increasing, partly due to climate change.
“There are just so many things they should be doing that they’re not, or they weren’t doing well, or they weren’t auditing to ensure that their measures were being actually implemented,” Booth said.
“There’s definitely some things they do well, but others, they just don’t have the resources.”
The Guardian understands the recommendation has since been implemented.

Hamish McIntyre, the president of the National Farmers’ Federation, said farmers “believe we are watching a national biosecurity and human health disaster unfold in front of our eyes around fire ants” due to a failure of the quarantine system.
“We can’t even keep [illicit] cigarettes out of the country through our borders, let alone some of these difficult-to-detect pests.”
He said being an island nation was Australia’s greatest biosecurity advantage.
The federal minister for agriculture, Julie Collins, said the government had delivered over $2bn in additional biosecurity resourcing since 2022.
“This includes more than $296m in the current red imported fire ant eradication program,” she said.

“In the last financial year alone, federal biosecurity officers inspected almost 350,000 commercial sea and air cargoes, preventing tens of thousands of harmful pests, diseases and weeds from entering Australia.”
Tom Kompas, a professor of environmental economics and biosecurity at the University of Melbourne, said it was likely that Sydney’s infestation was broader than currently thought.
“If it does get into metro Sydney, it would be a disaster. It would be an absolute disaster,” he said.
Australia has a reputation for extraordinarily tough and strict biosecurity controls but no system can block, inspect or decontaminate every container of every pest.
“We’re going to have incursions of fire ants, among other things,” the Invasive Species Council chief executive, Jack Gough, said.
“The key is basically how early in the biosecurity system we’re catching these things, such that then it’s a lot easier to deal with.”
While the Enfield site had been subject to pest inspections, Gough said there had been “clear failings” because its fire ant mitigation process did not match the ant’s biology.
Lures were only placed in some businesses once a year but ants can move after six months, he said. They were also placed too far apart, further than the 40 or so metres the ants will roam.
He said this was partly due to underfunding and an overreliance on mitigation in the private sector.

Kompas said the biosecurity system was hampered by its approach to risk, with funding against an individual pest allocated according to concern levels. According to him, a better approach would be to allocate funding based on an assessment of cost effectiveness and suggested testing Australian cows for foot-and-mouth disease is probably overfunded.
He said the system placed an overemphasis on mitigating risks to agriculture rather than the environment.
Ultimately, it falls to the taxpayer to pay for eradication, Gough said. Queensland’s fire ant eradication program costs more than $100m a year.

The Invasive Species Council has long called for a new tax on importers to fund the country’s biosecurity system but Gough said Australia’s obligations under World Trade Organization agreements had prevented its implementation as a flat fee.

articles.title: צוות טקילה פעל באזור השרון במשך שעות: נעצר החשוד שתכנן לבצע פיגוע | צפו
articles.summary: כוחות רבים של המשטרה, שב"כ ויחידות מיוחדות חיפשו אחר חשוד ברחבי רמת השרון. ל"מעריב" נודע כי לפי מידע שהתקבל מהשב"כ, מדובר ככל הנראה דרוש חקירה כגורם עוין. הוא נעצר ללא נשק
paragraphs: כוחות רבים של המשטרה, שב"כ ויחידות מיוחדות חיפשו אחר חשוד ברחבי רמת השרון. ל"מעריב" נודע כי לפי מידע שהתקבל מהשב"כ, מדובר ככל הנראה דרוש חקירה כגורם עוין. הוא נעצר ללא נשק

ל"מעריב" נודע כי על פי מידע שהתקבל מהשב"כ, מדובר ככל הנראה בגורם עוין שהצליח לחדור לתחומי מדינת ישראל והגיע לאזור רמת השרון. אולם, בשלב זה לא נמסרו הנחיות מיוחדות לציבור. כוחות הביטחון ממשיכים בחיפושים אחר החשוד במטרה לאתרו.

בהמשך לכך, לפי צה"ל, הם לא פעלו ברמת השרון. מי שלבושים במדים זה לוחמי טקילה וימ"מ. הופעל צוות טקילה על בסיס מידע של דרוש שב"כ שנע על ציר 5 והגיע לאזור רמת השרון, לאחר שכנראה ניסה להסתתר באתר בניה. בשב"כ לא לקחו סיכונים ולכן הפעילות.

מדובר על פי החשד באדם יחיד שככל הנראה הסתתר באתר בנייה של אחת החברות המובילות בתחום הבנייה בישראל. למקום הוזנקה גם יחידת הכלבנים שסורקת את האתר בסיוע גלאי קול. במקום הוקם חפ"ק והופעל צוות טקילה כשרחפנים חגים באוויר כבר למעלה משעתיים.
מהצבא נמסר, כי "בהמשך לפניות כתבים, נבהיר כי המשטרה פועלת בעת הזו לאיתור אדם הדרוש לחקירה באזור העיר רמת השרון. אין שינוי בהנחיות לציבור".

articles.title: Israeli strikes kill 16 schoolchildren so far this month, Gaza ministry says
articles.summary: Statement follows death of sisters, aged 15 and 13, in airstrike on residential apartment in Gaza City Israeli strikes have killed at least 16 schoolchildren in Gaza since the start of November, as young people across the territory face intensifying bombardment and a struggle to find food, clean water and shelter. On Wednesday, Gaza’s ministry of education said: “Palestinian students had been targeted for the third time in less than 24 hours, in an escalation reflecting the continued Israeli violations against children in the Gaza Strip. The number of schoolchildren killed since the…
paragraphs: Israeli strikes have killed at least 16 schoolchildren in Gaza since the start of November, as young people across the territory face intensifying bombardment and a struggle to find food, clean water and shelter.

On Wednesday, Gaza’s ministry of education said: “Palestinian students had been targeted for the third time in less than 24 hours, in an escalation reflecting the continued Israeli violations against children in the Gaza Strip. The number of schoolchildren killed since the beginning of November has now risen to 16.”
The statement follows the death of two sisters, Yusra, 15, and Jana Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, 13, in the early hours of Wednesday in an airstrike targeting a residential apartment in western Gaza City.
Yusra was a pupil at Kafr Qasim school, while her sister Jana attended al-Manar private school.

The ministry added: “The girls’ father, Mohammed Majed Abu Al-Ouf, and their mother, Noura Ezzat Abu Al-Ouf, were also killed in the strike which injured several other Palestinians.” The father was a director of internal security services for Hamas in northern Gaza.
Earlier this year, an independent UN inquiry found that Israel continued to commit genocide by deliberately targeting Palestinian children in Gaza.
On 6 November, Mohammed Nidal Barbakh, 15, was shot by Israeli forces in the Bir 19 area of al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, and later died from his injuries.
He was in the 10th grade at the Muscat school and dreamed of becoming a professional football player.

“That day, after lunch, Mohammed went to the sports academy at 1.30pm to take part in training,” his father, Dr Nidal Mohammed Barbakh, said. “An Israeli tank had advanced and positioned itself on a nearby hill before firing two rounds towards the pitch. One of them ricocheted after hitting a metal object, striking Mohammed in the back and exiting through his neck.

“He was talented and an excellent student. He was killed at the age of 15, on a sports pitch in al-Mawasi, an area where people had been told to go because it was considered safe. I do not absolve the Israeli army of responsibility for what happened. It kills every ambition within us and buries our children’s dreams before they have a chance to come true.”
On 13 November, Israeli artillery shelling killed three people in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, including a father and his 12-year-old son, Ahmed Abu Daher, as well as a woman.
Ahmed dreamed of becoming an Arabic language teacher, like his grandfather Saleh, said his mother, Walaa Abu Daher.

“That day, my husband was heading to a condolence gathering in the al-Qastal area, east of Deir al-Balah,” Daher said. “Ahmed asked his father if he could accompany him. While they were at the gathering, they were targeted by Israeli artillery fire.

“Ahmed ran to ask the people attending the gathering for help. He then rushed back towards his father when a second shell was fired. Shrapnel struck Ahmed in his legs, abdomen and head. I cannot describe how deeply their loss has affected me. I feel as though my life stopped that day.”
Thousands of school-age children and hundreds of education workers have been killed in Israel’s war in Gaza, while tens of thousands of children have been unable to attend school regularly.

On Thursday, Israeli attacks killed at least nine Palestinians across Gaza, including Khaled Abu Nada, the undersecretary of Gaza’s ministry of education, and his wife, according to health officials, as attacks continued despite the ceasefire in the territory.
A few days ago, the ministry of education said Israel’s attacks against students, civilian leaders and teachers were “part of a systematic assault on the Palestinian education system”.
According to Unicef, 98% of school buildings in Gaza have sustained damage, with more than 93% requiring major rehabilitation or full reconstruction, while approximately 81% were directly hit.
Young Palestinians in Gaza face a fourth winter in overcrowded tents and makeshift shelters, with limited access to basic services as the humanitarian and public health crisis deepens.

Children and young people are among those most vulnerable to meningitis, for which Gaza’s health ministry issued an epidemic alert on Tuesday after a sharp rise in infections, with more than 270 new cases reported in October.

Health organisations attribute the rise in infections to the destruction of infrastructure, overcrowded shelters and the contamination of drinking water with sewage – a crisis made worse by winter flooding and restrictions on humanitarian aid.

At least 74,746 Palestinians have been killed in Israel’s war in Gaza over the last three years, according to the territory’s health ministry. More than 20,000 children have been reported killed by Israeli strikes.
The Israel Defense Forces said there was not enough information to comment on the incidents involving Ahmed and Mohammed.
It said that on the day Ahmed died it was carrying out operations that resulted in the killing of “10 terrorists” and “prior to the strikes, measures were taken to mitigate harm to civilians”.

articles.title: אחרי ההתקדמות בהקמת ועדת חקירה ממלכתית: אייל אשל במסר נחרץ
articles.summary: לאחר אישור החוק להקמת ועדת חקירה ממלכתית בקריאה טרומית, אייל אשל, אביה של התצפיתנית רוני אשל ז"ל, דורש למצות את הדין עם האחראים למחדל ומשתף בכאב על השיחות עם בתו לפני הטבח
paragraphs: לאחר אישור החוק להקמת ועדת חקירה ממלכתית בקריאה טרומית, אייל אשל, אביה של התצפיתנית רוני אשל ז"ל, דורש למצות את הדין עם האחראים למחדל ומשתף בכאב על השיחות עם בתו לפני הטבח

"אני לא זעקתי לבד, אנחנו זעקנו כולנו. הצטרפו אלינו הרבה מאוד אנשים טובים, מה שנקרא עם ישראל היפה והקול השפוי. הזעקה הייתה המשימה שנקראנו אליה. אני באופן אישי קיבלתי את המשימה הזאת מרוני, שזעקה לי 'תוציא את האמת והצדק לאור'".

"הבקשה היא בעיקר 'תוציא את האמת והצדק לאור', כי רוני רדפה צדק. היא אהבה לחיות והיא איננה פה איתנו פה היום. אז זו המשימה שקיבלתי ואלינו הצטרף רפי בן שטרית, אביו של אלרועי, ויחד איתנו היה חיים רובינשטיין שעזר, סימן לנו את הדרך לאורך כל התקופה הזו. בין אם זה ועדת החקירה האזרחית שהקמנו ומועצת אוקטובר שאליה נשלחנו אחרי אותה ועדת חקירה אזרחית. זעקתנו נשמעה ונשבענו שלא נרפה ולא נפסיק. אנחנו בהחלט רואים את הנורה הקטנה".

על המשך המאבק אמר: "נכון שזו קריאה טרומית וזה השלב הראשון, אבל יהיה גם שלב סופי. באותו שלב הסופי אנחנו מאמינים באמת, באמונה שלמה, שבסוף האחראים למחדל, לטבח, לשואה בת יום שקיבלנו בישראל, יישאו בתוצאה ויצטרכו לצעוד אחר כבוד לבית המשפט ולשלם על כך בדין. אני לא רואה שום קונסטלציה אחרת, למעט השלב הזה שבוא יבוא".

אשל שב לשיחות שניהל עם בתו לפני הטבח: "אנחנו גרמנו לכולם לראות את מה שאנחנו יודעים וידענו, אני מייסר את עצמי עד היום ששמעתי בקולה של רוני. אני מייסר את עצמי ששמעתי בקולה 'אבא, אל תעשה לי פדיחות'. אני התחננתי אליה 'תני לי טלפון אחד, על כל העוולות שמרביצים לכן, לא במובן הפיזי כמובן - אלא במובן שהבנות זעקו את נשמתן בחמ"ל ואף אחד לא הקשיב להן'".
"כל התקופה הזו זעקתי לצה"ל 'איך הושבתם את הבנות הטובות האלה על המערכות היקרות ביותר בעולם, ובסוף לא הקשבתם להן?'", הוסיף.

על השינויים במערך התצפיתניות מאז 7 באוקטובר סיפר: "סימנו 'וי' על כל התהליך של כניסת הבנות החדשות לחיל הגנת הגבולות, בהיותן המתגייסות החדשות, להיות תצפיתניות. סימנו 'וי' כי כל חיילת כעת שמתגייסת מקבלת נשק, מה שלא היה בתקופה של רוני, וסימנו 'וי' בהתייחסות כי מתייחסים לבנות הללו כמו מלכות, גם אם יש בעיות פה ושם".

עם זאת, הבהיר: "הבנות הללו עדיין נמצאות על קווי הגבול, אני האחרון שיכול להגיד משהו למערכת הביטחון, אבל כן הבנות מוגנות יותר. תשאל אם אני דואג? אני ממשיך לדאוג. אני חושב שלא הפיקו או התכנסו לתוך כל המחדל של שבת 7 באוקטובר".
לקראת סיום הריאיון שאל בר-און את אשל: "מה יהיה המסר שלך, כשתעמוד בפני חמשת החוקרים בראשות שופט עליון, אם אתה צריך בשורה אחת להגיד לו למה או מה אתה לוקח מכל מסע האבל שלך ופעילותך".

אשל השיב: "אדוני השופט, אני מבקש ממך להיות איתך, להיות יחד איתנו בצד הזה, ולהוריד את המונח הזה חטא היוהרה. אנחנו לא יכולים להמשיך עם הקו של אנחנו הכי טובים ומקצועיים או מלומדים. יש עוד אנשים שלמדו את המקצוע, קרי צבא חמאס, שעשה מה שעשה לנו באותה שבת. אנחנו לא יכולים להמשיך עם המונח הזה שאנחנו הכי מושלמים ולא יקרה לנו כלום - תראו מה קרה לנו ב-7 באוקטובר".

articles.title: ‘Complete madness’: Outrage in Milan after Christmas tree renamed ‘Tree of Gifts’
articles.summary: Critics accuse Milan’s city hall of downplaying Christian traditions to avoid offending Muslims following last month’s violent unrest; Mayor Giuseppe Sala rejects the allegations, saying the name reflects a fundraising initiative for people in need
paragraphs: Critics accuse Milan’s city hall of downplaying Christian traditions to avoid offending Muslims following last month’s violent unrest; Mayor Giuseppe Sala rejects the allegations, saying the name reflects a fundraising initiative for people in need

A public controversy has erupted in Italy after Milan's municipal authorities chose to call the giant fir tree installed in the city's iconic Piazza del Duomo the "Tree of Gifts" rather than the traditional "Christmas tree."

The dispute comes several weeks after violent unrest erupted in the northern Italian city, involving young people, many from immigrant families, who vandalized numerous shops in the city center and clashed with security forces. Critics have suggested that the decision to rename the traditional Christmas symbol was intended to avoid offending Muslim residents.
The giant fir tree installed in Milan's Piazza del Duomo
(Photo: Municipality of Milan)
Many residents expressed outrage over the name given to the 26-meter-tall tree, which is scheduled to be officially illuminated on December 4.

"What happened to the Christmas tree? Has it become a problem to call it by its name?" social media users asked. "Milan has lost its traditions," another user wrote, while another commented: "They're changing names to rewrite history, all in an attempt to please everyone."

Many critics accused the municipal administration, led by center-left Mayor Giuseppe Sala, of attempting to appease Muslims and Islamists by downplaying the tree's traditional Christian religious significance.

Deborah Dell'Acqua, a local representative of the right-wing Brothers of Italy party, argued that Christmas was an integral part of Italy's history, culture and identity, and that respecting local traditions did not mean excluding anyone. She accused Sala of censoring Italian traditions.
Other right-wing politicians in Milan and across Italy were quick to condemn the decision, arguing that the country had succumbed to excessive political correctness and progressive "woke" culture.
Milan City Council member Francesco Rocca went further, describing the decision as "complete madness" and calling on residents to rebel.
Former Milan Mayor Gabriele Albertini also criticized the decision. "We celebrate Christmas. Our Christian civilization celebrates Christmas, and changing that is simply wrong," he said.
Protesters wave a Palestinian flag in Milan in October
(Photo: AP Photo/Antonio Calanni)

Albertini pointed to the traditional use of BC and AD in Western society, describing attempts to erase such references to avoid offending people of other faiths as absurd. "Those who come to our country as Muslims remain Muslims. We believe in the right to be different, but they believe in having different rights," he said.

Municipal officials rejected claims that the name change was intended to obscure any religious or traditional identity, explaining that it was linked to sponsorship arrangements for this year's project, which aims to raise funds for people in need.

Mayor Sala dismissed the controversy and criticized those attacking the initiative. "It's called the Tree of Gifts because this year we are encouraging people to donate to those in need," he said, describing the controversy as pointless and foolish.
"Back in 2020, the Christmas tree was also called the Tree of Gifts, and nobody had a problem with it then."
Sala added that his administration would not be drawn into a shallow debate and would continue promoting Milan's high-quality cultural offerings.

articles.title: "הלקח המרכזי שלנו": המסר של צה"ל לאחר שהשמיד אתר אסטרטגי של כוח רדואן
articles.summary: צה"ל תקף עשרות רקטות וקני שיגור של כוח רדואן במרחב עין א-תינה שבדרום לבנון. גורם צבאי מסר כי התקיפה כוונה למחסן רקטות גדול, ולאחריה זוהו פיצוצי משנה המעידים על כמות אמצעי הלחימה שהוחזקו במקום
paragraphs: צה"ל תקף עשרות רקטות וקני שיגור של כוח רדואן במרחב עין א-תינה שבדרום לבנון. גורם צבאי מסר כי התקיפה כוונה למחסן רקטות גדול, ולאחריה זוהו פיצוצי משנה המעידים על כמות אמצעי הלחימה שהוחזקו במקום

צה"ל תקף הערב (חמישי) עשרות רקטות וקני שיגור במחנה אימונים של יחידת כוח רדואן של חיזבאללה, במרחב עין א-תינה שבדרום לבנון, כך מסר דובר צה"ל. על פי ההודעה, אמצעי הלחימה נועדו לפגיעה בכוחות צה"ל ובאזרחי ישראל, והותקפו מהאוויר להסרת האיום.
גורם צבאי התייחס בעקבות התקיפה להיקף אמצעי הלחימה שאוחסנו במקום ואמר: "התקיפה כוונה לעבר מחסן גדול של רקטות". לדבריו, "לאחר הפגיעה זוהו פיצוצי משנה מה שמעיד על כמות הרקטות הגדולה שהיתה במקום".
"זה הלקח המרכזי שלנו מה7 באוקטובר"

הגורם הצבאי הדגיש כי התקיפה משקפת את מדיניות צה"ל לפעול נגד איומים עוד לפני התממשותם. "צה״ל עוקב אחר פעילות חיזבאללה והוא לא יאפשר לאיומים להתפתח ולגדול ולסכן את מדינת ישראל. זה הלקח המרכזי שלנו מה7 באוקטובר. וזה מה שמנחה אותנו כעת", אמר.
בצה"ל מסרו אז כי האתר הותקף מספר פעמים במהלך המלחמה, וכי בתקופה האחרונה זוהתה הגעתם של מחבלי חיזבאללה למקום. בעקבות זאת תקף חיל האוויר את הכניסות לאתר, במטרה למנוע את שיקומו.
על פי הודעת צה"ל מאותה תקיפה, האתר שימש לייצור ולהרכבה של טילים מדויקים וכטב"מים, המיוצרים באיראן ומועברים לבקעת הלבנון כערכות להרכבה.

articles.title: Maccabi Tel Aviv basketball secures win in Munich as Hapoel Tel Aviv drops to .500
articles.summary: Maccabi Tel Aviv secured a convincing victory in Munich, while Hapoel Tel Aviv suffered another setback, dropping to a .500 record.
paragraphs: The Israeli Euroleague representatives left the international window with mixed results: Maccabi Tel Aviv picked up a much-needed win, while Hapoel Tel Aviv continued its recent poor play and dropped its fifth game in the last six.
Maccabi Tel Aviv defeated Bayern Munich 87-79 on the road in Euroleague action, snapping a two-game losing streak and improving its record to 4-10, moving up to 18th place in the standings.

In a game where the momentum shifted back and forth, Bayern held a slim 68–66 lead at the end of the third quarter. However, Oded Katash’s team ultimately prevailed thanks to a dominant fourth quarter.

With 4:44 remaining, Maccabi trailed 74–71, but from then on it went on a decisive 12-0 run while holding the German side scoreless for more than four minutes. Roman Sorkin, in what was his best performance of the season, sparked the run by scoring eight consecutive points.
Sorkin finished with 17 points, while Jimmy Clark and Yam Madar added 13 points each in the win, and Duane Washington and Marjon Beauchamp scored 13 points each for Bayern in the loss.
Head coach Katash satisfied with team's defense, performance in win against Bayern Munich
Katash was satisfied with his team’s performance, especially at the defensive end.
“As long as we keep it simple offensively, it will be good for us. But defensively, we won the game. We improved our defense in the last few games. I liked the attitude and the body language.”
Sorkin, the game’s MVP, also spoke about the victory.

“The most important thing was the win. We were really desperate for this. We lost a lot of close games where we felt we were the better team. We need to win every game. We still have goals for the season that we want to achieve. We can’t lose those games. Fortunately, we closed this game and got better from the last one.”
Hapoel drops to .500 on the season following loss to Olympiacos

Meanwhile, Hapoel Tel Aviv fell to Olympiacos 104-79 in a road defeat in Piraeus, dropping to 7-7 and 12th in the standings. For the Reds, it was their second consecutive defeat and their fifth continental loss in their last six games.

After an offensively strong first quarter, which Olympiacos won 32–29, Hapoel went on a 9-0 run to take a six-point lead early in the second quarter. However, the hosts closed out the first half with a 7-0 run of their own, taking a 49–44 lead into halftime.

In the third quarter, Olympiacos built a nine-point advantage and finished the period up 72-66. The hosts then opened the fourth quarter with a 9-0 run, while Hapoel went scoreless and lost the final frame 32-13, allowing the Greek side to finish off the rout.
Hapoel coach Dimitrios Itoudis spoke about the loss.

“Turnovers cost us a lot. We were still in the game at the end of the third quarter, and we could have done a much better job coming out for the final period. The way we gave up was humiliating, and we turned the ball over far too many times. Twenty-one turnovers is way too many.”
In other news, over the upcoming weeks. Hapoel will be moving its base of operations back to Tel Aviv from Sofia, Bulgaria, where it has been for the past three years due to the war.
See more Israeli sports coverage at www.sportsrabbi.com/en

articles.title: הניפו דגלי פלסטין במשחק מול הפועל באר שבע - כך הגיבה המשטרה
articles.summary: המשטרה הגאורגית הפעילה כוח נגד אוהדי בשיקטאש שהניפו דגלי פלסטין במשחק מול הפועל באר שבע בבאטומי. בעקבות העימותים האלימים ביציעים הופסק המשחק בדקה ה-26, ואוהדים פונו על אלונקות
paragraphs: המשטרה הגאורגית הפעילה כוח נגד אוהדי בשיקטאש שהניפו דגלי פלסטין במשחק מול הפועל באר שבע בבאטומי. בעקבות העימותים האלימים ביציעים הופסק המשחק בדקה ה-26, ואוהדים פונו על אלונקות

המחאה הפרו-פלסטינית של אוהדי בשיקטאש החלה שעות לפני שריקת הפתיחה. מאות מאוהדי הקבוצה הטורקית התאספו בכיכר אירופה שבמרכז באטומי, הניפו דגלי פלסטין וטורקיה ופרשו כרזה הקוראת לשחרור פלסטין. האוהדים שרו שירי עידוד והדליקו אבוקות עשן. לפי דיווחים בטורקיה, גם אוהדי פנרבחצ'ה וטרבזונספור, שתיים מיריבותיה הגדולות של בשיקטאש, הגיעו לעיר והצטרפו למחאה.

כשעה לפני תחילת המשחק הניף אוהד בשיקטאש דגל פלסטין לכיוון היציע שבו ישבו אוהדי הפועל באר שבע. המאבטחים התערבו ולקחו ממנו את הדגל, ובעקבות התקרית התפתחה מהומה בין האוהדים הטורקים לאנשי האבטחה. סרטונים שהופצו ברשתות החברתיות הציגו גם את התערבות המשטרה הגאורגית נגד אוהדים נוספים שניסו להניף דגלי פלסטין.

לפי הדיווחים, עימותים בין אוהדי בשיקטאש לכוחות הביטחון התפתחו גם מחוץ לאצטדיון. בסרטונים שהופצו ברשתות החברתיות נראו אוהדים מתעמתים עם שוטרים, ובתיעודים נוספים ובדיווחים שעלו במהלך השידור נראו כיסאות מושלכים מהיציעים ואוהדים מפונים מהמקום על אלונקות. המתיחות החריפה במהלך המחצית הראשונה, עד לעצירת המשחק ולירידת השופטים והשחקנים לחדרי ההלבשה, בעוד הקהל ביציעים נקרא להירגע.

articles.title: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
articles.summary: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the U.S. tightens its push to keep AI chips out of China.
paragraphs: Nvidia is under pressure to do things differently, and a new WSJ report shows how far that’s going.

According to the Journal, Nvidia has told manufacturing partners, including Dell and Super Micro, to hit pause on server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia for an unspecified period as it assesses whether its regional partners are meeting U.S. export requirements.

As for why those countries, Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers there, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed — reportedly grudgingly — earlier this month. The Journal notes that the think tank Institute for Progress estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China’s AI computing power.

articles.title: Net migration to UK falls to lowest level since 1997 excluding pandemic
articles.summary: Latest figures show difference between number of people arriving and leaving UK was ⁠77,000 in ​year ‌to ‌June Analysis: How much of the fall in UK immigration is due to Labour’s policies? Net migration across the UK has fallen to its lowest level since 1997 with the exclusion of the years of the Covid pandemic. Figures released by the Office for National Statistics and the Home Office show that the difference between people arriving and leaving the UK was ⁠77,000 in ⁠the ​year ‌to ‌June ‌2026. Continue reading...
paragraphs: Net migration across the UK has fallen to its lowest level since 1997 with the exclusion of the years of the Covid pandemic.
Figures released by the Office for National Statistics and the Home Office show that the difference between people arriving and leaving the UK was ⁠77,000 in ⁠the ​year ‌to ‌June ‌2026.
The ONS figures cover the year ending June 2026, down from an estimated 171,000 in 2025 and a peak of 944,000 in 2023. Annual net migration to the UK in 1997 was 48,000.

UK net migration is also for the first time in the “tens of thousands” since that target was set but never fulfilled by David Cameron’s government in 2010. An estimated 738,000 people immigrated to the UK in the year to June while 661,000 emigrated, according to the data published on Thursday.

The 62% fall over the past 12 months – from 204,000 in the year ending June 2025 – results from lower immigration. Net migration has fallen more than 90% since the peak of 944,000 in the year ending March 2023.
Immigration fell by 17% over the year to June 2026, driven by fewer non-EU citizens being granted permission to work, study, bring family members to the UK or apply for asylum.

Keir Starmer’s policies last year made care workers and some mid-skilled jobs ineligible for work visas, suspended family reunion for refugees and toughened restrictions for universities sponsoring international students.
Emigration remained relatively high but fell by 4% (-28,000) compared with the year ending June 2025.

Most people leaving the UK to live in another country were non-citizens who previously migrated for work or study, including those who moved to the UK as part of the “Boriswave” from 2021 onwards when immigration was unusually high.

Reacting to the figures, the home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, said Labour’s policies should be credited for the drop. It will be seen as a boost to Andy Burnham’s plans to keep hold of “red wall” seats in any future general election.

“The Conservatives lost control of our borders. Year upon year, they promised they would bring net migration down to the tens of thousands. Instead, they let it reach close to a million a year, overseeing four decades worth of migration in their last four years alone.
“This government has restored control. Where they failed, we have delivered for the British people,” she said.
Burnham said of the figures: “I think we are finally, as a country, getting into the position that the public has long wanted to see.”

Asked about the UK’s future relationship with the EU and whether freedom of movement should be up for discussion, he said the Channel crossings crisis “arose significantly in the post-Brexit years when we lost that ability to collaborate with our European partners, and we’ve had to work hard to catch up again … So, no, I don’t think you can say that Brexit did anything other than weaken control of immigration in this country.”
The drop has been driven by policies pushed through by Labour and Conservative governments.

Home Office visa data from January to June 2026 shows visa grants to international students fell by 38% (-39,200) and grants to skilled workers including those in the health and care sector and their dependants also dropped by 38% (-26,300) compared with the same period in 2025.
The end of social care visas has caused numbers to fall from 108,000 at their peak to just 1,400 last year.

Migration remains a key political issue, with Labour’s 2024 manifesto promising to reduce net migration, and aiming to “smash the gangs” involved in irregular migration and bringing asylum seekers across the Channel in small boats.

Burnham’s arrival in No 10 has signalled a shift in the way the government views legal migration. Some Labour insiders say that policy is now being driven by economic demands rather than a fear of the rise of Nigel Farage’s Reform UK, which has suffered a dip in the polls.

The Conservatives claimed their policies under Rishi Sunak’s administration were responsible for the drop, including restrictions on family members that could be brought over by care workers and changes stopping dependants moving to the UK with international students.

Chris Philp, the shadow home secretary, said: “The fall in net migration is mainly a result of changes made by the previous Conservative government. We now need to go even further with a legally binding annual cap, set by parliament, at a far lower level.”
Ben Brindle, a senior researcher at the Migration Observatory at the University of Oxford, said net migration could drop even further next year, and may have a “fiscal cost”.
“We are entering an unusual period where immigration has come down and may still have further to fall.

“Falling net migration is not automatically a problem for the UK economy, especially in the long run. Falling asylum migration is expected to benefit public finances. On the other hand, the number of migrants on skilled work visas has fallen even more over the past year, and that is expected to have a fiscal cost,” he said.

Sunder Katwala, the director of the British Future thinktank, said the figures “will come as a surprise to most of the public” who still tended to believe that immigration was rising. “It must now be time for the political and media debate to catch up and start a new phase of the debate about what happens next,” he said.

Other data published by the Home Office showed the number of asylum seekers living in hotels was at the lowest level since records began in 2022, but there was a 9% rise of those in “dispersal” accommodation – privately managed houses, flats or rooms in properties of multiple occupancy. There has been a drop in the number of new asylum applicants and Channel crossings are down 39% year on year, with 23,983 people having arrived in the UK in small boats in 2026.

articles.title: Is Alice Huang a spy or not?
articles.summary: The central, still-unproven claim in the Nvidia scandal is that Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed exec with whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair, is a Chinese spy.
paragraphs: The central, still-unproven claim in the Nvidia scandal is that Alice Huang, a former executive at the data-center company Megaspeed, is a Chinese spy. She had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who abruptly resigned on Nov. 12 after acknowledging it and was just as abruptly reinstated on Monday of this week.

What’s publicly known is murkier than the headlines suggest. U.S. intelligence has reportedly tracked Alice Huang’s contact with an officer of China’s spy agency, but officials haven’t offered public evidence that she was commissioned to target Nvidia’s chief. In the past week, after President Trump successfully pushed to bring Jensen Huang back, the administration has played down the allegations it once circulated internally. Whether that reflects new intelligence or political pressure is the big question.

Undisputed reporting shows the claim emerged from the White House itself. It first appeared in a highly classified memo written in March under the oversight of Secretary of State Marco Rubio and circulated to White House officials ahead of Trump’s trip to China in May. The memo formed the partial basis for the New York Times’ initial reporting on the scandal, published Oct. 29 and its existence was first reported on Nov. 8.

The memo did not definitively say, according to the Wall Street Journal, that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. CNN, by contrast, has reported that the memo concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset.

What’s better established is that Alice Huang was in touch with Chinese intelligence. The Ministry of State Security (MSS) is Beijing’s civilian spy agency, responsible for both foreign intelligence and domestic counterintelligence. Last weekend, the Times, citing people with knowledge of U.S. intelligence reports, reported that Huang was in contact with an MSS officer from the spring of 2025 until this fall, a period that overlaps her relationship with Jensen Huang. (The Chinese government has called the spy claims a “smear,” and Megaspeed says Huang left the company in August 2025 and that its business is legitimate.)
Top Trump officials have nonetheless all but discredited the espionage claims, along with the suggestion that Nvidia fell prey to spying or foreign influence.

Attorney General Todd Blanche, who was Trump’s personal defense lawyer before taking over the Justice Department, told journalists on Tuesday: “I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.” On the same day, Trump said a pardon was an option for Jensen Huang but that he did not think one would be needed. Senior intelligence officials reportedly told Congress that the government apparently has no actual evidence that the MSS directed Alice Huang to pursue an affair with Jensen Huang.

None of those statements necessarily exonerates Alice Huang as an intelligence agent. Instead, they support the alternate theory that the Chinese government didn’t tell her to begin the affair and that Jensen Huang broke no law by having it. Not being directed to have an affair isn’t the same as not being a spy, though.

From a certain angle, the circumstantial evidence surrounding Alice Huang looks quite suspicious. She was a top executive at a company investigated for illicitly channeling Nvidia chips to China, and her husband, Kang Wei, is said to have even closer ties to the MSS, with some sources saying he worked for the agency.

The timing of the government’s reversal is at the heart of the matter. Trump has said he lobbied the board “directly and indirectly” to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, so it wouldn’t be surprising if officials who serve at his pleasure were recasting the case in terms that satisfy his agenda. That wouldn’t necessarily make their assessments wrong. But unless new intelligence has actually resolved the question, and none has been publicly identified as yet, that backdrop is critical to keep in mind. CBS has also reported that Rubio, whose office oversaw the original memo, has privately voiced concerns about aspects of Jensen Huang’s return.

Doubts persist elsewhere, too. Earlier this month, CNN reported that the intelligence community was still working to understand Alice Huang’s relationship with Jensen Huang and that the intelligence collected on her to date does not prove she was acting as a spy for Beijing. After a briefing by top intelligence officials earlier this month, Rep. Jim Himes (D-Conn.), the incoming chair of the House Intelligence Committee, said he was unsure whether she was a spy or a “useful idiot.” And this week, the Wall Street Journal pointed out that under Chinese leader Xi Jinping, top corporate executives routinely maintain ties to the country’s intelligence service without being formally deputized as assets.

The crush of conflicting claims, most from anonymous government sources, obviously leaves large questions unanswered as to what actually transpired. Some of those questions that naturally spring to mind:

Alice Huang is said to have been under U.S. surveillance for over a year. If the government suspected her of espionage, why wasn’t Jensen Huang warned earlier (and privately, so as not to cause the stock-market-destabilizing maelstrom that followed the more recent disclosure)? One explanation that has been given is that alerting the Nvidia chief might have tipped off Huang that her cover had been blown.
If Alice Huang was a spy, what information did she pass to the Chinese government, and what influence did she actually have?

Most critically, how did the allegation reach the public at all? The likeliest answer is a leak. A source told CNN that Rubio briefed Trump on the intelligence in May, yet Trump has since said he only recently learned of the concerns, and in October he presented Jensen Huang with the National Medal of Science. Officials who felt they could not get through to the president may have turned to reporters instead, which would explain how the contents of a memo whose existence has never been disputed found their way into print. What remains unclear is who leaked it, and whether they anticipated the fallout.

There are answers to all of these questions, of course, but when the public will get them is anybody’s guess. Jensen Huang is due to appear before the Senate Banking Committee next week, and by the look from the statements of some of its members, he’s likely in for a rough ride. Unfortunately, congressional hearings, particularly public ones, rarely unearth secrets that haven’t already been disclosed.
