Lenders - including some of the UK's biggest banks and specialist motor finance firms - have already set aside billions of pounds for potential payouts.
The body that represents the lending industry, the Finance and Leasing Association, said it had "concerns" about the central programme but that it was choosing not to raise a legal challenge.
Santander, Barclays and Lloyds also accepted the scheme, despite raising concerns that the level of redress is disproportionate to those who suffered harm.
Even if drivers are entitled to compensation from these lenders they will need to wait.
There were some concessions made to lenders in a scaled-down final compensation plan from the FCA.
The Supreme Court considered three test cases which influenced the FCA's decision and, ultimately, limited how broad the compensation programme could have been.

It focused on whether the car dealers had a duty to act on behalf of their customers, rather than in their own interests. The test case which was upheld was that of Marcus Johnson, who bought his first car - a Suzuki Swift - in 2017.

In his case, the Supreme Court said the terms of his finance deal were unfair due of the size of the commission payment, and the fact he appeared to have been misled over the relationship between the finance firm and the dealer.

articles.title: Musk's plan to send a million SpaceX data satellites into space approved
articles.summary: The Starmind constellation aims to be the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for AI computing power.
paragraphs: Image source, Getty Images
US regulators have given SpaceX the go-ahead to launch a million satellites into Earth's orbit to help build data centres in space - the first approval of its kind.
The company, which is owned by Elon Musk, wants to use sunlight to power satellites that will process data for AI and send the results back to Earth.
The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Wednesday that the project, known as Starmind, would "support America's booming super intelligence economy".

However, rival firm Amazon has criticised it as a "lofty ambition rather than a real plan", while astronomers in the US said the move would "significantly undermine" the public's ability to study and observe the night sky.
There is increasing opposition to data centres on earth, including in the US where experts say they were a factor in the Republicans big losses in the midterm elections.

SpaceX believes the "orbital data centres" are the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) computing power that is beyond "terrestrial capabilities".
FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement that the project "opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth".
"This is the kind of American ingenuity that can unite our strengths in space and advanced technology, reinforce our economic leadership, and expand prosperity here at home," Carr said.
Responding to the announcement, Musk wrote on X: "Much appreciated. This will be a great asset to America and the world."
Under the FCC licence, deployment of the satellites must begin no later than November 2033. SpaceX will be required to have deployed 10% by November 2035, rising to 50% by November 2038.
The company has already said it wants to launch its first Starmind satellite next year.
It is unclear whether a million satellites will indeed be launched or whether SpaceX has sought approval for a higher number than it will use.

Like SpaceX's current Starlink network, which provides high-speed internet via more than 10,000 satellites, Starmind's satellites will operate in low-Earth orbit at altitudes ranging between 500-2,000km (310-1,242 miles).
Starmind's satellites will communicate with Starlink's and then relay the data to Earth.

Speaking to the Today programme, on BBC Radio 4, Prof Sir Martin Sweeting, founder and executive chairman of Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd, said while the idea of data centres in space seemed "technically feasible", whether it "makes sense at scale yet" still needed to be analysed.
Being able to get the data from the network of satellites, he added, would depend on being able to use laser links from the ground to them.
"That has not yet been perfected to the level at which it would be able to support the huge amounts of data that are likely to be transferred backwards and forwards," he said.
Meanwhile, the American Astronomical Society (AAS) said it was "disheartened and dismayed" by the decision.

It said the proposed constellation would "significantly undermine decades of federal investment in astronomical facilities" as well as "the ability of astronomers and the public to enjoy and study the night sky".

It noted that the constellation "involves larger (and therefore brighter) and more numerous objects", meaning the satellites would "be visible as extremely bright objects for longer periods in the night sky".

Jan Hasselman, a senior attorney at the non-profit group Earthjustice, said in a statement: "Drastically expanding satellites in space has a direct impact on people's everyday lives as well as the future of our planet."

The orbiting data centre concept is also being explored by other firms - including Google and Blue Origin - and is being pitched as a greener alternative to traditional centres, which require enormous amounts of power to run and water for cooling.
The ever-expanding use of AI computing has seen a massive increase in the amount of data that needs to be stored and processed around the world.

New facilities continue to be built but it is becoming difficult to find places to put them. Data centres are large and sprawling, use enormous amounts of power and water for cooling, and increasingly local people don't want them built nearby.

An expert previously told the BBC that launching hardware into orbit remains expensive and that the infrastructure to protect, cool and power them can be complex - while a growing quantity of space debris puts the physical hardware at risk.
Separately, another cautioned that the growing number of low-orbit craft increases the possibility of crashes between objects - which could damage machines or send materials falling back to earth.
Starlink has been accused of creating congestion in space, something Musk denies. He has also rejected claims his satellites have been taking up too much room and crowding out competitors.

articles.title: Watch: Alaskan flying team airdrops Thanksgiving turkeys to remote communities
articles.summary: For the last few years, the "turkey bombers" have taken to the skies for the benefit of residents in off-grid communities.
paragraphs: For the last few years, "turkey bombers" Esther Keim and Heidi Hastings have taken to the skies to airdrop Thanksgiving turkeys to residents in off-grid communities in south-central Alaska.
Hastings pilots the plane while her best friend Keim drops the turkeys out the plane window, delivering to families who may not otherwise get one of the birds, since they are cut off by snow and ice.

articles.title: UK tells 100,000 military reservists to prepare for war amid Russia threats in first since Cold War
articles.summary: Britain's Defense Ministry has contacted approximately 100,000 military reservists for the first time since the Cold War, amid growing security concerns over Russia and NATO's defense capabilities.
paragraphs: Britain's Ministry of Defense (MoD) has contacted approximately 100,000 military reservists, urging them to prepare for a potential wartime call-up amid growing security threats from Russia, The Telegraph first reported on Thursday.

British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting confirmed the initiative on Thursday during an interview with Sky News, describing the measures as a necessary precaution given the increasingly challenging security environment facing Britain and its NATO allies.

The letters, reportedly the first of their kind since the Cold War, were sent to former personnel across the British Army, Royal Navy, and Royal Air Force (RAF). Reservists were asked to update their contact information and provide details regarding their current employment and professional skills.
The correspondence also offered veterans opportunities to volunteer for military training and exercises, including NATO's flagship Steadfast Defender exercise scheduled for spring 2027.
The initiative follows Streeting's warning in October that Britain must be ready for war by 2030, citing Russia's growing military capabilities and intensifying hybrid warfare against NATO members.
Britain strengthens military readiness amid Russian threats

The initiative is intended to improve the UK's ability to mobilize former military personnel in an emergency, allowing defense officials to assess the experience and qualifications veterans have acquired since leaving active service.
Britain's regular army currently comprises approximately 73,000 active personnel, increasing the importance of its strategic reserve in strengthening national defense capabilities.

The move comes less than a week after Russia violated Polish airspace with what Polish authorities identified as suspected missiles and a drone, amid military exercises involving Ukraine's European allies.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham condemned the incursion, while Poland called for additional NATO support to strengthen the alliance's eastern flank.
UK seeks to strengthen deterrence while avoiding escalation

Despite Britain's efforts to increase military preparedness, Streeting has previously expressed support for establishing additional military communication channels with Russia to reduce the risk of miscalculation and unintended escalation.

Earlier this month, Britain also announced plans to invest £90 million in drones, sensors, and artificial intelligence systems to counter Russian underwater threats and protect critical infrastructure in the North Atlantic.
The developments come as NATO allies assess Washington's review of US troop deployments in Europe, amid concerns over potential gaps in the continent's defense capabilities.
British officials emphasized that the letters do not constitute an immediate mobilization order, but rather form part of broader efforts to strengthen military preparedness and deterrence.
“People should find it reassuring rather than alarming,” Streeting told Sky News on Thursday.

articles.title: Nearly a decade of legal drama: the key milestones in Netanyahu's corruption trial
articles.summary: From his first police interrogation in 2017 to failed plea bargain talks, a presidential pardon request and the judges' latest push to end proceedings, a timeline of the unprecedented criminal case against Israel's longest-serving prime minister
paragraphs: From his first police interrogation in 2017 to failed plea bargain talks, a presidential pardon request and the judges' latest push to end proceedings, a timeline of the unprecedented criminal case against Israel's longest-serving prime minister

Nearly a decade after police first questioned Benjamin Netanyahu in a corruption investigation and seven years after he was indicted, the legal proceedings against the prime minister remain unresolved.

In an unusual hearing Wednesday that lasted just 10 minutes, the judges overseeing Netanyahu's trial recommended that Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara reconsider the continuation of the proceedings, citing difficulties in securing convictions in two of the three cases and suggesting that an agreement could be reached in the third.
Benjamin Netanyahu in court
(Photo: Yonatan Sindel/Flash90)

Netanyahu, the first sitting Israeli prime minister to face criminal charges, has consistently denied wrongdoing. He faces charges of bribery, fraud and breach of trust in three separate cases involving luxury gifts from wealthy businessmen and alleged attempts to secure favorable media coverage in exchange for political or regulatory benefits.
Here is a timeline of the major developments in Netanyahu's corruption trial, from his first police questioning to the latest intervention by the judges.

Police questioned Netanyahu for approximately three hours at the prime minister's official residence in Jerusalem on suspicion of receiving improper benefits in investigations known as Case 1000 and Case 2000.

Following the questioning, then-attorney general Avichai Mandelblit issued a special statement explaining that preliminary suspicions had emerged approximately three months earlier and that police had since worked extensively to substantiate them.
“Over the past month, evidence was collected that changed the evidentiary situation in this matter,” Mandelblit said.

Ari Harow, Netanyahu's former chief of staff, signed a cooperation agreement with prosecutors. Harow had recorded conversations between Netanyahu and Arnon “Noni” Mozes, publisher of the daily Yedioth Ahronoth, that became central to Case 2000.

Under the agreement, Harow would provide testimony against Netanyahu, be convicted of fraud and breach of trust in a separate criminal case, pay a fine of 700,000 shekels and perform six months of community service instead of serving a prison sentence.
Police said the agreement had been approved by Mandelblit and then-state attorney Shai Nitzan.
Police informed Netanyahu that they were recommending he be charged with bribery, fraud and breach of trust in Cases 1000 and 2000.
Investigators also recommended charging Israeli billionaire and Hollywood producer Arnon Milchan with giving a bribe and Mozes with offering a bribe.

Case 1000 centered on Netanyahu's relationships with Milchan and Australian billionaire James Packer, including allegations that the prime minister and his family received expensive gifts from the businessmen.

Case 2000 concerned discussions between Netanyahu and Mozes over potentially curbing the growth of Israel Hayom, a free daily newspaper that competed with Yedioth Ahronoth, through legislation and other measures in exchange for more favorable coverage of Netanyahu.

Police described the investigations as complex and extensive, conducted by the national fraud investigation unit of Lahav 433, Israel's elite police investigative division, under the close supervision of the state attorney and attorney general.
Police went public with their investigation into Case 4000, arresting several senior officials and Netanyahu associates.

Among those arrested were Shaul Elovitch, the controlling shareholder of telecommunications giant Bezeq; Communications Ministry Director General Shlomo Filber; and Nir Hefetz, a former adviser and spokesman for Netanyahu and his wife, Sara.

Case 4000, widely regarded as the most serious of the three investigations, centered on allegations that Netanyahu advanced regulatory decisions benefiting Bezeq in exchange for favorable coverage on Walla, a major news website controlled by Elovitch.
Filber, who had been suspended from his position at the Communications Ministry, signed a cooperation agreement guaranteeing that he would not serve prison time.
“Someone was operating above my head,” Filber said at the time. “I didn't know this was what was happening behind my back regarding favorable coverage on Walla.”
Filber maintained that he had received no personal benefits and that the regulatory decisions he had made could be debated on their professional merits. “I was manipulated,” he said.
Hefetz signed a cooperation agreement in Case 4000, becoming the third former Netanyahu associate to turn state's witness.

Under the agreement, Hefetz received full immunity from prosecution, ensuring that he would neither serve prison time nor pay a fine. He agreed to provide police with text messages and give investigators a comprehensive account of the information in his possession without that testimony being used to incriminate him.
On March 2, Netanyahu was questioned as a suspect in Case 4000 for the first time. Police and Israel Securities Authority investigators questioned him for approximately five hours.

Meanwhile, Sara Netanyahu arrived at Lahav 433 headquarters in the central city of Lod to provide testimony in the Bezeq investigation. Her questioning subsequently became a formal interrogation as a suspect.

Police and the Israel Securities Authority announced that they had completed their investigation into Case 4000 and had gathered sufficient evidence to recommend charging Netanyahu with bribery, fraud and breach of trust.
Mandelblit informed Netanyahu's attorneys of the charges he intended to bring against the prime minister, subject to a pre-indictment hearing.
Under Israeli law, suspects facing serious criminal charges generally have an opportunity to present arguments to prosecutors before a final decision is made on whether to indict them.
The announcement came more than two years after Netanyahu was first questioned as a suspect.
Following the pre-indictment hearing, Mandelblit announced his final decision to prosecute Netanyahu in all three cases:
Case 1000 (the gifts affair): Fraud and breach of trust over allegations that Netanyahu received luxury gifts, including cigars and champagne, from wealthy businessmen.
Case 2000 (the Netanyahu-Mozes affair): Fraud and breach of trust over discussions concerning favorable media coverage in exchange for measures that could weaken a competing newspaper.
Case 4000 (the Bezeq-Walla affair): Bribery, fraud and breach of trust over alleged regulatory benefits for Bezeq in exchange for favorable coverage on Walla.
In a special statement delivered at the Justice Ministry, Mandelblit described the decision as a difficult moment for Israel.

“This is a difficult and sad day,” he said. “A day on which the attorney general decides to indict a sitting prime minister for serious offenses is a difficult and sad day for the Israeli public and for me personally.”
Netanyahu appeared before the Jerusalem District Court as his corruption trial formally opened, becoming the first serving Israeli prime minister to stand trial on criminal charges.
The proceedings were assigned to a three-judge panel consisting of Presiding Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman and Judges Moshe Bar-Am and Oded Shaham.
Unlike criminal trials in the United States, Israeli criminal proceedings are conducted without juries, leaving judges responsible for determining both the facts of the case and the verdict.
Netanyahu appeared before the Jerusalem District Court and formally denied all the charges against him.
The other defendants, Shaul Elovitch, his wife, Iris Elovitch, and Mozes, also denied the charges against them.
Lead prosecutor Liat Ben-Ari delivered her opening statement, accusing Netanyahu of attempting to “trade” his governmental power for personal benefits.
The prosecution's first witness, former Walla CEO Ilan Yeshua, then began testifying.
Netanyahu left the courtroom following Ben-Ari's opening statement after the judges granted him permission to be absent during Yeshua's testimony.
Hefetz, Netanyahu's former spokesman, began testifying, initially focusing on Case 4000.

He claimed that Netanyahu devoted at least as much attention to media-related matters as he did to national security issues. According to Hefetz, media reports concerning Netanyahu's family could leave the prime minister unable to attend to his work for hours.

Hefetz also testified about Netanyahu's decision to replace Gilad Erdan as communications minister and assume the position himself. He claimed the decision followed consultations between Netanyahu and members of his family, including his son Yair.

Reports emerged that Netanyahu's defense attorneys and Mandelblit were conducting confidential negotiations in an attempt to reach a plea agreement. The talks ultimately failed to produce an agreement.
The Justice Ministry clarified at the time that Netanyahu had not formally approached Mandelblit with a request to enter negotiations and finalize the terms of a deal.
The discussions took place shortly before Mandelblit completed his six-year term as attorney general.
Filber began testifying in Case 4000, providing an account that contradicted key elements of the statements he had given police after signing his cooperation agreement.
Prosecutors asked the judges to declare Filber a hostile witness. The court rejected the request but allowed prosecutors to cross-examine him.

Netanyahu's defense attorneys also succeeded in undermining a central element of the prosecution's case concerning an alleged meeting during which Netanyahu purportedly instructed Filber to advance regulatory decisions benefiting Elovitch.
The alleged meeting was a key component of the prosecution's attempt to establish a connection between Netanyahu's actions as communications minister and favorable coverage on Walla.
Hadas Klein, Milchan's longtime personal assistant, began testifying in Case 1000.
During approximately six hours of testimony, Klein described the cigars supplied to Netanyahu and the champagne she said Sara Netanyahu had requested.
She also described how Sara Netanyahu would obtain gifts from Packer's residence in the affluent coastal town of Caesarea, where the Netanyahu family owns a private home.
“On more than one occasion, Sara entered Packer's house in Caesarea and took things herself,” Klein said. “It was routine.”
Baharav-Miara, who succeeded Mandelblit as attorney general in February 2022, informed Netanyahu's defense attorneys that she opposed criminal mediation in the case.
The possibility had been raised during discussions earlier that year over the scheduling of witnesses.
Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara
Jacques Chen, an attorney representing Elovitch in Case 4000, suggested mediation, and Judge Shaham encouraged the parties to examine the option.
Netanyahu's attorneys did not object, but Baharav-Miara's opposition effectively ended the initiative.
Criminal mediation is a procedure in which a judge who is not responsible for deciding the case helps prosecutors and defense attorneys explore the possibility of reaching a negotiated resolution.
The three judges overseeing Netanyahu's trial released, with the parties' consent, a brief summary of a closed-door discussion in which they had raised concerns about the bribery charge in Case 4000.
The judges said they had identified difficulties in substantiating the bribery allegations and recommended that prosecutors consider withdrawing the charge.
“In light of these difficulties, it was suggested that the state consider withdrawing the bribery offenses in this charge,” the judges said.
The panel also stressed the importance of bringing the proceedings to an end in the interests of both the case and the country.
However, the judges clarified that their remarks about the need to conclude the trial were unrelated to how it should end or what its outcome should be.
The recommendation did not amount to an acquittal or a formal ruling on the evidence, and prosecutors continued pursuing the charge.
Five years after he was indicted, Netanyahu appeared for his first day of testimony in his own defense.
Friedman-Feldman, Bar-Am and Shaham heard Netanyahu personally address the allegations against him for the first time.

The testimony was held in a fortified courtroom at the Tel Aviv District Court because of security considerations during the ongoing war, although the Jerusalem District Court panel continued to preside over the proceedings.
The request consisted of 14 pages, accompanied by appendices that included the indictment.

In a video statement announcing the move, Netanyahu argued that the prolonged proceedings were deepening divisions within Israeli society. “The continuation of the trial is tearing us apart from within,” he said.
Herzog subsequently proposed dialogue between the prosecution and defense, but Netanyahu did not respond to the proposal.
The request was unusual because Netanyahu sought a presidential pardon before his trial had concluded and without a conviction.
Approximately 18 months after taking the witness stand, Netanyahu completed his testimony in the fortified courtroom at the Tel Aviv District Court.

articles.title: Deadly fire erupts near Cairo killing dozens of people
articles.summary: At least 31 people have died in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo, after a fuel tanker overturned, says Egypt's health ministry.
paragraphs: Thirty-one people have been killed and 21 others injured after a large fire broke out on a busy highway in Cairo.
Footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched.
The fire occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, north of the old city centre. Egypt's health ministry said the injured were being treated at hospitals nearby.

Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported that a high-voltage cable fell in front of a fuel tanker, causing the driver to lose control and the tanker to overturn, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol.

articles.title: ה-FDA אישר וחברת שבבי המוח של אילון מאסק תתחיל ניסוי ראשון מסוגו
articles.summary: החזון של אילון מאסק (ושל אחרים לפניו) לשלוט במחשבים ולהזיז איברים בגוף בכוח המחשבה בלבד הולך והופך לאט לאט ממדע בדיוני למציאות. חברת Neuralink הודיעה אתמול (ד') שקיבלה אישור ממנהל המזון והתרופות האמריקאי, ה-FDA, להשיק את LINK, הניסוי הגדול הראשון שלה בארצות הברית. במסגרת הניסוי היא תבדוק את ה-BCI או ממשק המוח-מחשב שלה על מספר […]
paragraphs: החזון של אילון מאסק (ושל אחרים לפניו) לשלוט במחשבים ולהזיז איברים בגוף בכוח המחשבה בלבד הולך והופך לאט לאט ממדע בדיוני למציאות. חברת Neuralink הודיעה אתמול (ד') שקיבלה אישור ממנהל המזון והתרופות האמריקאי, ה-FDA, להשיק את LINK, הניסוי הגדול הראשון שלה בארצות הברית. במסגרת הניסוי היא תבדוק את ה-BCI או ממשק המוח-מחשב שלה על מספר מצומצם של נסיינים.

הניסוי החדש מיועד למספר מוגבל של מטופלים שסובלים משיתוק חמור בעקבות מחלת ה-ALS, מחלה ניוונית מתקדמת הפוגעת בתאי העצב השולטים בתנועת השרירים הרצוניים. "קיבלנו אישור FDA להשיק את LINK, הניסוי החשוב הראשון לממשק מוח-מחשב מושתל בארה"ב", כתבו ב-Neuralink בפוסט ברשת X. "הניסוי מתבסס על העבודה שלנו עם יותר מ-30 משתתפים בעלי שתל של Neuralink עד היום". אותם משתתפים, מניסויים מוקדמים שערכה נוירלינק בארצות הברית, קנדה ובריטניה, צברו יחד אלפי שעות שימוש בצ'יפ ובממשק בעולם האמיתי, שימוש שכלל בין היתר לימודים אקדמיים, משחקי וידאו ותקשורת עם קרובי משפחה וחברים. בפועל, איפשרה להם המערכת להמיר אותות מוחיים לשליטה מלאה בסמן העכבר ובמקלדת וירטואלית, מה שאפשר לאנשים משותקים להקליד עבודות אקדמאיות, לצייר, לשחק במשחקי מחשב ולנהל שיחות שוטפות עם בני משפחה וחברים – הכל בלי להזיז שריר.

איך זה קורה בפועל? המערכת של החברה כוללת את N1, שתל שמוחדר בניתוח לתוך הגולגולת. לאחר מכן נכנס לפעולה הרובוט הכירורגי R1, שמחדיר אלקטרודות גמישות ישירות למוח. התוכנה של החברה מפענחת אז את הפעילות העצבית שקשורה לתנועה ומתרגמת את האותות לפקודות דיגיטליות, כך שהמטופלים יכולים להפעיל מחשבים ומכשירים אחרים בלי מקלדת או עכבר.

היכולת הזו הודגמה כבר בשנה שעברה אצל ברדפורד סמית', חולה ה-ALS הראשון שהשתתף בבדיקה של החברה והצליח לתקשר באמצעות אותות מוחיים בלבד. "Neuralink נתנה לי חופש, תקווה ותקשורת מהירה יותר", אמר אז סמית'. "זה שיפר את החיים שלי כל כך. אני שמח להיות מעורב במשהו גדול שיעזור להרבה אנשים".

חשוב לשים לב שהאישור הנוכחי (בהמשך לאישור הראשון מ-2023) ניתן לבדיקות בלבד, כלומר עדיין לא מדובר באישור שיווק מסחרי, שמאפשר לרופאים לרכוש ולהשתיל את המכשיר לכל מטופל, אלא באור ירוק רגולטורי לגייס קבוצה מוגבלת של משתתפים ולבחון את הטכנולוגיה תחת פרוטוקול קליני מחמיר ומפוקח.

על פי החברה, המחקר ייערך במספר אתרים קליניים ויתמקד "בתוצאות פונקציונליות המשפרות עצמאות בחיי היומיום", לצד בחינת הבטיחות והאמינות של המערכת לטווח הארוך. ב-Neuralink לא פירטו כמה משתתפים יגויסו או מה תנאי הסף המדויקים להשתתפות בניסוי, אבל ההרשמה לניסוי פתוחה כבר כעת. אם המערכת תוכיח את עצמה כבטוחה ומן הסתם יעילה גם תחת הפרוטוקול הקליני המחמיר של ה-FDA, הדרך לניסויים מתקדמים יותר בקנה מידה רחב יותר, ובהמשך לאישור שיווק מסחרי – תהיה קרובה מתמיד.

articles.title: Shufersal to launch new chain as profit falls
articles.summary: Alongside the results, Shufersal co-CEO Shlomi Amir announced the launch of the Hyper Neto discount warehouse supermarket chain.
paragraphs: Alongside the results, Shufersal co-CEO Shlomi Amir announced the launch of the Hyper Neto discount warehouse supermarket chain.
Israeli supermarket chain Shufersal (TASE: SAE) today reported lower revenue and profit for the third quarter of 2026 and announced it would be launching a new chain.

Net profit in the third quarter fell 14.5% to NIS 130 million, from NIS 152 million in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue fell 4.6% to NIS 3.55 billion, from NIS 3.72 billion in the corresponding quarter of 2025.

The company said retail revenue fell mainly because online sales declined after a change to its distribution operations reduced service availability for some customers, and because wholesale revenue fell. Shufersal also attributed the decline to an increase in Israelis travelling abroad and the days of the week on which the holidays fell. According to Central Bureau of Statistics figures cited by the company, Israelis travelling abroad rose 21% from the corresponding period.
Shufersal to launch new chain

Alongside the results, Shufersal co-CEO Shlomi Amir announced the launch of the Hyper Neto discount warehouse supermarket chain. The chain will begin with 20 stores through a combination of conversions and new openings. The first store will open in Kiryat Motzkin in the coming weeks. The company said the format would take a new approach to marketing and merchandising and offer a wide range of products, including in its fresh food departments.

In its online business, the group reported that it had completed an overhaul of its delivery operations, from order-picking sites to customers’ homes. It also upgraded its website and app, changing how customers navigate them, tailoring offers to customers and expanding its range of products and categories.

The group continues to upgrade stores and fresh food departments, open new stores, convert existing ones and close loss-making locations. It also reported importing meat directly from South America and expanding its imports of non-food products. Shufersal’s loyalty club has about 2.4 million members.

The group said its real estate arm, LARO, signed a land-for-development deal with Tidhar involving a 5,600 square meter plot that LARO owns in Jerusalem’s Talpiot neighborhood. The group also announced that construction had begun on a shopping center in the Ramot neighborhood of Beersheva. These developments follow a tender win to build a retail, employment and tourism complex in Ramat Negev, the acquisition of the remaining rights in the Kordani complex in Kiryat Motzkin and the acquisition of commercial rights in a project in Havatzelet Hasharon in Netanya.
Published by Globes, Israel business news - en.globes.co.il - on November 26, 2026.

articles.title: Two screenings of Pakistani TV show cancelled in India after backlash
articles.summary: The show, Dar-e-Nijaat, has become a sensation in India but is now embroiled in a political row.
paragraphs: Until Wednesday, the weekend plans of some television enthusiasts in the Indian city of Bengaluru involved dressing up, having an elaborate dinner and finding out what happens next in the lives of a wildly popular fictional Pakistani couple.
Then geopolitics intervened.

Two private screenings of Dar-e-Nijaat (Door to Salvation), a Pakistani television drama that has become something of a sensation on Indian social media, were called off after an online backlash and police scrutiny.
The serial, which airs on Pakistan's ARY Digital, is available to Indian viewers through some YouTube channels, though the broadcaster's official channel is blocked in India.

The controversy comes amid a renewed appetite for Pakistani entertainment in India, even though cultural engagement remains a sensitive issue following a brief but intense military confrontation between the two nuclear-armed neighbours in May last year.
A similar gathering in Delhi, featuring quizzes and even a virtual interaction with the show's director, had already divided opinion online last week.

In Bengaluru, one screening, scheduled for Saturday at a restaurant, offered a Persian and Arabic dinner alongside two episodes of the serial for a small ticket charge. The other - scheduled at a private theatre and meant only for family members - asked guests to dress in their "best Pakistani ensemble".
As promotional posters circulated online, several social media users questioned the appropriateness of such gatherings and called for police intervention. Both events have since been called off.
The backlash has coincided with calls to block the release of another Pakistani drama in India.

The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi demanding that Netflix's upcoming Pakistani series, Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo (Gather whatever is left), be barred from release in India.
Featuring Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan, Sanam Saeed and other stars with many Indian fans, the series is Pakistan's first Netflix original. Its global premiere is scheduled for 4 December.

In its letter to Modi on Tuesday, the AICWA argued that releasing the series in India would disregard the sentiments of families affected by terrorism. India has long accused Pakistan of supporting cross-border terrorism, an allegation Islamabad denies.
The association has also sought permanent legislation prohibiting Pakistani entertainment content in India. Netflix is yet to clarify whether the series will be available to Indian subscribers.
The developments have revived an old debate in India over whether cultural ties with Pakistan should be kept separate from political differences.
India and Pakistan share a rich cultural heritage, but relations between them have often been fraught since they were carved out of British India as independent nations in 1947.

And cultural exchanges have often been among the first casualties of political tensions. Pakistani ghazal singers with devoted audiences in India have periodically found themselves unable to perform there. Indian films, immensely popular in Pakistan, have disappeared from its cinemas. Artistic collaborations have flourished during periods of relative calm, only to unravel when tensions flare again.

The early 2010s were a particularly fertile period. Pakistani singers Atif Aslam and Rahat Fateh Ali Khan were among the most recognisable voices in Hindi cinema. The launch of the television channel Zindagi in 2014 brought Pakistani serials into Indian living rooms, introducing viewers to stories whose language and emotional worlds were familiar, but whose treatment of everyday life often felt refreshingly different.

By 2016, Fawad Khan was appearing in some of Bollywood's most prominent productions. But attacks on Indian security forces in Uri that year and in Pulwama in 2019, both of which India blamed on Pakistan-based militant groups, narrowed the space for cultural collaboration. Pakistan - which has constantly denied any involvement - also imposed restrictions on Indian entertainment.
Even as formal exchanges dwindled, Pakistani dramas found new audiences in India on YouTube, while music continued to travel across the border through streaming platforms.
But the events of last year disrupted even this relatively informal relationship.

On 22 April 2025, militants killed 26 people, most of them tourists, in Pahalgam in Indian-administered Kashmir. India blamed Pakistan-linked militants; Islamabad denied involvement. In May, India launched military strikes on what it described as terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-administered Kashmir. Four days of fighting followed before a ceasefire was announced.
Amid widespread anger in India, the government asked streaming platforms to discontinue Pakistani-origin content, while social media accounts of several Pakistani celebrities were blocked.

Fawad Khan's much-anticipated return to Hindi cinema with Abir Gulaal was thwarted when the film was denied permission for release in India. Criticism of India's military action by Pakistani artistes fuelled further anger.

For much of the past year, Indian audiences have encountered Pakistan on screen largely through the prism of national security. In December, millions flocked to watch Dhurandhar, Aditya Dhar's espionage thriller, whose success inspired a fascination with the gangsters, spies and political intrigues of Karachi.
But in recent months, a more familiar kind of fascination with Pakistan has begun to resurface.
Pakistani songs like Alfaaz have become hugely popular on Indian social media, while Dar-e-Nijaat, a story about marriage, heartbreak and domestic life, has found an enthusiastic audience.

Written by the celebrated Urdu novelist Umera Ahmed, the serial revolves around the marriage of Zaryab (Durefishan Saleem), a young woman recovering from a romantic betrayal, and Abu Bakar (Sheheryar Munawar), a deeply religious man.

Though the drama explores questions of faith and redemption, it is Abu Bakar's tenderness towards his wife that has earned him perhaps the highest accolade in the contemporary vocabulary of courtship: a "green flag".
It was this enthusiasm for the drama that prompted the organiser of one of the screenings in Bengaluru to plan an event at a private theatre in her apartment complex.
What she had envisaged as a small family gathering, she said, had been interpreted quite differently once the invitation found its way onto X.
"My family was saying why should we cancel?" she said. But ultimately, she decided to call it off.

articles.title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk
articles.summary: The discount chain has fallen into administration after its owners failed to find a buyer.
paragraphs: Poundland has collapsed into administration, putting 11,000 jobs at risk, after its owners failed to find a buyer to keep it in business.

The retailer's shops and distribution centres will remain open and continue to trade during the administration process with the business likely to be broken up and some of its stores sold off to rival retailers.
Poundland's US owners held talks with several bidders over a last-minute rescue deal, but no agreement was reached.
Poundland boss Barry Williams said in a note to staff that the board had "no alternative but to take this decision", but was making it with "sincere sadness and intense regret".

He said the US owners Gordon Brothers had removed "all borrowing facilities and access to our bank accounts" on 27 October, and adequate funds had not been released since then to keep the business solvent.
"Under these circumstances, it is impossible for the board of directors to see how Poundland can continue to operate as a going concern," he added.

Bally Auluk, national officer at the union Usdaw, which represents Poundland workers, told the BBC'S Wake Up to Money programme that Gordon Brothers' "intention was perfectly clear from the offset... to force the company into administration".
"It's such a devastating blow any time of year, but most certainly in the run up to Christmas for 11,000 colleagues, most of whom are our members," he said.
Gordon Brothers rejected Auluk's characterisation of the process and said it had "explored every avenue to secure a sale of the whole company".

Kelvin Blake, 62, who has worked for the firm for 25 years, and whose partner has been there 29 years, said he was feeling "down, depressed", and because of his age, feared he would not find a job elsewhere.
"We didn't want it, but it's come so now we've just got to face it and see what the future holds.
"My income's gone," he added. "Obviously, we'll be working until we're told to leave."
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Poundland was "part of the fabric of high streets and communities up and down the country".
He said the news of it going into administration just weeks before Christmas would be "deeply concerning for workers and their families".

He added: "While it is worrying, going into administration does give other potential buyers the opportunity to engage and we will work hard with all the relevant parties to ensure the best possible outcome."
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said protecting staff is the government's top priority.

"I'm also very mindful that for lots of people across the country, Poundland is a place they go on the high street to get bargains and... given the cost of living challenges we face, that is of concern to us in government," he told the BBC.
Alix Partners, which has been appointed as administrator, said it would look at all options for the business, "including sales of the business and its assets, either in whole or part".
"We appreciate this is a deeply concerning time for all involved - customers, suppliers and, in particular, Poundland colleagues," they said.

Gordon Brothers has been criticised over how it handled a potential sale of Poundland, with accusations the investment firm hoped to profit from selling off the chain's 600 shops and stock piecemeal after running it into the ground.
Gordon Brothers, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, has denied such claims.
On the funding question, Gordon Brothers said it had loaned the firm £85m over a year to help save it from insolvency.
But insiders critical of the US firm have said it stands to make its loans back and more from the insolvency process.
Previously, Gordon Brothers netted millions from liquidating the stock of fashion retailer LK Bennett, and in insolvency fees.

Labour MP Liam Byrne told the BBC the House of Commons' Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee will recall Gordon Brothers before Parliament - two weeks after Gordon Brothers representatives last appeared at the committee to answer questions about Poundland, and where MPs said they were "deeply concerned" about the business.
Byrne said: "I am really worried that a 'greed is good' approach to business by its owners has forced [Poundland] into an administration."
He added the committee wants to know "how much money they're ripping out and crucially, how do we make sure, as a country, that we don't have this kind of scenario unfold again".

Poundland's co-founder Steve Smith said the administration "should not be happening". He told the BBC the chain has undergone a turnaround since being taken over by Gordon Brothers, returning to profitability.
He said: "Everybody was behind Poundland. It had turned round. And with buyers on the table, why was it put into administration?"
"It should not have happened," he added.
Gordon Brothers met Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds on Monday to update him on the process.

The firm said on Wednesday that, despite the Poundland management bringing about a turnaround over the past year, the firm was "still vulnerable" to inflation and any downturn in sales or profit margin, and it had faced "several years of instability".
A spokesperson added the firm's "thoughts are with Poundland colleagues".
It said it had stepped in to take over the retailer in 2025 when it was struggling, and when "no-one else was willing to finance the business".
One of the central stumbling blocks in negotiations to keep the business afloat was a shareholder loan Gordon Brothers inherited when it bought the business for less than £1 last year.
Gordon Brothers was owed £22.5m of that loan, while the previous owner Pepco was owed £7.5m.
Gordon Brothers rejected various offers to buy the business as a going concern with deals to pay off that loan.
Irish firm Martin Property Group offered to pay off £5m of the loan up front, and defer the rest of the payments to 2030.
London-based Xyra group offered £12.5m up front but ran out of time to get a deal over the line.
German investment firm Zachert Private Equity is also understood to have made a late offer.
All of these were rejected.
The crisis at Poundland really came to a head over the past few weeks after Gordon Brothers restricted access to funds for day-to-day operations.
This meant that stock at the retailer was not being replenished at the necessary pace in the vital run-up to the festive period.

articles.title: Eisenkot denies reported talks with Palestinian Authority over Gaza's future; Ramallah does not
articles.summary: Representatives of Eisenkot and Mahmoud Abbas reportedly discussing postwar arrangements in Gaza; Eisenkot's party dismisses the report as an outright lie, while a senior Palestinian official signals openness to renewed dialogue
paragraphs: Representatives of Eisenkot and Mahmoud Abbas reportedly discussing postwar arrangements in Gaza; Eisenkot's party dismisses the report as an outright lie, while a senior Palestinian official signals openness to renewed dialogue

Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar! party who has been tasked with forming the next government, denied Thursday a report that his representatives were holding talks with officials representing Palestinian Authority Chairman Mahmoud Abbas over the future of the Gaza Strip.

An unidentified source told Sky News Arabia that contacts were underway between representatives of Eisenkot and Abbas, focusing on postwar arrangements in Gaza. According to the report, Abbas' representatives made clear that any arrangements for the territory must be made through the Palestinian Authority, without sidelining it.
Gadi Eisenkot, Palestinian Authority Chairman Mahmoud Abbas
(Photo: REUTERS/Mohammed Torokman)
The source also claimed that Eisenkot considers the U.S. peace plan the most realistic path toward disarming Hamas.

Eisenkot swiftly denied the report, saying no such contacts had ever taken place. “In recent hours, a false report has been circulating about contacts and discussions between representatives of the Yashar! chairman and Palestinian Authority officials,” his party said in a statement. “To remove any doubt: This is an outright lie.”
However, a senior Palestinian official in Ramallah told ynet that the Palestinian Authority was not denying the existence of contacts with Eisenkot's representatives.

“The Palestinian leadership has always extended its hand in partnership, seeking peace, easing tensions and preventing hatred, but Netanyahu and his right-wing government chose violence and killing,” the official said. “We hope the new Israeli government will recognize the dangers of perpetuating the conflict and extend its hand in peace.”
Following the announcement of Israel's election results, Abbas publicly signaled his willingness to resume negotiations with Israel.
Abbas and Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides

During a visit to Cyprus last month, Abbas expressed hope in a meeting with Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides that the formation of a new Israeli government would allow the two sides to return to the negotiating table.

“For many years, we have extended our hand to the Israeli side to achieve peace so that Israel and Palestine can live in security, stability and peace,” Abbas said. “We hope that immediately after a new Israeli government is formed, we can begin a dialogue together.”

Abbas also asked Cyprus to help mediate between the two sides, saying its good relations with both Israel and the Palestinians could enable it to play a significant role. Christodoulides expressed willingness to help promote regional stability.

Despite Abbas' overtures, Eisenkot, like Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, opposes the establishment of a Palestinian state. However, the former IDF chief favors a different approach toward the Palestinian Authority and has called for action against Israeli settler violence in the West Bank.

articles.title: Greece receives shipment of Israeli munitions
articles.summary: Greece has received its first shipment of air-to-ground munitions from Israel, including Spice bombs and Rampage missiles, senior officials told the Greek media.
paragraphs: Greece has received its first shipment of air-to-ground munitions from Israel, including Spice bombs and Rampage missiles, senior officials told the Greek media.

Greece has received its first shipment of air-to-ground munitions from Israel, including the Spice bombs and Rampage missiles. This was confirmed by senior officials in Athens to Greek media. This offensive enhancement for the Hellenic Air Force’s F-16 fleet is not being well-received in Turkey, especially as it accompanies strategic deals in air defense and artillery.

The agreement for the procurement of Spice 1000 and Spice 2000 guidance bombs, as well as Rampage missiles, was signed in 2022. The delivery of these munitions marks the final stage of its integration into the Greek military. The Spice 1000 is manufactured by Rafael Advanced Defense Systems as part of the Spice series of bombs, which consists of guidance kits for air-to-ground munitions, designed for three types of bombs of varying weights.

The Spice 1000 weighs 450 kilograms and has a range of 100 kilometers, while the Spice 2000 weighs 900 kilograms and has a range of 60 kilometers. The entire system, also developed by Rafael, was awarded the Israel Defense Prize, owing to its unique capability. Spice allows munitions that were originally unguided, such as the MK 83 and MK 84, to navigate and home in on a target autonomously, without relying on GPS. This is achieved via an electro-optical seeker head, which utilizes an innovative mathematical algorithm to compare the target image against the system's real-time visual input, resulting in an accuracy of less than three meters.

The "Greek City Times" reported that senior officials in the Hellenic Air Force have also expressed interest in procuring the Spice 250, which weighs 75 kilograms, and has a range of 100 kilometers with the 250ER variant extending that range to150 kilometers.

The Rampage, developed jointly by Elbit Systems, Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI), and Tomer, is integrated into various Israeli Air Force aircraft and designed to strike targets from a range of 150-250 kilometers. The primary advantage of conducting strikes from such distances is the combination of high precision (with a margin of error of only about three meters) and a reduced risk to combat pilots operating in enemy airspace.

In the context of Greece, should a conflict with Turkey arise, these missiles could be launched from Greek territory against targets in Turkey. Greek reports highlight this as a critical factor given Turkey’s diverse air defense network, which includes the Russian S-400 system for high-altitude defense, as well as domestically produced systems, such as the Hisar and Siper, for lower-altitude coverage.

Both Spice and Rampage share a key feature: their electro-optical capabilities render them immune to GPS jamming. In the case of the Rampage, its supersonic speed, launch range of 150-250 kilometers (depending on the aircraft's altitude), and the fact that an F-16 can carry four such missiles simultaneously make it extremely difficult to intercept. This capability has already been demonstrated by Israel in Iran.
Israel signs biggest-ever defense deal with Greece

The Greeks also do not hesitate to highlight their capabilities and recently, took advantage of their Ministry of Defence’s Security Forces Day to showcase the Spice and Rampage munitions. Greece is also significantly upgrading its F-16 fleet. Earlier this month, it received its 63rd aircraft of the advanced Viper variant, with the remainder of the order expected to arrive from the US by the end of 2027.

The delivery of air-to-ground munitions follows strategic agreements between Israel and Greece with signs that further deals are in the pipeline. About three months ago, Greece procured three air defense systems from Israel, Spyder, Barak MX, and David’s Sling, for €3.1 billion, as part of the strategic Achilles' Shield deal. In April, Greece finalized a €650 million agreement with Elbit Systems for the procurement of PULS artillery systems.

Earlier this week, Greek news outlet "Kathimerini" reported that Greece and Israel are in talks on additional deals worth €1 billion. These discussions cover electronic warfare systems, long-range missiles, and the expansion of the combat aircraft training center established by Elbit in Kalamata three years ago. Furthermore, according to "Kathimerini," Greek officials are continuing talks with IAI on procurement of LORA missiles, which have a range of 400 kilometers.
Published by Globes, Israel business news - en.globes.co.il - on November 26, 2026.
Rampage missile credit: Elbit Systems

articles.title: המחקר המפתיע שמגלה למה לפעמים שווה לשלם למתחרים כדי שיגידו את האמת
articles.summary: חברות מתחרות עשויות להרוויח משיתוף במידע ביניהן, אך הפרדוקס הוא שלכל אחת מהן עשוי להשתלם לשקר • מחקר חדש מראה כיצד שילוב של בלוקצ'יין ותמריץ כספי הופך את אמירת האמת למשתלמת, ולמה לעיתים אפילו שווה לממן את השתתפות המתחרה במנגנון
paragraphs: מדור "הפקולטה" הוא שיתוף פעולה מערכתי ייחודי בין גלובס והפקולטה לניהול באוניברסיטת תל אביב שנועד להנגיש, בשפה בהירה ותמציתית, ידע מחקרי ואקדמי בנושאי כלכלה, אסטרטגיה, שיווק, ביג דאטה, פינטק וחדשנות. הפקולטה לניהול ע"ש קולר של אוניברסיטת ת"א היא מבתי הספר המובילים בעולם למנהל עסקים, וחוקריה עוסקים בסוגיות העדכניות ביותר בענף. במדור יכתבו מיטב חוקרי הפקולטה לניהול לצד בחירת הנושאים, העריכה והתמצות של מערכת גלובס.

פרופ' יבגני ליאנדרס הוא חבר סגל בפקולטה לניהול ע"ש קולר באוניברסיטת תל אביב. מחקריו מתמקדים ביחסי הגומלין בין האסטרטגיה הפיננסית לאסטרטגיה התפעולית של חברות, ובהשפעת התחרות בשוקי המוצרים על החלטות פיננסיות שונות של חברות
בעולם העסקי, מידע הוא משאב חשוב. חברות משקיעות במחקרי שוק ובחיזוי ביקושים משום שהחלטות על ייצור, מלאי והשקעות מתקבלות בתנאי אי־ודאות. אבל מידע יכול לשמש גם להשפעה על המתחרים.

דמיינו שתי חברות המתחרות בשוק מוצרי החשמל. לקראת עונת המכירות הן צריכות להחליט כמה לייצר: יותר מדי, והן עלולות להיתקע עם מלאי יקר; מעט מדי, והן עלולות להחמיץ מכירות. לכל אחת מהן יש מידע חלקי על הביקוש הצפוי, המבוסס על הזמנות מוקדמות, נתוני מכירות והערכות שוק. לכאורה שיתוף במידע יועיל לשתיהן ויאפשר לקבל החלטות טובות יותר ולשפר את הרווחיות.

● הפקולטה | המספרים משתפרים, אבל האם הארגון באמת מצליח? המבחן של המנהלים ● הפקולטה | אל תבנו על ה-AI: שלושת הדברים שמאפשרים לעובדים לפתור בעיות בצורה יצירתית● הפקולטה | משאירים 15% טיפ כמו כולם? המחקר שמראה למה זאת בעיה

אבל מה אם אחת מהן תדווח דיווח לא אמין במטרה להשפיע על החלטות המתחרה? למשל, לגרום לה לצמצם את הייצור כדי להקטין תחרות. כך נוצר פרדוקס: שתי החברות יכולות להרוויח משיתוף פעולה, אבל לכל אחת מהן עשוי להשתלם לשקר.

מחקר חדש שערכתי, באמצעות מודל כלכלי הבוחן את התנהגותן של שתי חברות מתחרות, מראה כיצד ניתן להפוך את אמירת האמת למשתלמת יותר מהטעיה באמצעות מנגנון מבוסס בלוקצ'יין. המסקנה מפתיעה: במקרים מסוימים, לחברה עשוי להשתלם לממן את השתתפות המתחרה במנגנון שיתוף המידע.

כששתי החברות מבינות שקיים תמריץ להטעות, גם מידע אמיתי הופך לחשוד ושיתוף הפעולה עלול להתפרק. טכנולוגיית הבלוקצ'יין, המוכרת מעולם המטבעות הדיגיטליים, מאפשרת לתעד מידע באופן שקשה מאוד לשנות בדיעבד. אלא שהטכנולוגיה אינה יכולה להבטיח שהמידע היה נכון מלכתחילה.

לכן המחקר מציע לשלב מנגנון כלכלי: כל חברה המוסרת מידע נדרשת להפקיד בטוחה כספית. אם מתברר, בהתאם למנגנון הבדיקה, שהדיווח היה שגוי, היא תאבד את הבטוחה. ההסדר מופעל באמצעות "חוזה חכם" - תוכנה שמבצעת באופן אוטומטי פעולות שנקבעו מראש כשמתקיימים תנאים מוגדרים.
במקום לבקש מהחברות להתנהג בהגינות, יוצרים עבורן תמריץ כלכלי לעשות זאת. אם הסיכון הכספי הצפוי מאובדן הבטוחה גבוה מהרווח האפשרי ממסירת מידע מטעה, הדיווח השקרי כבר אינו משתלם.
המחקר מראה שגובה הבטוחה הנדרשת תלוי במידת אי־הוודאות בשוק, בדיוק המידע ובעוצמת התחרות. ככל שהרווח האפשרי מהטעיית המתחרה גדול יותר, כך עשויה להידרש בטוחה גבוהה יותר.

אחד הממצאים המפתיעים ביותר הוא שלעיתים משתלם לחברה לממן את הבטוחה של המתחרה. נניח למשל שהשתתפות המתחרה צפויה, הודות למידע שבידיה, להגדיל את הרווח של חברה גדולה ורווחית בשני מיליון שקל, בעוד שלמתחרה הקטנה חסרים 500 אלף שקל להפקדת הבטוחה. מימון הסכום החסר עשוי להיות החלטה עסקית רווחית, ולא מחווה של נדיבות.
זו דוגמה למצב שבו תחרות ושיתוף פעולה מתקיימים במקביל. החברות ממשיכות להתחרות על הלקוחות, אך יש להן אינטרס משותף ליצור מנגנון לחילופי מידע אמינים.
ומה עם הלקוחות?

אבל המחקר מצביע גם על צד פחות נוח. כשחברות מתחרות מקבלות מידע טוב יותר על הביקוש, הן יכולות להתאים את הייצור באופן מדויק יותר. לפי המודל, הדבר עשוי להוביל לעליית מחירים ולפגיעה בצרכנים, גם כשהיעילות הכלכלית הכוללת משתפרת. למשל, חברות עשויות להימנע מייצור עודף שהיה מפעיל לחץ להורדת מחירים. התוצאה עשויה להיות רווחים גבוהים יותר לחברות, אך מחירים פחות נוחים ללקוחות.
המחקר מראה, שבמסגרת המודל העלייה ברווחי החברות גדולה מהפגיעה בצרכנים, ולכן הרווחה הכלכלית הכוללת עולה. אבל העובדה שהמשק כולו עשוי להרוויח אינה אומרת שכל המשתתפים מרוויחים באותה מידה.
לכן שיתוף מידע בין מתחרים מעלה גם שאלות רגולטוריות. רשויות התחרות צריכות לבחון לא רק אם שיתוף הפעולה משפר את יעילות החברות, אלא גם כיצד הוא משפיע על המחירים, התחרות והצרכנים.

המסקנה המרכזית של המחקר חורגת מעבר לבלוקצ'יין. ארגונים נוטים לחשוב שכדי לשפר שיתוף פעולה צריך לפתח מערכת טכנולוגית מתקדמת. אבל גם המערכת הטובה ביותר לא תצליח אם למשתתפים אין אינטרס להשתמש בה באופן אמין.
לכן, לפני שמנהלים משקיעים בפלטפורמות לשיתוף מידע, כדאי לשאול: האם כל המשתתפים מרוויחים מהשיתוף? האם יש להם תמריץ למסור מידע אמין? והאם הם מסוגלים לעמוד בעלויות ההשתתפות?
פרופ' יבגני ליאנדרס / צילום: פרטי
בסופו של דבר, אמון אינו חייב להישען רק על יחסים טובים. אפשר ליצור מנגנון שבו גם מי שאינם סומכים זה על זה מוצאים שכדאי להם לומר אמת.
וכאן נסגר הפרדוקס שבו פתחנו: בעולם העסקי, המתחרה אינו בהכרח רק מי שממנו צריך להיזהר. לפעמים הוא מחזיק במידע שיכול לעזור לנו לקבל החלטות טובות יותר, עד כדי כך שמשתלם לנו לשלם כדי שגם הוא יוכל להשתתף.

לתשומת לבכם: מערכת גלובס חותרת לשיח מגוון, ענייני ומכבד בהתאם ל קוד האתי המופיע בדו"ח האמון לפיו אנו פועלים. ביטויי אלימות, גזענות, הסתה או כל שיח בלתי הולם אחר מסוננים בצורה אוטומטית ולא יפורסמו באתר.

articles.title: Guinea orders residents to clean up the capital months after deadly rubbish dump collapse
articles.summary: The capital's main rubbish dump has been closed since the disaster, leading to rubbish piling up in the streets.
paragraphs: Guinea has ordered residents to do a mass clean-up of the capital, Conakry, months after a rubbish landfill collapsed, killing dozens of people.
Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah on Wednesday announced a deadline of 31 December to clear rubbish in the city and its suburbs, which has seen an increase in illegal dumping in recent months.
In August heavy rains caused a landslide at the capital's main waste dump, with the rubbish collapsing onto homes killing 31 people and injuring others.
The site in the city's Dar es Salaam area was subsequently closed permanently, which has led to piles of rubbish accumulating outside homes and on the streets.
At a public forum on sanitation, Sanitation Minister Aboubacar Camara said Conakry was generating about 3,000 tonnes of waste every day.
He said much of the garbage was ending up in the streets because of weaknesses in the collection system.
The prime minister called on local authorities to become more involved in organising waste collection, saying this could become a way to create jobs.
"The state will do its part, but the municipalities must also organise themselves to ensure waste collection and provide jobs for young people," the prime minister said.
"Conakry must be completely clean by the end of December," he added, relaying a directive from the country's president, Mamady Doumbouya.
He cited measures the government was taking to improve waste collection and recycling, including a national sanitation fund that would guarantee financing for the sector.

Camara said talks had been finalised with a waste collection operator, with a plan for equipment to move waste from transit and sorting centres to a new disposal site in Baretodé, outside the capital.
The August tragedy at the Dar es Salaam landfill was not the first - 10 people were killed at the same site in 2017.
The government had ordered people living close to the site to move, but many residents chose to stay.
According to the prime minister, the government now plans to transform the closed waste site into an urban park.

articles.title: הפריצה הגדולה ל-1Password: כל מה שאתם צריכים לדעת (ולעשות)
