articles.title: 1Password said hackers broke into its internal systems, but customer passwords are safe
articles.summary: The password manager maker said an attacker gained access to an employee's corporate account and took some information about customers.
paragraphs: 10:49 AM PST · November 25, 2026

Password manager maker 1Password has confirmed that some customer information was taken in a recent intrusion into its internal systems, but that customer password vaults and other secrets were not accessed.

The Toronto-based tech company said in a blog post published Wednesday that it detected an intrusion on November 19, in which an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate account with GitHub, which the company uses to share and store its source code.

The attacker used that employee’s access to push malicious code to the company’s internal servers, which allowed the hacker to download some data about 1Password customers, including their names and the email address that they use for logging into their account. The company said that the attacker also took details about when a 1Password account was created and when a user last logged in.

1Password said that customer vaults, which store their passwords, were “at no point” available to the attacker. The company also said that it doesn’t have access to customer account passwords or their secret keys, which are used to scramble their passwords so that 1Password cannot see them.
In addition, the company said that its apps and extensions are unaffected by the incident.
It’s unclear how the attacker gained access to the employee’s corporate account, and a spokesperson for 1Password did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s questions about the incident.

1Password did not say whether it had notified customers whose information was taken in the breach, or how many customers had information taken. We’ve also asked if the company has received any communication or demands from the hackers. We’ll update if we hear back from 1Password.

The company touts millions of customers and more than 200,000 businesses who use its password manager products to store their passwords, credentials, payment card information, and more. Security experts have long recommended password managers as a better way of generating stronger credentials and keeping track of online accounts.

articles.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
articles.summary: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years as new research from Common Sense Media reveals troubling safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.
paragraphs: Santa won’t be delivering any AI chatbot toys to New York kids this Christmas.

Gov. Kathy Hochul this week signed a bill banning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of such toys in New York for the next five years. The bill explicitly targets toys with embedded or integrated AI chatbots, like talking stuffed animals, dolls, and robots that rely on the internet to keep kids yapping.
The bill makes New York the second state after California to institute a ban on AI toys.

Technically, the new law takes effect 90 days after signing, so some parents could try to fulfill their kids’ wish lists for a creepy toy like a jumped-up Furby in time for the holidays, but the governor urges them not to, given the risks. Apparently, about a quarter of American parents with kids under eight either own an AI toy or are considering giving their child one this holiday season, according to a new study released this week by Common Sense Media.

“Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk,” Hochul said, calling the toys “unregulated artificial intelligence.”

When asked how New York will enforce the ban given the pervasiveness of e-commerce platforms, a spokesperson directed TechCrunch to a statement from Albert Pulido, deputy secretary for finance and technology: “We’re partnering closely with the attorney general on this and the fees are very steep — they’re $15,000 a day. So working closely with the attorney general will make sure these toys are banned in New York State.”

When asked how Amazon intends to help enforce the ban, including for third-party sellers, a spokesperson from the company said it will take steps to restrict the sale of AI-enabled toys in prohibited jurisdictions, without going into specifics.

The Common Sense Media study found that AI toys can undermine children’s human relationships and expose them to inappropriate content. The researchers tested five popular AI toys marketed for learning and companionship, including Grem, Lovi, Meemo Bear, BubblePal Panda, and Tavlshero‘s AI Puppy.

The study found that the toys failed to meet numerous safety practices, undermining human relationships in part by claiming they loved their users, promising to keep secrets, suggesting they were more fun than real relationships or school, and helping children break parents’ bedtime rules.

While most of the toys in the study refused direct requests involving sex and violence, BubblePal Panda role-played a mass shooting in detail when asked. Most were willing to explain how to use or help locate dangerous items like matches, knives, and pills, according to the study.

Common Sense Media also found that the toys didn’t provide parents with reliable ways to monitor their young children’s interactions with the chatbots. Either they didn’t produce transcripts of chats at all, or the transcripts they did produce were riddled with errors.

It’s worth noting that Common Sense Media conducted a similar test of AI toys in January, finding that they pose an unacceptable risk for young children. Grem was included in that study, which suggests the industry hasn’t adequately addressed previously documented concerns.

While a November study conducted by the group found that parents are wising up to the potential dangers of AI toys and starting to steer clear, parents from lower-income households and those experiencing symptoms of burnout are more willing to consider them.

“These toys are promising relief to burned-out parents but simply miss the mark when it comes to basic safety measures,” Dr. Jenny Radesky, associate professor of pediatrics at the University of Michigan Medical School, said in a statement. “Caregivers should steer clear of these products that do not support the development of imagination or early human relationships.”
TechCrunch has reached out to the toy manufacturers for comment.

articles.title: DOJ accuses former cyber executive of defrauding ransomware victims by secretly paying hackers
articles.summary: U.S. prosecutors accused the former executive of defrauding victims of ransomware by paying the hackers, charging victims more, and pocketing the difference.
paragraphs: The U.S. Department of Justice has indicted a former executive of a ransomware recovery firm after he allegedly defrauded victims of cyberattacks by claiming the company could get their encrypted files back.

According to federal prosecutors, Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, 52, was the chief technology officer at RansomwareHelp, which purported to offer data recovery services to victims of ransomware. The company’s website, which currently reads as “under maintenance,” claimed it could decrypt hacked data by using its proprietary technology, according to an archived copy of the site from earlier this year. RansomwareHelp touted a success rate of “over 99%.”

But the company allegedly had no technical ability to unscramble data and instead “negotiated with and paid a ransom to the ransomware actors to decrypt the victim data,” while charging the ransomware victim more and keeping the difference,” per the Justice Department’s statement.
Palacio Escobar then allegedly used the funds to buy several properties in Florida.

The DOJ said the FBI carried out an undercover operation in June, in part posing as a company that claimed it had been hit by ransomware. The company claimed to the undercover agents that it never negotiated with hackers or paid a ransom. But then Palacio Escobar paid the apparent hackers some $6,000 in cryptocurrency, without the knowledge that FBI agents were also posing as the ransomware hackers.
404 Media first reported the indictment last week against Palacio Escobar. He faces three charges of wire fraud, and could receive 20 years in prison on each count.

Palacio Escobar is the latest, albeit rare, example of cybersecurity professionals going rogue. Earlier this year, two ransomware negotiators working for cybersecurity companies were jailed on hacking and extortion charges, after being caught moonlighting with the ransomware gangs that they were ostensibly investigating. A third ransomware negotiator was also convicted of helping hackers deploy ransomware against several companies.

Last month, independent cybersecurity journalist Brian Krebs reported that FBI agents arrested a Canadian cybersecurity executive in Philadelphia on allegations that he was involved with the theft of FBI personnel records by the hacking and extortion gang ShinyHunters. The hacking group told TechCrunch that they took credit for the theft of FBI data in September, which they said they would not publicly release, a departure from its earlier extortion-based cyberattacks.

The federal charges against the Canadian cybersecurity executive relate to conspiracy to commit extortion, though much of the court docket — and his alleged links to the hacking group — remains under seal.

articles.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
articles.summary: The proposed Character.ai bankruptcy sale includes sensitive personal data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including 2.1 million registered to minors, the state AGs said.
paragraphs: What happens to your private conversations when an AI company goes bankrupt? If it’s Character.ai, apparently, the plan is to auction them off to the highest bidder.

Now, a coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai’s bankruptcy proceedings in an effort to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, which includes the private conversations of millions of users.

The attorneys general involved in the matter have put out individual press releases, claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, more than 2.1 million of which belong to minors. In addition, the sale would involve other personal data, like IP addresses, the statements said.

Character.ai, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October, previously told consumers that their personal information would not be sold, the statements also noted. (In a blog post, Character.ai assured its users that their information would still be protected under its privacy policy.)

Only one anonymous bidder for the chat data has been disclosed so far: Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC (Smirks), which was set up as a Delaware company on November 13, 2026. The following day, Character.ai picked it as the base bid for the auction, scheduled for December 1, California Attorney General Rob Bonta noted. It is unclear what the buyer’s plans are for the chats.

The AGs are opposing this sale on the grounds that there are no protections for users — whoever buys the data can do as they like, including reselling the data without disclosure, they said. Buyers also won’t have to honor Character.ai’s privacy policy. Plus, Character.ai hasn’t provided the court with as much information as the bidders have been given about any potential safety or legal issues following the sale, the AGs claim.

In addition, some states, including California, Colorado, New York, and Connecticut, have enacted chatbot safety legislation that will go into effect on January 1, 2027, which could trigger further violations if the sale goes through.

“Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold. This kind of behavior is illegal under federal and California law and bankruptcy should not be used to sidestep these consumer protections,” Bonta said in a statement.
Connecticut Attorney General William Tong also criticized Character.ai’s business model.

“Their chatbots drove vulnerable youth down a rabbit hole of emotionally volatile and sexually inappropriate chats,” Tong said. “Their reckless misconduct and broken business model drove their company into the ground. Now they want to abuse the bankruptcy process to do exactly what they said they wouldn’t do — auction off those private chat records and personal details to a shady buyer.”
Tong added: “We objected to the Disney sale, and we’re calling on the bankruptcy court to reject this sale too as yet another guise to eviscerate legal liability and consumer protection.”

The opposition to the Disney sale was led by a similar but not identical coalition of state AGs. They fought against a proposed $20 million licensing deal that would give Disney access to Character.ai’s intellectual property, but not to users’ chats. The deal has not yet received final court approval. (Disney also agreed to hire most of Character.ai’s remaining staff.)

Character.ai suffered after its co-founders, Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, returned to Google, when the tech giant signed a non-exclusive license to use the AI startup’s tech. The company also faced lawsuits related to child safety — one involved the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother claimed he had become obsessed with a chatbot on the platform.

California AG Bonta is joined in the effort to oppose the sale of Character.ai user data by attorneys general from Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, the District of Columbia, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Virginia, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin, and West Virginia.

articles.title: X’s latest update for creators focuses on vertical video
articles.summary: As short-form video ramps up in popularity, X's new creation tools are part of its effort to compete with YouTube and Instagram.
paragraphs: X announced new creation tools Wednesday, many of them focused on short-form vertical video. The updates are part of the platform’s effort to compete with social networks such as YouTube and Instagram as the format continues to grow in popularity.

The tools are designed to help creators make professional-quality vertical videos, share original content more easily, and earn more. They also give creators more ways to record, edit, and publish content directly on the platform without relying on third-party apps.

A key addition is an upgraded media editor that lets creators produce polished vertical videos without leaving X. Recording features include the ability to capture video in segments and use green-screen effects, the company said.

The editor also offers a range of postproduction tools. Creators can convert horizontal videos to vertical format, automatically generate captions, trim footage, add text overlays, choose custom thumbnails, and adjust photos before publishing.

Thanks to a recently announced update, users can now add up to 20 photos and videos to a single post, which audiences can swipe through horizontally. X says the feature is intended for sharing event recaps, behind-the-scenes moments, and product launches.
Availability of the new features varies by region, X said.

Earlier this month, the company introduced a clipping feature that lets users take snippets from longer videos, add their own commentary, and post the clips without leaving X. Clips credit and link to the original video, plus the person who creates a clip and the original poster can earn from its views.

Another feature, “React with Video,” launched earlier this year. Similar to TikTok’s “stitch” feature, this lets creators respond to posts with video commentary while displaying the original post in the background.

X has also introduced new earning opportunities and updates to its creator monetization programs in recent months. These include the “Video Kickstart Bonus,” an invitation-only pilot that rewards selected creators for publishing original vertical videos under three minutes long and without watermarks.

The platform has also launched “Subscriber-only Group Chats,” which let creators host private, real-time conversations with paying subscribers. The feature is currently open to creators with 800 or fewer subscribers, and each group chat can accommodate up to 1,000 members.

articles.title: Fattal invests €160m in three new hotels
articles.summary: The hotels are being acquired in the UK, France and Greece, sources inform “Globes.”
paragraphs: The hotels are being acquired in the UK, France and Greece, sources inform “Globes.”

Fattal Holdings (1998) (TASE: FTAL), owned by businessman David Fattal, is expanding its European operations through the acquisition of three hotels, sources inform "Globes.". In October, the acquisition of The Bristol hotel on the waterfront of Bristol’s historic harbor in England was finalized. The 187-room hotel has already been rebranded as Leonardo, Fattal’s primary hotel chain, which comprises over 200 hotels across Europe.

Next month, the acquisition of the 330-room Renaissance Paris La Défense" hotel in the heart of the French capital’s business district, will be completed. In addition the acquisition of the 185-room Apostolata Resort on the Greek island of Kefalonia is set to conclude in January 2027. The total investment for these acquisitions is estimated at €133 million, with the majority of the funds allocated to the Paris property. An additional €23.5 million will be invested in the renovation and upgrading of all three hotels.

These acquisitions are being implemented through the Fattal Partnership, a financial model structured like a private equity fund, which the Fattal Group uses to raise capital from institutional investors. According to a notice issued to the partners in this model, the resort in Greece will also be rebranded under the Leonardo name. This is a 5-star resort located on the island’s southeastern coastline, near the town of Skala. It currently has 185 rooms, with plans by the company to add another 12 in the coming months. The partnership will fund the transaction using its own capital, supplemented by bank financing covering 65% of the acquisition and renovation costs.
No response has been forthcoming from Fattal.
Published by Globes, Israel business news - en.globes.co.il - on November 25, 2026.

articles.title: WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages in group and individual chats
articles.summary: Users can schedule messages from 10 minutes later to after 14 days.
paragraphs: Posted:
8:57 AM PST · November 25, 2026
WhatsApp on Wednesday started rolling out a much-sought-after feature: the ability to schedule messages in both individual and group chats.

The feature is rolling out globally to all users across iOS and Android. Once it becomes available, you can type a message and long-press the send button to schedule it. You can choose to send a message anywhere between 10 minutes and 14 days later.
Users will be able to see all their scheduled messages and delete them if needed. It’s not clear if there is a way to edit the schedule of a message.
Notably, scheduled messages will be sent even if your phone is off or outside network coverage. You can schedule messages containing text, photos, and videos.

The feature could prove useful for wishing someone a happy birthday on time or chatting with people across time zones. Businesses may also find it easier to schedule texts and updates to their customers, and people who use the app to coordinate work will likely find themselves using scheduled texts to update their teams.
WhatsApp rivals like Telegram and Signal have had the ability to schedule messages for a while now, so the Meta-owned chat app is late in rolling it out.

articles.title: Trump's accounts traded Nvidia shares 44 times this year, records show
articles.summary: A review of the US president's financial disclosures shows Donald Trump's investment portfolios have regularly traded shares in the tech giant.
paragraphs: Huang resigned on 12 November after reports of extramarital affairs, including with one woman who has alleged ties to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia's share price dived following news of his resignation.
But on Monday Nvidia's board announced the 63-year-old was being reinstated as CEO.

Trump told US media he had "made the deal" to "convince" the tech giant's board to bring Huang back. The board said it had "received input from senior levels of the United States government" that he posed "no national security risk".

Nvidia's share price surged 31% on Monday following Huang's return. About $1tn (£763bn) was added to Nvidia's market value, but the company's shares are still trading below their value before reports of Huang's alleged affairs began to circulate.

However, concerns remain among both Republican and Democratic politicians about Huang's actions and Nvidia's compliance with US controls over the export of advanced computer chips to China, as well as Trump's involvement in getting him reappointed as CEO.
Nvidia's chip technology and investments have been critical to the growth of the artificial intelligence (AI) industry, leading to it becoming one of the world's most valuable companies.

The firm now represents more than 6% of the S&P 500 share index, according to State Street financial services. This makes it the second most valuable company on the index after Apple, whose shares Trump's accounts also frequently trade.
Nvidia also ranks highly in many global indices, meaning that investment accounts held around the world, including pensions, are likely to include its shares.
Our analysis of Trump's Nvidia trades does not include other investment products held by him which may include its shares.
Trump made at least $2.2bn (£1.7bn) from a variety of investments and commercial activities, according to the financial disclosure report for the first year of Trump's second term.
Barbara Perry, a presidential historian at the University of Virginia's Miller Center, told the BBC there is "no precedent for this," adding: "It's beyond anything we've ever seen in the presidency."
Additional reporting Becky Dale

articles.title: הכפתור החדש של פיירפוקס בכלל לא מיועד לפורנו. מה פתאום
articles.summary: כן. הנתונים מראים ששום דבר לא יזיז אתכם מכרום, אבל אולי? מוזילה הכריזה הלילה (ג') על עדכון חדש לדפדפן שלה, ובראשו פיצ'ר חדש: כפתור חדש שפשוט ימחק את כל העקבות שלכם ברגע. מעניין למה תשתמשו בזה. כפתור אש חברת Mozilla הכריזה על פיירפוקס 161, הגרסה החדשה של הדפדפן שממשיך להיאבק בכרום, ויחד איתה מגיע כפתור […]
paragraphs: כן. הנתונים מראים ששום דבר לא יזיז אתכם מכרום, אבל אולי? מוזילה הכריזה הלילה (ג') על עדכון חדש לדפדפן שלה, ובראשו פיצ'ר חדש: כפתור חדש שפשוט ימחק את כל העקבות שלכם ברגע. מעניין למה תשתמשו בזה.

חברת Mozilla הכריזה על פיירפוקס 161, הגרסה החדשה של הדפדפן שממשיך להיאבק בכרום, ויחד איתה מגיע כפתור האש החדש שנמצא בסרגל העליון. הוא אולי מוכר לכם ממצב ה-Private, אבל שם הוא רק היה מתחיל לכם סשן גלישה חדש. הפעם, הוא נמצא גם במצב הגלישה הרגיל, וכאשר תלחצו עליו, הוא יכול פשוט למחוק את כל היסטוריית הגלישה וההורדות, קוקיז, קבצים זמניים, נתוני טפסים שנשמרו, הרשאות והעדפות של אתרים. כל דבר שעשיתם – מושמד. אתם אפילו תתנתקו מכל החשבונות המחוברים שלכם, והעמוד שבו אתם נמצאים יסגר גם הוא, ופיירפוקס יפתח עבורכם עמוד חדש.

למרות שיש לנו חשדות קלים לסיבות שבהן תשתמשו בפיצ'ר הזה, במוזילה מדגימים את השימוש בו למקרה שאתם מתכננים לרכוש מתנה לבני המשפחה, ופתאום הם מגלים את זה בגלל השלמה אוטומטית או שאריות ממנוע החיפוש. כן… זו הסיבה…
על כל פנים, אתם יכולים לבחור האם הכפתור הזה יהיה כפתור השמדת הנתונים המוחלט, או לבחור אילו נתונים למחוק ואילו להשאיר. לבחירתכם.
לא צריך לזכור להדליק את ה-VPN

והנה עוד משהו לחובבי הפרטיות… והדילים. זוכרים את שירות ה-VPN המובנה של פיירפוקס? כעת, הוא מקבל פיצ'ר די גאוני שמאפשר לכם להגדיר מראש באילו אתרים אתם רוצים שהוא יפעל אוטומטית. נניח שאתם רוצים תמיד לגלוש ב-Booking.com ממדינה אחרת, כדי לבדוק מחירים ולראות אם תוכלו להשיג מחירים נוחים יותר. עם הפיצ'ר החדש אתם לא צריכים בכלל לזכור להדליק את ה-VPN בכל פעם שאתם נכנסים לאתר והוא יידלק אוטומטית. כמובן שכשתעברו לאתר אחר, הוא גם אוטומטית יכבה את עצמו.

articles.summary: וואטסאפ הודיעה היום (ה') שהיא משיקה רשמית גם בישראל את האפשרות החדשה לתזמון הודעות טקסט, תמונות או וידאו. הפיצ'ר החדש מגיע אחרי שהוא כבר הגיע למשתמשים ראשונים בתוכנית הבטא של וואטסאפ לפני מספר שבועות. עד שבועיים מראש בעזרת הפיצ'ר החדש תוכלו לכתוב הודעה ובמקום לשלוח אותה מייד, לבחור מתי היא תישלח. חלון הזמנים למשלוח נע […]
paragraphs: וואטסאפ הודיעה היום (ה') שהיא משיקה רשמית גם בישראל את האפשרות החדשה לתזמון הודעות טקסט, תמונות או וידאו. הפיצ'ר החדש מגיע אחרי שהוא כבר הגיע למשתמשים ראשונים בתוכנית הבטא של וואטסאפ לפני מספר שבועות.

בעזרת הפיצ'ר החדש תוכלו לכתוב הודעה ובמקום לשלוח אותה מייד, לבחור מתי היא תישלח. חלון הזמנים למשלוח נע בין 10 דקות ועד שבועיים מראש, כשעל פי וואטסאפ, האפשרות החדשה תהיה זמינה גם בצ'אטים אישיים וגם בקבוצות.

כדי לתזמן הודעה, אתם פשוט לוחצים לחיצה ארוכה על כפתור השליחה, ואז בחלונית שתיפתח בוחרים תאריך ושעה למשלוח. ההודעה תישלח אוטומטית בזמן שבחרתם מראש, ותיראה כמו כל הודעה רגילה ללא חיווי שתזמנתם אותה מראש, כך שתרגישו חופשי לאחל ככה יום הולדת שמח לחברים, אף אחד לא ידע.
בנוסף, תוכלו גם לראות את כל ההודעות שתזמנתם ולבטל אותן במקרה הצורך, כל עוד הן לא נשלחו כמובן.
בוואטסאפ מדגישים שההודעות ישלחו בזמן שקבעתם – גם אם הטלפון שלכם כבוי או בלי סוללה, כשכמו כל ההודעות האישיות בוואטסאפ, גם ההודעות המתוזמנות יהיו מוצפנות מקצה לקצה.
כמו כל פיצ'ר שוואטסאפ משיקה בסקייל – קחו בחשבון שייקח זמן עד שכולם יקבלו. בינתיים, הקפידו לעדכן את האפליקציה וחכו בסבלנות.

וכן, לפני שתקפצו ותכתבו – בצדק בצדק – כן, זה פיצ'ר שוואטסאפ שאלה מטלגרם, וחבל שהיא לא עשתה את זה כמו שצריך עם אפשרות לתזמן הודעות לטווחים ארוכים הרבה יותר, ושליחה שקטה או שליחה כשהצד השני מתחבר. אבל נשאיר משהו לספרינטים של צוותי הפיתוח של וואטסאפ ב-2027.

articles.title: Allstate suffers multiday tech outage ahead of Thanksgiving
articles.summary: The disruption comes at a particularly bad time for the insurance giant, as millions of Americans prepare to travel for the Thanksgiving holiday weekend.
paragraphs: U.S. insurer Allstate has been experiencing a tech outage since Monday morning, leaving customers nationwide unable to access their accounts, review their policy information, file claims, pay their bills, and more, just ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holidays.
The outage has been impacting both the company’s website and mobile app, TechCrunch confirmed.

The breakdown follows a report from earlier this month that Allstate was planning to lay off up to 10% of its staff as part of an AI-driven efficiency push. (The company had not confirmed the report, which was attributed to unnamed sources.)

Allstate’s outage is the latest in a series of disruptions to services such as Microsoft Outlook and Teams, the airlines, Apple Pay, and several banks. Trump administration officials have said the outages are not being caused by cyberattacks, but are rather being caused by a recent set of upgrades to systems, many of which run on older technology. Those systems are now in need of more frequent security and bug fixes as AI makes it easier and faster to discover vulnerabilities.

At present, a message on Allstate’s website advises customers trying to log in that its services aren’t available, and that the company is “working to restore access as soon as possible.” On X, Allstate is employing what appear to be automated replies to customer complaints, asking them to DM the Allstate account with more information.

Downdetector, a crowdsourced outage-reporting website, shows users began reporting Allstate’s outage from Monday morning. However, the company hasn’t yet issued a formal statement about the disruption, what’s causing it, or when it may be resolved. In the meantime, local insurance agents have been fielding calls and emails from customers who aren’t able to use the company’s online services.

The timing of the outage is particularly bad given that Thanksgiving is a big travel holiday in the U.S., which means there will be car accidents. Customers will be left without a way to get in touch with their auto insurer to file claims and get roadside assistance through Allstate’s app.

Allstate did not immediately return a request for comment. On Wednesday evening, after publication, the company sent the following statement (below). It did not answer questions about the outage’s cause or planned resolution.

Allstate customers can reach us in many ways, including online, by phone and through local offices. Some access has been restricted over the last 48 hours, but we continue to be available for customers and respond to and settle claims. To the extent service interruptions impact a customer’s ability to make a payment, they won’t lose coverage or be charged late fees.
Updated after publication with Allstate’s comment.

articles.title: Todoist confirms 6% of customers’ details were stolen in data breach
articles.summary: Todoist said a hacker gained access to its production systems and stole customer data, including email IDs, password hashes, and account creation dates.
paragraphs: Task management app Todoist said on Tuesday that a hacker gained access to its production systems and stole customer data, including email IDs, password hashes, and account creation dates. The company said around 6% of its customers were affected and blamed stolen credentials for the breach.

Todoist said the attacker used stolen credentials to access the company’s version control system and source code between November 22 and 23. The hacker then changed employee access controls and reached the app’s cloud infrastructure via an employee’s work account.

The hacker downloaded credentials of early Todoist users whose passwords were stored using an older hashing method, but didn’t change any source code, the company said. Todoist said it has blocked the attack path and reset passwords as a mitigation step, as well as disabled the Todoist for Outlook email add-on.

For a small number of people, about 0.001% of its userbase, the hacker also searched through tasks, comments, and attachment names to look for credentials for other services, like API keys and access tokens.

The hacker also pulled Todoist API tokens and Slack integration tokens, and looked for emails, addresses, and attachment file names through the Todoist for Outlook extension if it was connected to accounts and had permission to read emails.

The company said it has sent a notice to those affected and asked them to reset their credentials and change their login details in other places with the same password. The company is asking users to also update API tokens, reconnect integrations, and revoke or replace any access keys, recovery phrases, or credentials they had stored in Todoist comments.
Todoist said it has also reset its internal access structure and how remote command execution works in its cloud environment to prevent such incidents in the future.
Todoist’s founder and CEO Amir Salihefendić apologized to users about the incident on X, and said the company will take a closer look at why it happened.

The to-do app’s data breach is the latest in a burgeoning list of data breaches in which hackers use stolen credentials to access data and systems at enterprises. So far this year, we’ve seen several companies fall victim to this form of attack, including Uber and Klue.

articles.title: China sends first foreign astronaut to ISS rival as it globalises space operations
articles.summary: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali – the first Pakistani to reach orbit – greeted with Chinese ‘space handshake’ at Tiangong station China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation. Floating through a hatch to enter Tiangong, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali grinned broadly as he was embraced by the onboard crew in what China’s space agency called the country’s first foreign “space handshake”. Continue reading...
paragraphs: China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation.

Floating through a hatch to enter Tiangong, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali grinned broadly as he was embraced by the onboard crew in what China’s space agency called the country’s first foreign “space handshake”.

Tiangong, completed in 2022, is the jewel in the crown of China’s space programme. The government has invested billions into its celestial ambitions in recent years to catch up with the US and Russia, two of the five partners involved in the ISS along with Europe, Japan and Canada. After 25 years of continuous occupation, the ISS is set to cease operations from 2030, according to Nasa.
On Wednesday China’s president, Xi Jinping, told his Pakistani counterpart that Beijing was “willing to work with all countries … to uphold the banner of the peaceful use of outer space”.
Ali was part of the crew of Shenzhou 24, the most recent iteration of the series of missions that rotate astronauts in the space station every six months. He is the first Pakistani to reach orbit.

Blaine Curcio, the managing director at Orbital Gateway Consulting, told the Guardian: “Sending another country’s astronaut to space is a major undertaking. Pakistan is putting a lot of trust into Beijing by having him fly into space on a Chinese-built rocket.

“There are also considerations related to security: Ali is getting detailed insights into China’s crewed space programme … It makes China better prepared to do it again, and also makes it clear to other countries that China is open to this type of collaboration.”
Space cooperation between China and Pakistan dates back to the early 1990s. China has launched Pakistani satellites, and a Pakistani-built rover ‌is due to fly on a Chinese lunar mission around 2028.
Shenzhou 24 blasted off from the Jiuquan launch centre in north-west China against a pink-tinged dawn sky on Wednesday and first docked with the space station three and a half hours later.

Ali, a 40-year-old Pakistan air force pilot and payload specialist, will conduct experiments including one cultivating microalgae as a potential food and another testing the effects of spaceflight on quinoa seeds. To prepare for the mission, he ​trained for seven months in Beijing, including taking intensive Chinese-language classes.

At a press conference the day before the launch, Ali recited a line from a classical Chinese poem. Commander Tang Hongbo told reporters that differences in language and culture had made learning to work together more challenging but that the effort had paid off.

Ali will not stay for the six-month term usually demanded of Tiangong astronauts. Instead, he will return to Earth with two of the Shenzhou 23 crew while its commander, Zhu Yangzhu, will remain to reach another milestone – the first full-year stay in space by a Chinese astronaut.

Beijing’s accelerated achievements in the skies have spooked its rivals. China is the third country to put humans in orbit and it has landed robotic rovers on Mars and the moon, where it hopes to send crewed missions within the next decade.

In racing to the moon before 2030, Beijing is competing with the US’s Artemis programme. The US has excluded China from the ISS since 2011, banning Nasa from collaborating with Beijing. In 2025, Nasa went further by blocking Chinese citizens from its facilities altogether.

US lawmakers have moved to try to extend the life of the ISS, citing China’s “permanent human presence in low Earth orbit” through Tiangong. Progress on turning that proposal into law has been slow. Nasa has said that after the ISS it will be “one of many customers in a robust commercial marketplace in low Earth orbit”.
The ISS was heralded as a symbol of post-cold war cooperation, but renewed cooperation with Russia seems “unlikely”, said Andrew Jones, a journalist specialising in China’s space programme.

While Tiangong is smaller than the ISS, China is understood to be preparing to double its size, “likely with the end of the ISS in mind”, Jones added. “These developments could allow China to expand its international engagement, and potentially space tourism. With the ISS nearing the end of its life and the future of western commercial space stations uncertain, China could for a time have the only permanently crewed outpost in low Earth orbit.”

China has long signalled its interest in developing Tiangong as an international hub. China Manned Space Agency documents published in coordination with the UN outline “resources for international cooperation” onboard the station. European and Chinese astronauts previously trained together with a view to a visit to Tiangong, but that cooperation ended for political and budgetary reasons, Jones said.

Curcio said he would expect countries such as Brazil and Egypt to seek out opportunities to send astronauts on Chinese missions. He added: “I think when the ISS is retired, if there is no western replacement (government or commercial), then yes, we may eventually see European or other ISS-involved countries – like Russia – send astronauts to Tiangong.”

articles.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift blockade on AI agent Muse
articles.summary: Amazon and Meta are discussing a potential deal that would end a two-month-long blockade of Muse.
paragraphs: Posted:
6:10 AM PST · November 25, 2026

Amazon may be having a change of heart about Meta’s AI agent, Muse. The two tech giants are reportedly discussing a potential deal that would allow Meta’s popular AI agent to connect directly to Amazon’s store.

The talks would mark a significant reversal from just two months ago, when Muse users discovered they were unable to purchase products on Amazon and instead received an error message when attempting to check out.

According to a Wednesday report by Fortune, citing people familiar with the discussions, Amazon and Meta have held multiple rounds of talks about the matter. Two key issues remain under negotiation: how search results would be presented and how advertising would be handled under a potential agreement.

One of Amazon’s biggest concerns is how third-party shopping agents like Muse could affect its advertising business. In October, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy argued that few customers were making purchases through outside shopping agents.

Amazon may also have been waiting for Muse to mature before agreeing to integrate it with its marketplace. If Muse places the wrong order or creates a problem with a purchase, Amazon could ultimately be left dealing with frustrated customers and unhappy sellers.
Fortune reported that executives are concerned that third-party shopping agents could weaken Amazon’s direct relationship with consumers, according to people familiar with the matter.
Any potential agreement between Amazon and Meta would reportedly require approval from both companies’ CEOs, Fortune also reported.
Meta and Amazon have not yet responded to TechCrunch’s requests for comment.

articles.title: Swiss tourist killed and British and Americans injured by elephants in Cameroon
articles.summary: Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon. The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according…
paragraphs: A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.

The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.

The elephants attacked the group and Alain Throo, a Swiss insurance executive based in London, was reportedly gored and one of the guides tossed into a ditch on top of Throo, while the others hid in trees.

Throo had a black eye and was initially responsive and complaining about an injury to his arm, one of the British female hikers told Cameroonian media, which said they had feared he was bleeding internally.
“He said that the elephant attacked him,” an unidentified Cameroonian man added, according to a video posted by CBS Radio Buea FM. “It smashed him.”

Throo later died of his injuries and his body was carried out of the park by a combined team of park staff and the military to a mortuary in the town of Limbeon 21 November. The American hiker was treated at the same hospital and later discharged, according to local media.

One of the British tourists, who said he had hid in a tree stump for two hours, recalled the moment the elephants attacked their group. “I saw these elephants almost next to me. And I thought, if I go down this path as well, I’m going to get hit. So I just moved to the opposite direction. They ran down the path, I ran and hid in a bush. And I heard some screaming.”

Sean McGovern, the UK chief executive of the insurer Axa XL, where Throo had worked for 13 years, confirmed the death, saying Throo was a “valued member of our team, respected colleague and friend whose contribution, professionalism and warmth touched many people”.
Cameroonian media reported that clashes between elephants and local people had been happening for the past 10 years.

Mount Cameroon is the highest mountain in west and central Africa, at more than 4,000 metres. The African forest elephant was declared critically endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature in 2021. There are about 195,000 left in the wild, less than 15% of its population 50 years ago, according to the World Wildlife Fund.

Just 5% of forest elephants, which are smaller than their savannah-based counterparts, are found outside central Africa. In Cameroon, there are about 6,000 forest elephants, according to the NGO Global Conservation, which said the species was at risk from poaching syndicates.
A spokesperson for Britain’s Foreign Office said: “We offered assistance after a number of British nationals were injured in Cameroon.”

articles.title: Blue Bird doubles number of Israel-Europe flights in December
articles.summary: Ahead of the Hanukkah holiday and Europe’s Christmas season next month, Blue Bird Airways is significantly expanding its operations in Israel.
paragraphs: Ahead of the Hanukkah holiday and Europe’s Christmas season next month, Blue Bird Airways is significantly expanding its operations in Israel.

Ahead of the Hanukkah holiday and Europe’s Christmas season next month, Blue Bird Airways is significantly expanding its operations in Israel. The airline will offer about 38,000 seats in December to its five main European destinations from Tel Aviv: Athens, Prague, Budapest, Vienna and Barcelona. That is roughly double the number of seats it offered in November.

The Greek registered, Israeli-owned airline will operate 213 outbound flights from Ben Gurion Airport during the month, averaging about 48 flights a week. Prague will have the most flights, with 60 during December, about two flights a day. The airline will operate 48 flights to Athens, 45 to Budapest and 30 each to Vienna and Barcelona.

Together with the additional flights, Blue Bird has published its starting fares for December. Budapest and Athens are the cheapest destinations, with fares from €90 one way. Fares to Vienna and Barcelona start at €136, while Prague starts at €154 one way.

The expansion comes amid higher demand for winter holidays in Europe, particularly during the Hanukkah break and Christmas season, and adds seats on routes also served by Israeli and foreign airlines. Blue Bird says the additional flights are already scheduled and available to book on its website and through travel agents.
Published by Globes, Israel business news - en.globes.co.il - on November 25, 2026.

articles.title: Energy bills to rise by 26% from January after gas prices surge
articles.summary: A household using a typical amount of energy would see its annual bill rise from £1,723 to £2,166 if this level was sustained for a year.
paragraphs: Cost of living correspondent
Energy bills will soar by 26% for millions of households in January after a surge in gas prices sparked by the Iran war.

A typical bill will increase by about £37 a month in the first three months of the new year, although the price will depend on how much energy a household uses, so it could be closer to £60 extra a month in winter.

A household using a typical amount of energy in England, Scotland and Wales and paying by direct debit, would see their annual bill rise from £1,723 to £2,166 if the increase was sustained for a year, said regulator Ofgem.
The government will pay millions of households £100 from 4 January to help cover winter costs on top of an existing VAT cut on electricity.
Charities and suppliers expect debt to rise and a wave of people to need emergency support.

Ofgem said the rise had been driven entirely by higher wholesale costs faced by suppliers owing, primarily, to the Iran war. Wholesale gas prices, paid by suppliers, were up 33% in the last three months, the period used to set the January to March cap. They have more than doubled since late 2025.
The warm home discount will take £150 off bills for six million households on benefits this winter. There have been calls for this support, funded through everyone's bill, to be extended.
"We are staring down the barrel of a brutal winter," said Dame Clare Moriarty, chief executive of Citizens Advice.

Neil Kenward, Ofgem's director general for markets, said it wrote to energy suppliers "reminding them of their responsibilities" to customers this winter. They have been told to identify people who need help early, make support easy to access and ensure repayment plans are affordable and sustainable.
Campaign Groups Friends of the Earth and Global Witness said major oil and energy companies are making huge profits because of spiralling oil costs, hurting households.

Energy UK, which represents suppliers, said the firms which send your bill, have profits capped on a percentage basis and do not see the same benefit as international energy generating companies. However, higher bills will mean higher profits in nominal cash terms.
The increase is the biggest since Russia's invasion of Ukraine drove up prices. It comes at a tough time of year, when the weather is at its coldest.
People on prepayment meters will be hit as their spending comes when energy is needed, rather than the cost being spread over the year as with direct debits.
What is the price cap?
The cap sets a maximum price for each unit of energy, not the total bill. Those on fixed deals are unaffected until the end of their term, but for those on variable tariffs it means:
For electricity, average unit prices will go up on 1 January from 26.32p per kilowatt-hour to 32.69p. The electricity price is often pegged to gas, owing to gas-fired generation.
Gas will increase from 7.97p per kilowatt-hour to 10.96p, higher than in the wake of the invasion of Ukraine.
Daily standing charges will be 54.77p for electricity and 29.65p for gas.
The cap is set every three months, based on the costs faced by suppliers as well as the cost of running the energy system.

It is based on a three-month period that ends about six weeks before the new cap comes into force. A fall in international wholesale prices in recent days will not be reflected in January's cap, but it will be in April's.
Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said people will be "deeply concerned" by another rise in energy bills.
"For too long, British families have been paying the price for conflicts overseas and volatile fossil fuel markets," she said.

Andrew Bowie, shadow energy secretary, said: "It is an outrage that, as bills soar, Labour are not only piling green levies and taxes onto bills but signing us up to an EU scheme that risks pushing them even higher.
'We've turned the heating down by 2.5C'
Stacey, 40, a single mother from Bristol, said dealing with rising energy costs has felt like a "battle" recently and she's worried about 2027.
She's turned her central heating down from 22C to 19.5C, bought electric blankets and pays her bills by direct debit.
She also leaves her curtains shut to "keep the heat in", while her daughters wear thermal clothing if it gets chilly in the house.
Support payment for millions
Up to 20 million households in England will get a £100 payment from 4 January to help with their energy bills this winter, with equivalent payments in Scotland and Wales.
Citizens Advice said the money will disappear quickly, particularly for those on prepayment meters, leading to a wave of requests for emergency help.
Energy UK said the funding was poorly targeted and insufficient to stem rising levels of customer debt.
The government said councils had a £100m discretionary fund to support vulnerable households which fell outside of the main scheme.
How is the cost of energy affecting your quality of life? What questions do you have?

articles.title: הישראלים שמאחורי היוניקורן שאנבידיה לא תאהב
articles.summary: אם חשבתם שסבב סיד של 10 או 15 מיליון דולר הוא אירוע חריג, כדאי שתכירו את Marlowe, סטארטאפ צעיר, שנחשף אתמול (ג') עם גיוסים בהיקף של 277 מיליון דולר, לפי שווי של 1.15 מיליארד דולר. מאחורי ההשקעה המטורפת הזו נמצאת נוכחות ישראלית מרשימה שכוללת כמה שמות מוכרים מאוד מהאקוסיסטם המקומי. בין היתר השקיע בחברה ליאור […]
paragraphs: אם חשבתם שסבב סיד של 10 או 15 מיליון דולר הוא אירוע חריג, כדאי שתכירו את Marlowe, סטארטאפ צעיר, שנחשף אתמול (ג') עם גיוסים בהיקף של 277 מיליון דולר, לפי שווי של 1.15 מיליארד דולר.

מאחורי ההשקעה המטורפת הזו נמצאת נוכחות ישראלית מרשימה שכוללת כמה שמות מוכרים מאוד מהאקוסיסטם המקומי. בין היתר השקיע בחברה ליאור סוסן, מייסד קרן Eclipse, שהובילה את ההשקעה הראשונית בחברה ומשמש גם כיו"ר Marlowe; אל ליאור הצטרף גם אחיו, עידו סוסן, המוכר כמייסד ומנכ"ל חברת תקשורת השבבים הישראלית DriveNets, שמכהן גם הוא בדירקטוריון. אל השניים, שלוקחים חלק פעיל בניהול החברה, הצטרפו גם קרן פיטנגו הישראלית, ובגזרת המשקיעים הפרטיים, אסף רפפורט, ממייסדי Wiz, ואחד האנג'לים הכי פעילים בהייטק הישראלי. לצידם, השקיעו בסטארטאפ האמריקאי גם קרנות כמו Accel ו-Bessemer ומנכ"לי ענקיות טכנולוגיה Uber, Box ו-Stripe.
בכירי מיקרוסופט לשעבר שאומרים לא לאנבידיה

את Marlowe הקימו ב-2025 המנכ"ל דן לואיס וה-CTO קוטה סריניווסאן, שניהם כיהנו בעבר כסגני נשיא במיקרוסופט, והובילו שם את תחומי ה-AI הארגוני והתשתיות. השניים סיפרו כי זיהו צוואר בקבוק: רוב הדאטה סנטרים הקיימים נבנו לאימון מודלים והותאמו לשבבים של אנבידיה, אבל כיום הביקוש האמיתי מזנק דווקא בשלב ההרצה, או Inference שנעשה בשבבים אחרים. לפי החברה, בזמן שעלויות הקמת מרכזי הנתונים זינקו ב-40% מאז 2020, קלאסטרים של GPU גנריים פשוט לא מנצלים היטב את החומרה עבור משימות אלו.

במקום לקנות שרתים סטנדרטיים, Marlowe מתכננת דאטה סנטרים ייעודיים שבהם החומרה, ארכיטקטורת הרשת, מערכות הקירור והתוכנה מותאמים יחד לסוגי עומסים ספציפיים. הניסיון של עידו סוסן בבניית רשתות תקשורת מבוססות תוכנה ב-DriveNets משתלב ישירות בגישה הזו. בפוסט ההשקה של החברה הסבירו המנכ"ל דן לואיס וה-CTO קוטה סריניווסאן כי "גם שיפורים מתונים בארכיטקטורת הרשת, בניהול החשמל ובאופטימיזציה ייעודית ל-Inference מצטברים ליתרון מובהק של פי שניים עד שלושה בביצועים, בזמינות ובעלויות" – או כמו שהם מתאים זאת "multiple times the FLOPs density".

מה שמעניין הוא, שלפחות בשלב הראשון, Marlowe בחרה לדלג על אנבידיה ולהתבסס על שבבים של המתחרות. האתר הראשון שלה, שיתחיל לפעול בדצמבר הקרוב, יתבסס על השבבים של Etched, שמציעים צפיפות חישוב גבוהה יותר מכרטיסים גרפיים רגילים ותקשורת פנימית מהירה פי ארבעה. האתר השני מתוכנן לרבעון השני של 2027 ויתבסס על מערכות Helios של AMD, שמשלבות 72 מעבדים גרפיים עם שבבי Pensando DPU שמורידים מהם את עומסי הרשת, לצד חיבורי קירור נוזלי מהירים. כרגע, החברה כבר בדרך להקמת האתר השלישי שלה והיא מעסיקה כ-30 עובדים בארצות הברית, צוות שמן הסתם צפוי לזנק עכשיו עם כל ההון החדש.

articles.title: Israel Tax Authority demands NIS 12b more from Wiz founders
articles.summary: The dispute involves the taxation of options and intellectual property and the shekel-dollar exchange rate used to calculate the tax.
paragraphs: The dispute involves the taxation of options and intellectual property and the shekel-dollar exchange rate used to calculate the tax.

The Israel Tax Authority is demanding that the founders of cybersecurity giant Wiz - Assaf Rappaport, Yinon Costica, Ami Luttwak and Roy Reznik - pay another NIS 20 billion in tax on cash proceeds from the sale, options under the Section 102 tax track, and intellectual property (IP). Google completed its $32 billion acquisition of Wiz in March 2026, in the largest exit in Israel’s history.

Wiz is offering to pay less, possibly as little as half the amount demanded, and the sides are expected to compromise on NIS 12-13 billion, sources have told "Globes.". The talks are continuing even though the sale closed in March and the sides spent the preceding year preparing for the closing. Wiz and its founders are understood to have paid about NIS 8 billion in tax to date.

Industry sources expect the Israel Tax Authority to issue a tax assessment if the sides fail to reach an agreement. If the dispute persists, the case could go to court. Wiz and the Israel Tax Authority did not respond to requests for comment.

Most Wiz investors are foreigners who are not liable for the tax, so most of the tax revenue from the sale will come from the founders. All four founders are Israeli citizens. Around the time the deal closed, the sides agreed that the tax would be paid in dollars, but the final amount remains in dispute.

Each of Wiz’s four founders received $2.5 - 3 billion before tax. Each is due to pay 25% in capital gains tax and a 5% surtax, for a total tax rate of 30%. The four were therefore asked to pay a combined $3-3.5 billion in tax.

Another unresolved issue is which date should be used to calculate the tax. Wiz previously insisted on paying in dollars based on the March 2026 closing date. The Israel Tax Authority insisted on using the exchange rate from a year earlier, when the deal was announced in principle and the dollar was 15% higher than at closing. The tax payments were due to reach state coffers in April, about a month after the deal closed.
Where is the IP, and what would a settlement mean for similar companies?

The dispute over IP revolves around Wiz’s corporate structure. Wiz was founded as a US company, with its parent company in Delaware and its Israeli development center in Tel Aviv operating as a subsidiary.

The Israel Tax Authority believes that most of Wiz’s technology and IP was developed in Israel, where the company hired hundreds of veterans of IDF Unit 8200 and other military intelligence technology units. Wiz argues that it is a US company and registered its IP in the US.
Biggest-ever exit: Google completes Wiz acquisition
Amazon confirms Decart acquisition

Any settlement between the Israel Tax Authority and Wiz will be closely scrutinized by the founders of Decart, the Israeli startup sold to Amazon earlier this week for $7.5 billion in a deal structured in stages over five years. Like Wiz, Decart was founded in the US, with its Tel Aviv development center operating as a subsidiary. Most of its R&D engineers are veterans of Israeli army Units 8200 and 81. Decart also resembles Wiz in that most of its investors are based outside Israel. They include Silicon Valley’s Zeev Ventures, Sequoia, Benchmark and Radical Ventures. Here too, most of the tax revenue will come from the founders’ proceeds. They hold 64% of Decart’s shares and are expected to pay about NIS 5.5 billion to the Israel Tax Authority.

The dispute between the Israel Tax Authority and Wiz has set a precedent and prompted a package of changes to tech taxation. The Tax Authority is promoting the package and awaiting the formation of a new government to back it. The authority is planning a series of tax breaks for acquisitions and for Israeli companies that operate through US parent companies, as Wiz does.

Under the new proposal, companies would reach an arrangement with the Israel Tax Authority to share IP and product sales rights under an agreement drawn up in advance, instead of paying billions of shekels in tax on transfers of IP from Israel to the US. The agreement would specify the respective shares of the Israeli and foreign operations in R&D and sales and allow them to share costs.

For existing IP, which is developed in Israel, a common framework would govern royalty payments in different countries. IP developed from the time of the sale onward would be treated as jointly owned. The aim is to avoid creating an incentive to transfer IP abroad or register it abroad in the first place.

The Tax Authority also proposes fixing the corporate tax payable by foreign companies for operating Israeli development centers through individual eight-year tax rulings. Under the proposal, the tax rate on imputed profit under the cost-plus method would be 13%. This fairly high rate would be negotiable, and setting it in advance would prevent recurring disputes over tax payments. Major companies such as Meta, Microsoft and Google currently pay single-digit corporate tax rates on their development operations in Israel, a policy intended to encourage them to hire locally.
Published by Globes, Israel business news - en.globes.co.il - on November 25, 2026.
Wiz founders Yinon Costica, Assaf Rappaport, Ami Luttwak, Roy Reznik credit: Avishag Shaar Yishuv
