articles.title: Judges propose dropping two of three cases against Netanyahu
articles.summary: The three judges suggested to Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara that the bribery and breach of trust cases against Netanyahu be dropped and a deal in the gifts case be sought.
paragraphs: The three judges suggested to Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara that the bribery and breach of trust cases against Netanyahu be dropped and a deal in the gifts case be sought.
Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara attended the Jerusalem District Court today for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s trial, as directed by the judges. Netanyahu did not attend.

At the hearing, Judges Rivka Friedman-Feldman, Moshe Bar-Am and Oded Shaham suggested that the prosecution drop the charge against Netanyahu in Case 4000, reconsider the charge in Case 2000 and seek a deal in Case 1000.

Friedman-Feldman said, "Now that Netanyahu has finished testifying, the trials have reached a point where we need to consider how to proceed. The public interest requires a rethink. We are sharing our impressions so far to convey how we see things. These comments concern Netanyahu alone because we have not heard from the other defendants."

On Case 4000 (the charge of accepting a bribe from Shaul Elovitch), Friedman-Feldman said, "The bribery charge presents considerable difficulties. The quid pro quo element rests mainly on the meeting at which instructions were allegedly given. It is difficult to make findings based on Shlomo Filber’s testimony. There is serious doubt as to whether the unusually favorable treatment was proven, and it is unclear on what basis it is considered unusual. The conflict of interest also raises doubts about whether Netanyahu committed a breach of trust. The chances of conviction are low enough to warrant reconsideration."

On Case 2000 (Noni Mozes), the presiding judge said, "We doubt whether the charge entails an offense. There is a real question as to whether the legal conclusions asserted are supported by the evidence. The prosecution was not given an opportunity to present a full argument on this point, and it can submit one before we decide. It is unclear whether there is a basis for the allegation of abuse of official authority."

On Case 1000 (the gifts case), the judges said a decision must be reached. Their remarks suggest they see grounds for a conviction on some offense, even if it is not breach of trust, the offense Netanyahu was originally charged with. "Here we can work toward a resolution. We are open to every possibility," the judges said.
Baharav-Miara: We will consider what the court said

Baharav-Miara responded, "We are open to hearing whatever the court has to say, and we will consider it. We are always willing to consider what the court says, and of course we are willing to do so now. There are two ways to conclude the case: a verdict or an appropriate deal that reflects the nature of the conduct and the evidence.
"We will review each of the court’s comments with the team. As for resolving the case through a deal, that is the quickest route, and it is open to us at any stage."
Netanyahu’s defense attorney Amit Hadad said, "We extend our hand in return. We believe the right course is mediation here in court, not with the president."
"There is added value in the attorney general appearing in person"

The judges ordered Baharav-Miara to attend the hearing so they could have "a substantive two-way discussion." They made the decision despite her position that the lawyers handling the case from the Tax and Economic Prosecution Office were authorized to take part in the discussion and were conveying the message to her.

The judges said, "There is still added value in the attorney general appearing in person. In our view, a substantive two-way discussion requires that the person responsible for making the decisions be able to hear what is said directly and respond as needed."
The court set the aim of the hearing as "Exploring with the parties’ authorized representatives various options for conducting and advancing the proceedings as they relate to Mr. Netanyahu."

In June 2023 and again in June 2026, the judges recommended that the prosecution drop the bribery count in the indictment, which alleges that Netanyahu granted regulatory benefits to Shaul Elovitch, then the owner of Bezeq and the Walla website. In September the judges said, "Having heard the prime minister’s testimony, our position remains as it was in June 2023."
Presumption of innocence: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Shaul and Iris Elovitch, and Arnon (Noni) Mozes have not been convicted of any offense and are presumed innocent.
Published by Globes, Israel business news - en.globes.co.il - on November 25, 2026.

articles.title: 'I only use the washing machine on a Sunday' - how we're keeping our energy bills down
articles.summary: The BBC speaks to three people about steps they take to keep their energy bills under control.
paragraphs: ByDaniel Thomas and Anuk WeerawardanaBusiness reporters
Domestic energy prices will soar by 26% in January under the regulator Ofgem's new price cap, pushing up bills for millions of households across England, Scotland and Wales.
With household budgets already under pressure, finding ways to reduce gas and electricity costs has become increasingly important. But how much difference can simple changes really make?
The BBC spoke to three people about what they're doing to keep their energy costs down.
'We power down at peak times'
Image source, Kelly Anne Harvey
Like many people, Kelly Anne Harvey, a building surveyor from Cleveleys near Blackpool, is worried about her energy bill going up next year.
The 44-year-old, who is married with a five-year-old son, has a combined household income of £60,000.
She currently pays about £154 a month for gas and electricity on a standard variable rate with Octopus, but is looking for a fixed-rate deal to offset the rise.
The family fell into arrears on their energy bills a few years ago and Kelly says she won't let it happen again.
To control her costs she pays by direct debit, which spreads her payments and is typically £138 cheaper a year than paying on receipt of a bill.
The family uses electric blankets and portable oil radiators in some rooms so they don't have to turn the central heating on as often.
They also take part in Octopus's energy saving scheme, which rewards customers who use less electricity at peak times, such as early evenings, with a free hour of energy at the weekend.
"On Sunday we'll turn on the dishwasher, tumble drier, washing machine and maybe even charge our electric cars," says Kelly.
'We've turned the heating down by 2.5C'
Stacey, 40, a single mother from Bristol, says dealing with rising energy costs has felt like a "battle" recently and she's worried about 2027.

The office worker, whose daughters are aged 10 and 12, is on a fixed-term tracker tariff with E.On Next, which charges rates set below the quarterly Ofgem price cap. She expects to pay £1,800 for energy this year, up £400 on last year.
Stacey, who is part of the Changing Realities project at Glasgow University, which documents life for people on low incomes, has tried a number of things to control her energy costs.
She's turned her central heating down from 22C to 19.5C, bought electric blankets and pays her bills by direct debit.
She also leaves her curtains shut to "keep the heat in", while her daughters wear thermal clothing if it gets chilly in the house. The family is also using less hot water.
"I've got girls and they're growing up and they want to spend loads of time in the shower [but] it's just not possible."
'I order heating oil in bulk'
Around 1.5 million households in the UK rely on heating oil for heating and hot water, and their costs have already soared in the past year due to disruption in global oil markets.

"When I first moved here two years ago you could get a litre of heating oil for 50-60p," says Bradley Knowles, 32, who lives in a barn conversion with his husband, mother and sister in rural Lincolnshire.
"At the height of the Iran war it went up to £1.20 or £1.30 and now it's stabilised at around £1."

To cut costs, the finance worker orders oil in bulk, buying 1,000-1,500 litres, preferably in the summer months when prices are lower. He also tries to order a few weeks in advance to avoid expensive next-day deliveries.
Bradley uses comparison sites to see which local suppliers offer the cheapest oil and puts money aside each month so he can always afford his orders.
Oil-powered boilers may take time to heat up, but Bradley advises against leaving them on all day as that can be very expensive.
Instead, he uses an electric tank to store his warm water and tops up the heating in parts of the property with electric radiators.
Additional reporting by Kris Bramwell & Bernadette McCague.
What are you doing to cope with rising energy bills?

articles.title: UK embassy in Japan warns of rise in drink spiking and credit card fraud at Tokyo bars
articles.summary: Social media campaign fronted by British rapper Shao Dow advises tourists not to let their guard down The British embassy in Tokyo has launched a social media campaign warning visitors to exercise caution after a rise in cases of drink-spiking and credit card fraud against tourists in the Japanese capital. In a recent clip made in conjunction with the embassy, the British rapper and manga artist Shao Dow, a frequent visitor to Japan, notes that although the country “is incredibly safe, that doesn’t mean you can let your guard down”. Continue reading...
paragraphs: The British embassy in Tokyo has launched a social media campaign warning visitors to exercise caution after a rise in cases of drink-spiking and credit card fraud against tourists in the Japanese capital.

In a recent clip made in conjunction with the embassy, the British rapper and manga artist Shao Dow, a frequent visitor to Japan, notes that although the country “is incredibly safe, that doesn’t mean you can let your guard down”.

He warns that young male tourists are particularly susceptible to being lured into bars on the promise of being able to chat to attractive, English-speaking women. They are then served drug-laced drinks and enormous sums are charged to their credit cards.
Drink-spiking cases involving British and other international tourists have been on the rise in the past two years in popular nightlife districts such as Roppongi, Shibuya and Kabukicho.

Some victims have lost up to £30,000 (US$39,000) in a single night, Dow says, and wake up with no memory of what happened. “Look, do me a favour,” he adds, “Stay alert, trust your gut, keep an eye on your stuff and don’t follow strangers into bars.”

Police in Tokyo have come under pressure to tackle the rise in incidents targeting tourists. Earlier this month, 160 riot police conducted predawn raids on two establishments in Kabukicho after reports they had ripped off customers. Five people were arrested.

Between January and October, police recorded 340 cases – up 195 from last year – in the Shinjuku area after customers, some of whom were lured into bars by street touts, were charged extortionate sums. In one case, ¥9.6m ($60,000) was allegedly charged to a customer’s credit card.

According to the newspaper Asahi Shimbun, victims have paid ¥390m in total and foreign nationals had been the targets in 70% of cases. The newspaper quoted a senior investigator as saying the reported crimes were the “tip of the iceberg” since many visitors returned home before they realised they had been swindled, while others had left Japan without reporting the incidents to police.
Reports say the rise in cases was being fuelled by Japan’s tourism boom. A record 42.7 million people visited Japan last year, including 530,000 from the UK.
The Guardian has approached the Japan National Tourism Organisation for comment.

articles.title: Sri Lankan asylum seeker killed himself after being sent by UK to Eswatini
articles.summary: Kishanth Peramalya was denied entry due to sexual assault convictions and sent to Africa where he had no connections The UK sent a Sri Lankan asylum seeker who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, a southern African country to which he had no connection and where he killed himself. Kishanth Peramalya was part of a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum there. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it got into difficulty and brought to Diego Garcia in the remote British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a US-UK military…
paragraphs: The UK sent a Sri Lankan asylum seeker who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, a southern African country to which he had no connection and where he killed himself.

Kishanth Peramalya was part of a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum there. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it got into difficulty and brought to Diego Garcia in the remote British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a US-UK military base.

In November 2024, the UK allowed 61 migrants to enter from Diego Garcia after a damning UN report about conditions in the camp. However, the then home secretary, Yvette Cooper, denied Peramalya entry to the UK due to his criminal convictions while he was on Diego Garcia for four counts of sexual assault, one count of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and one count of arson. Cooper’s decision was upheld by UK courts.

Peramalya had been granted protection from being returned to Sri Lanka, having been tortured and sexually abused by Sri Lankan military personnel as a teenager. In late March, the Maldives said it would take him for 30 days, according to the BBC. He was then transferred to Eswatini, a country landlocked by South Africa and Mozambique and formerly known as Swaziland, where he killed himself on 13 September.

A draft deal between the UK and Eswatini governments would have committed Downing Street to cover the costs of Peramalya’s resettlement there for three years, according to the BBC, which said the UK was also finalising arrangements for Peramalya to live in Eswatini permanently.

The Guardian has not seen the draft deal. Thabile Mdluli, a spokesperson for Eswatini’s government, said: “The initial arrangement was temporary in nature and intended to safeguard Mr Peramalya’s safety while the government of the United Kingdom worked towards a long-term solution regarding his circumstances.”

She said that no formal agreement was ever reached over Peramalya’s long-term residency status with the UK and declined to comment further on the specific arrangements of his stay in Eswatini or the circumstances around his death.

Mdluli said: “Eswatini has not received any other similar request from the government of the United Kingdom. The government of the Kingdom of Eswatini remains committed to ensuring that any agreements entered into with external partners safeguard national interest as well as the safety and security of Emaswati [Swazi people].”

A UK government spokesperson said: “Keeping the British public safe will always be our first priority, and we will continue to take the decisions necessary to protect the British people. That includes taking steps to ensure high harm foreign criminals cannot enter the UK. We continue to work with the Eswatini authorities in relation to this case.”
Peramalya had post-traumatic stress disorder and attempted suicide multiple times on Diego Garcia, according to a UK high court judgment in February 2025.

Peramalya’s family told the BBC he was initially housed alone in an isolated guesthouse in Eswatini. “My brother did not want to go there at all,” said his sister, speaking from India. “He couldn’t manage being there alone, he was very lonely.”

She said he had called her four times a day and was initially having weekly psychiatric appointments, which were made daily when his mental health deteriorated, as well as having someone brought in to prepare his food.
Peramalya’s relatives said they were not aware of his convictions for sexual offences or any plan to make his transfer to Eswatini permanent.

Eswatini has accepted dozens of third-country deportees from the US since July 2025. In November 2025, its government confirmed it had received $5.1m in exchange for taking up to 160 migrants from the US.

articles.title: Indian Cockroach movement leader asks court for permission to fly to UK
articles.summary: Officials at Delhi airport stopped Saurav Das from boarding flight to Britain, where students have invited him to speak A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has asked the Delhi high court to give him permission to fly to the UK after immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him boarding a flight early on Tuesday morning. The court is scheduled to hear Saurav Das’s case on Thursday morning. His lawyer asked the court for a quick hearing because Das has by now already missed some of his engagements at British universities and can only attend the other events on his…
paragraphs: A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has asked the Delhi high court to give him permission to fly to the UK after immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him boarding a flight early on Tuesday morning.

The court is scheduled to hear Saurav Das’s case on Thursday morning. His lawyer asked the court for a quick hearing because Das has by now already missed some of his engagements at British universities and can only attend the other events on his itinerary if he is allowed to fly out as soon as possible.
Das, 27, is one of the main faces of the Cockroach movement, which shot into the political firmament out of nowhere in May to challenge the Narendra Modi government with street protests.
The movement succeeded in forcing the education minister to resign in July over exam leaks and has since functioned as a pressure group.
Das had been invited by the Oxford Union Society to participate in a “fireside chat” on the movement.
Indian student groups at Edinburgh, Cambridge, Queen Mary University of London and the London School of Economics have also invited him to speak.
“Students want to know how we succeeded without any violence, how we began and where we are going. There is a great curiosity about the movement,” Das told the Guardian.
Reports in the Indian media have alleged that Das was informed well before the flight that his passport contained discrepancies.

“None of these reports is true,” said Das. “I received an email five hours before my flight saying that I should not use my passport for travel. It gave no reason. And I did not see the email until I arrived at Delhi airport. What’s more, I’ve travelled abroad before on this passport since it was issued in 2019 so what’s the problem with it now?”

He suspects that the government is using a frivolous case filed in Chennai against him as a pretext. The case has been filed, Das surmises, by someone hostile to the Cockroach movement and disputes his citizenship.

Das believes he was deliberately stopped by a government that is “scared” of someone such as him speaking abroad about the ideals of Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru (independent India’s first prime minister) and that it wanted to make an example of him.
“It’s a chilling signal to young Indians that we can do what we like, that if we can do this to a leader of a movement, we can do this to you too,” said Das.
In recent years, the government has stopped foreign speakers and academics, including several from the UK, from entering India.

Last year, Francesca Orsini, a professor at Soas University of London, was stopped at Delhi airport and deported despite holding a valid visa. The government said she had been blacklisted for allegedly conducting research and speaking at events while visiting on a tourist visa in 2024.
Also last year, Nitasha Kaul, a professor at Westminster University, was detained at Bangalore airport and deported for “anti-India activities”.

Some people who find themselves blacklisted have chosen to fight back. In 2023, the UK-based journalist Amrit Wilson had her overseas citizen of India card which allows free movement into India cancelled, also for alleged “anti-India activities”.
She took legal action and earlier this week, the Delhi high court ruled that the government had failed to give any concrete details of what it meant by “anti-India activities”.
The court has given the government a week to issue a fresh notice, this time giving specific reasons.

articles.title: China misusing Interpol to target dissidents, says leading UK lawyer
articles.summary: Concerns over Beijing’s use of ‘red notices’ as Hong Kong prepares to host police organisation’s general assembly China is misusing Interpol to target and silence dissidents, a leading British lawyer has claimed, as Hong Kong prepares to host the police organisation’s general assembly for the first time. Ben Keith, a specialist in “red notices” - the Interpol system under which national authorities are requested to locate and detain suspects - said he was working on five cases involving China making questionable requests through Interpol. Continue reading...
paragraphs: China is misusing Interpol to target and silence dissidents, a leading British lawyer has claimed, as Hong Kong prepares to host the police organisation’s general assembly for the first time.

Ben Keith, a specialist in “red notices” - the Interpol system under which national authorities are requested to locate and detain suspects - said he was working on five cases involving China making questionable requests through Interpol.

He revealed that he had also contacted officials at the law enforcement organisation in July on behalf of a group of five high-profile UK-based Chinese dissidents to find out if Beijing had sought the issuance of red notices relating to them.

Interpol responded in October that they were looking into his request for information but there had been no substantive information shared, he added, raising concerns that there might be data relating to the individuals on the Interpol system.

He said: “If there’s no data, than they will tell me there’s no data. If there is data, then they have to get permission from Hong Kong to tell me. It has been sometime now. Given the profile of these individuals, I think they may have had some data on them. That’s the fear.”

Many Hong Kong democracy campaigners who fled to the UK in recent years have British national (overseas) status but this does not protect them from red notices outside the UK and potential extradition to China.

A red notice is a request to law enforcement worldwide to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition, surrender, or similar legal action. It is based on an arrest warrant or court order issued by the judicial authorities in the requesting country. Member countries apply their own laws in deciding whether to arrest a person.

Keith said: “The Russian playbook was to accuse political opponents or business opponents of some sort of really technical criminal offence of fraud, employment law breach, regulatory offence, that sort of thing, to disguise the real purpose of the request. The Chinese have taken that on.”

Hong Kong will host the 94th Interpol general assembly between 30 November and 3 December, attracting police chiefs from its 196 member countries to set global policing policy, approve budgets and activities, and pass binding resolutions.

Keith said that hosting the assembly offered an opportunity for China to “reputation wash”, arguing that Beijing ran a sophisticated public relations machine to hide the high proportion of red notice and extradition requests that were politically motivated.

The red notice system is used by China to target those sought under the state campaigns launched under President Xi Jinping to track down fugitives overseas and recover illicit funds, known as Operations Fox Hunt and Sky Net, it is claimed.

A new report, The Red Notice Trap, by Ben Keith and Rhys Davies of the legal firm IHR Advisors, draws on court judgments, Interpol records and Chinese-language official documents, to show how red notices fit into Beijing’s campaign to silence critics and bring them home for persecution.

It notes under a 2025 revision of the implementing regulations for the People’s Repubilc of China’s supervision law that red notice requests sit with extradition, judicial assistance, law enforcement cooperation, prosecution abroad, asset seizure and ‘ideological education’, as tools for the recovery of people.

Among the cases cited in the IHR Advisors report is that of Yidiresi Aishan – a Uyghur activist who is also known as Idris Hassan – who was arrested in July 2021, when arriving at Casablanca airport on a flight from Turkey, where he had been living.

He was detained on the basis of a red notice issued by Interpol at China’s request “for belonging to a terrorist organisation”. Within two weeks, Interpol suspended the notice as it breached its rules and it was later cancelled.
The Moroccan extradition proceedings carried on regardless and in December 2021 the country’s court of cassation approved Hasan’s surrender to China.

The UN committee against torture found that Hasan’s extradition would breach article 3 of the convention against torture and Morocco did not carry out the extradition But Hasan remained in detention until 12 February 2025 after spending nearly four years in prison on the basis of an Interpol red notice.
“His case shows the central weakness this report returns to: Interpol can correct its own data, but it cannot undo what national authorities have already set in motion”, the authors write.
Hasan, who now lives in Canada, said he no longer travelled and that his life had been thrown “upside down”.
“Four years of life have gone, just spent in prison, I could not be with my children,” he told the Guardian. “Everything has changed. I cannot describe this. But I trust Canada.”
Hasan added: “I don’t understand how this kind of the big organisation like Interpol how they took my name down without evidence, without nothing. Just put my name out.”
The Chinese embassy has been approached for comment.

An Interpol spokesperson said: “Interpol knows Red Notices are powerful tools for law enforcement cooperation and is fully aware of their potential impact on the individuals concerned, which is why Interpol has a number of systems in place to avoid misuse of our systems, and these have been significantly strengthened over the last few years.
“Interpol’s constitution affirms the Organisation’s neutrality. Under Article 3, Red Notice requests must not be of a predominantly political, military, religious or racial character.”

articles.title: Pro-Palestine activist sought by US in extradition case: ‘I still have a right to my beliefs’
articles.summary: James ‘Fergie’ Chambers, at center of legal fight, says he ‘should not be unjustly accused’ because of leftwing views James “Fergie” Chambers, the wealthy leftwing activist and donor controversially sought in extradition by the US, has told the Guardian that he is “not asking anyone to endorse my ideas or not think I’m a jerk – but I still have a right to my beliefs and should not be unjustly accused because of them”. Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international…
paragraphs: James “Fergie” Chambers, the wealthy leftwing activist and donor controversially sought in extradition by the US, has told the Guardian that he is “not asking anyone to endorse my ideas or not think I’m a jerk – but I still have a right to my beliefs and should not be unjustly accused because of them”.

Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money-laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.
The complaint also includes riot and conspiracy to riot charges stemming from 2023 protests against New England branches of Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit.

Chambers was speaking from his Madrid apartment in his first in-depth interview after a Spanish appeals court ordered his provisional release on bail on Friday. That release was due to issues with the legally required US translation of the extradition request’s core documents into Spanish, first reported by the Guardian.
“Support for my case doesn’t imply support of me, or my ideas,” Chambers said. “It’s about my right to have those ideas – and not be falsely accused of things.”
Chambers, whose case has gained attention across the world, had been detained since 10 July, when Spanish authorities arrested him in Ibiza.

The order granting Chambers’s provisional release asserted that the translation issues cause “a diminishment, at least for the time being, in the solidity or foundation of the extradition request”. Spanish judges had previously denied bail three times.

The wealthy heir to at least $250mn from his family’s business – Atlanta–based Cox Enterprises – was in the middle of his first visit without being separated by glass with his mother, Lauren Hamilton, when he was summoned to receive the “good news” on Friday, Chambers told the Guardian.

Minutes later, he returned to tell his mother he was being released. “She freaked out crying. We went nuts for about five minutes. Then we got to contacting my lawyer and getting my kids on a plane to Spain.”
On Monday, Chambers’s five-year-old son with actor and activist Stella Schnabel could be heard in the background. The tableau was in stark contrast to his months in prison.

“I tried to build a cocoon to deal with the immense unknown, the immense fear,” he said of his time in Aranjuez prison. “I would pray a lot. The only idea I could hold onto was, my home is the truth. The truth of who loves you. The truth of my own innocence. And the truth of what is happening in Palestine and all the things connected to what is happening in Palestine – other wars, gas prices. No one can take that away from you.”

Chambers has been supported by his mother throughout his case, and has reconnected with his father, James Cox Chambers – who owns an estimated 17% stake in Cox Enterprises but does not play an active role in the company – for the first time in five years.
“Speaking with my parents has provided emotional stability – and intelligent, adult minds to help make decisions,” Chambers said.

Although he has had political disagreements with his father, a donor to the Democratic party, Chambers said his father “sees this situation as totally unthinkable and out of step with anything resembling a just society”.
He also invoked his grandfather, the ACLU civil rights lawyer James Cox Hamilton, who died in 2014. “He would’ve turned in his grave over this,” Chambers said.

While locked up, Chambers, a US citizen, received hundreds of letters of support from friends, family and strangers, postmarked from Atlanta to Barcelona – including, he said, “from a guy who had been imprisoned under [Spanish dictator Francisco] Franco, who painted the ‘key of return’ [a symbol of homes lost in the 1948 Nakba] on the Palestinian flag”.

Chambers’s views and donations to progressive and humanitarian projects have been extensively profiled in US media, including his controversial public comments on Israel and Gaza. A week after the 7 October Hamas attacks on Israel, he posted on X about Israel’s response: “Stop calling it ‘collective punishment’/There’s nothing to be ‘punished’ for/No faction of the Palestinian resistance, Hamas or other, has done *anything* wrong/It’s simply genocide/Like it has been.”

His release followed a separate decision on Thursday by a three-judge panel at Spain’s high court tasked with deciding on the extradition to pause the proceedings in order to evaluate the impact of the alterations the US made to the original, machine-made translation of the extradition request into Spanish.

The US admitted to making several of the changes, calling them “substantial [and] inadvertent”. These and dozens of other changes introduced prejudicial notions with specific legal implications that in turn wound up in the Spanish prosecutor’s report on the case, Aitor Martínez, a member of Chambers’s defense team, told the Guardian last week.

It was also recently revealed that there is no indictment behind the complaint, meaning the federal government has not had a grand jury evaluate evidence against Chambers, and instead is seeking his extradition based on the affidavit of a single FBI agent, the core of the sealed criminal complaint.

During his time in prison, Chambers also began the process of applying for political asylum in Spain. He cannot be extradited until the asylum case runs its course, and also cannot be extradited if he is granted asylum. His legal team has notified the government office evaluating his asylum petition of the altered translations.

Chambers was arrested 10 July as he and Schnabel pulled into the driveway of a school they were visiting to see about enrolling their five-year-old, part of plans to move to Spain. They had been staying in Ireland, where Schnabel was working on a film.

Although the arrest came as a surprise – “I was confused! Did I speed?” he thought – Chambers revealed to the Guardian that a car had been following him around Dublin only days before, and that someone had broken into their car parked outside their house at night, without taking anything of value.
“I noticed signs of surveillance,” he said. Months later, last Wednesday, Irish police raided the same house, acting on a request from US authorities.
With his immediate future uncertain, Chambers said he was “looking forward to sharing a couple of nice dinners with my family this week”.
As for the past, he said the millions he has donated to an estimated 100 projects in about 20 countries is “the most important thing I’ve done”.

“Somebody with the political orientation I have and with resources, no matter how good of an activist I am, it’s not gonna be as effective as medical aid or feeding children in Gaza, supporting independent media that wouldn’t otherwise exist, or paying people’s bail who have been arrested for protesting.
“I’m giving a lot of money to things that other people aren’t giving money to.”
Chambers also said he was “grateful for the way Spanish courts have dealt with this – just focusing on the facts. It shouldn’t matter that I’ve made some emotional statements.”

articles.title: Energy bills will soar - here's how you can ease the pain
articles.summary: Household energy bills are about to increase but there are ways to keep a lid on your expenditure.
paragraphs: Image source, Getty Images
Cost of living correspondent
Energy bills will soar by 26% in the new year as the war in Iran pushes up wholesale prices.
Typical household bills will rise by £37 per month as Ofgem's latest price cap comes into force from January to March, but experts say it is possible to keep rising bills in check.
Here are four areas to consider ahead of the increase.
1. How you can save energy
Ofgem's price cap, as well as suppliers' fixed deals, set a limit on the price of each unit of energy, not the total bill.
So, you pay for what you use. Millions of people have cut back on their energy consumption during years of relatively high prices.
With the unit price of gas, in particular, set to soar, experts say you should take a fresh look at your energy use and renew good habits.
Research foundation Nesta suggests:
turning down the flow temperature on a combi boiler - usually indicated by a radiator icon, to make it operate more efficiently
turning off the pre-heat facility on some combi boilers, which would have kept some water heated up when not in use
turning down the thermostat one degree, although 18C is the recommended minimum
closing all curtains at night
lowering radiator valves outside of the living room
turning off the heating before April
These are small changes but - alongside washing clothes at 30C, blocking draughts and batch cooking - they can reduce energy use and bills.
Ofgem says about five million people still pay their bill when it arrives every three months, rather than receive a monthly bill often initially based on an estimate.
Taking regular meter readings, or having a smart meter, while paying by monthly direct debit solves that problem.
Paying by direct debit costs significantly less than by so-called standard credit - typically £138 cheaper a year.

Customers on prepayment schemes - usually people on low incomes struggling to pay bills - used to pay a higher rate than others, but now they pay slightly less than the capped direct debit variable rate.
Various deals may rely on paying by direct debit or having a smart meter.
3. Consider switching to a fixed rate

Moving to a fixed energy tariff means the price you are charged per unit of gas or electricity does not change every three months, although the total bill will still vary depending on how much energy you use.
The trouble is that it is very difficult to work out whether a fixed deal is a good deal at the moment, for those renewing fixed deals or looking for one for the first time.

Some fixed deals are available at unit prices below the next forecast price cap level. But should energy prices fall sharply then a longer-term fix might not seem such good value compared with the price cap.

So consumer group Which? also recommends paying close attention to any exit fees when picking a fixed deal. If variable prices fall below your fixed rate and you want to get out of it before the end of your agreement period, you may have to pay a hefty sum.
Before you fix, consumer website MoneySavingExpert advises you look at all the deals available, not just what your own supplier is offering.
4. Check what financial support you can get

The government will give a £100 payment to millions of homes to help cover winter energy costs. It will go to homes in council tax bands A to D in England, with the equivalent expected in Scotland and Wales.
There are also a range of other forms of support specifically for people on low incomes.
This winter anyone on means-tested benefits will get £150 off their electricity bill.
Your supplier will apply the discount automatically unless you are in Scotland, where you will need to contact your energy company to ask for the help.
Some people will also be eligible for a Cold Weather Payment, external and most pensioners will receive the winter fuel payment.
Beyond that, most energy suppliers offer hardship grants for people struggling to pay their bills and the government's Fuel Direct Scheme, external can help you repay energy debt.
You can get more advice from Ofgem, external, Citizens Advice, external, or your own energy supplier. Trade body Energy UK has a list of support schemes, external.
People on low incomes may also be eligible for grants to help with insulating their homes, and there are local schemes offering grants for solar panels, heat pumps and the like.
But if you are hunting around for grants, watch out for scams pretending to be official money-off schemes.
How is the cost of energy affecting your quality of life? What questions do you have?

articles.title: Susan brothers in next generation AI infrastructure venture
articles.summary: Lior and Ido Susan are executive board members of Marlowe AI, a US-based startup founded in May and already valued at $1.15 billion.
paragraphs: Lior and Ido Susan are executive board members of Marlowe AI, a US-based startup founded in May and already valued at $1.15 billion.

Brothers Lior and Ido Susan are collaborating on a new venture in artificial intelligence infrastructure. Marlowe AI , which has been operating under the radar for the past few months, emerged publicly this week, announcing a $277 million seed round, an exceptionally large round for a company at such an early stage. According to a Bloomberg report, the funding round values the company at $1.15 billion, just six months after its inception.

The latest funding round for the company, which was established in May of this year, was led by venture capital firm Accel, following an initial round led by Lior Susan’s Eclipse. Other investors in the company are Bessemer Venture Partners, Altimeter, Valor, and Israeli firm Pitango. Several of tech industry executives have also invested in the company, among them Wiz founder Assaf Rappaport, Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora, Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi, and the CEOs of Box and Dropbox.

Marlowe was founded last May by Dan Lewis and Kutta Srinivasan, both former senior managers at Microsoft, in collaboration with the Susan brothers and Stanford University AI researcher Chris Ré. Lior Susan, founder and CEO of Eclipse , serves as the company’s executive chairperson, while his brother Ido Susan, founder and CEO of Israeli communications infrastructure company DriveNets , serves as a board member actively involved in the company’s operations.

Lewis, who is CEO of Marlowe, previously headed the division responsible for Copilot Studio, Microsoft’s platform for developing AI agents. CTO Srinivasan, previously led the AI infrastructure division at the software giant. The company operates out of offices in Washington State and California and currently employs nearly 30 people.
Betting on the next phase of the AI revolution

Marlowe aims to capitalize on one of the key shifts currently taking place in the AI industry. While the early years of the revolution saw massive investment in computing infrastructure for training models, the growing adoption of AI tools is driving an increasing demand for computing power dedicated to running them-a process known as inference.

Essentially, every time a user submits a query to a chatbot, or asks an AI agent to write code or analyze a document, computing resources are required to execute the task. However, not all such tasks necessitate the same types of chips or computing infrastructure.

Marlowe plans to establish data centers at which the specific chips, communication systems, and software are pre-optimized for the types of tasks they are intended to perform. According to the company’s founders, this level of optimization could improve computing output-relative to power consumption and operating costs-by two to three times compared with the infrastructure currently in use. At this stage, this a matter of an estimate by the company.
The first server farms will operate without Nvidia chips

One of the most notable aspects of Marlow’s plan is the attempt to reduce reliance on Nvidia, whose chips underpin a large portion of the world’s artificial intelligence infrastructure. Rather than developing its own chips, the company aims to provide customers with computing power based on chips from various manufacturers, tailored to the customers' specific tasks.

Marlowe’s first data center is expected to become operational as early as next month. It will use chips from Etched, a US startup that develops specialized chips for running AI models, which was valued at $21 billion last August.

The second data center, slated to launch in the second quarter of 2027, will be based on new computing systems from AMD, a competitor to Nvidia. The company has not ruled out the possibility of using Nvidia chips in the future.

According to US tech news site GeekWire, Marlowe has also signed a letter of intent to establish a third data center, and has agreements with three customers whose identities have not yet been disclosed. Each of the planned data centers will have a capacity of several tens of megawatts. The funds raised will be used primarily for the procurement of chips and networking equipment, and to expand the company's engineering teams.

articles.title: מיקרוסופט מכריזה "קוד אדום" בעקבות הקריסה הנרחבת
articles.summary: אם גם אתם מצאתם את עצמכם בוהים במסך ריק לפני כשבועיים ותוהים למה לעזאזל האאוטלוק שלכם לא זז או למה הטימס התנתק, תתנחמו בזה שאתם לא בצוותי ההנדסה של מיקרוסופט, כי מתברר שמאחורי הקלעים במיקרוסופט המצב מלחיץ הרבה יותר. מיילים פנימיים שהגיעו לרויטרס חושפים עכשיו שבעקבות התקלה שנמשכה 24 שעות, הכריזה מיקרוסופט על מצב חירום […]
paragraphs: אם גם אתם מצאתם את עצמכם בוהים במסך ריק לפני כשבועיים ותוהים למה לעזאזל האאוטלוק שלכם לא זז או למה הטימס התנתק, תתנחמו בזה שאתם לא בצוותי ההנדסה של מיקרוסופט, כי מתברר שמאחורי הקלעים במיקרוסופט המצב מלחיץ הרבה יותר.
מיילים פנימיים שהגיעו לרויטרס חושפים עכשיו שבעקבות התקלה שנמשכה 24 שעות, הכריזה מיקרוסופט על מצב חירום הנדסי מיוחד ("Code Red"), כדי לשנות מהיסוד את הדרך שבה היא מטפלת בתקלות חמורות כאלו.

נזכיר שהתקלה הארוכה פגעה בלקוחות של מיקרוסופט במגוון רחב של תחומים – החל מממשלות, דרך ארגוני ענק וחברות תעופה ועד עסקים שונים ואתרי קניות, והשביתה שירותים כמו Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams ו-Copilot. במיקרוסופט הבהירו די מהתחלה שלא מדובר במתקפת סייבר או בסוכני AI שהשתגעו. אז מה באמת הפיל את המערכת?

בפוסט-מורטם שפרסם ב-X, הסביר צ'ארלס למאנה, סמנכ"ל בכיר ל-Copilot, סוכנים ופלטפורמה במיקרוסופט, ששלושה גורמים עיקריים גרמו לתקלה עולמית ב-networking gateway, שעליו מתבססים רבים משירותי Microsoft 365. הגורם הראשון היה באג רדום שהגיע לפרודקשן כבר ביולי כחלק מעדכון לשרתים. לדברי למאנה, "בדיקות העומס הרגילות שלנו לא זיהו את הבעיה החבויה בגלל סוג התעבורה וה-SKU השונה שבו השתמשנו במעבדות הבדיקה", כלומר הבאג השפיע בעיקר על חומרה חדשה עם יותר ליבות עיבוד, כשהבדיקות נעשו דווקא על חומרה חלשה יותר; הגורם השני היה מעבר (failover) של Teams מה-gateway החלופי ל-gateway הראשי, שתומך גם ב-Exchange Online, כ-15 שעות לפני התקלה; הגורם השלישי היה תקלה נפרדת, שהשביתה 14% מקיבולת השרתים.

השילוב שגרם לעומס הזה על מערכת עם פחות שרתים זמינים – בדיוק בשעות השיא של העבודה בארצות הברית – הפעיל את הבאג הרדום מיולי. התוצאה הייתה הצטברות בקשות שגרמה לשרתים להפסיק להגיב. בשלב הזה מערכות הניתוב האוטומטיות ניסו להציל את המצב והעבירו את הבקשות לשרתים אחרים ברשת, אבל התעבורה החדשה הפעילה את אותו באג רדום גם בהם, ויצרה אפקט דומינו שבשיאו הקריס מעל 80% מהשרתים של ה-networking gateway.
מיקרוסופט מכריזה על Code Red

במיילים, כותב ג'ייסון הנדרסון, נשיא M365 Core, שזהו האירוע שהשפיע על הלקוחות יותר מכל אירוע אחר בתולדות Exchange והבהיר: "Code Red אומר שזו העבודה בעלת העדיפות הגבוהה ביותר עבור הצוות שלנו". אמנדה סילבר, סגנית נשיא ל-M365 Core ו-Work IQ, תיארה עבודה ב"ערפל קרב", עם מעל 11 אלף הודעות ב-11 צ'אטים ב-Teams ונתוני ניטור מפוזרים.

עכשיו מיקרוסופט הציבה לעצמה יעד של פתרון תקלות גלובליות תוך שעה בעזרת load shedding, חלוקה גאוגרפית וסוכני AI לדיאגנוסטיקה של התקלות והגורמים שלהן. הנדרסון הודה שבאירוע אחר לקח לתיקון דחוף חמישה עד שישה ימים להיות מוטמע: 'בכל הנוגע לבעיות האבטחה הדחופות ביותר, אנחנו צריכים להגיע מזיהוי להטמעה גלובלית בטוחה תוך שעה. מיותר לציין שאנחנו עדיין לא שם".

articles.title: Teva to lay off 150 employees at Kfar Saba plant
articles.summary: Teva told employees at its Kfar Saba site that it would phase out generic drug R&D there, resulting in 150 layoffs by the end of 2027.
paragraphs: Teva told employees at its Kfar Saba site that it would phase out generic drug R&D there, resulting in 150 layoffs by the end of 2027.

Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd. (NYSE: TEVA; TASE: TEVA) is scaling back operations at its Kfar Saba plant and will lay off 150 employees in generic drug development in 2027. The company told employees at the site today.

Teva said the decision followed a comprehensive review of its global R&D operations aimed at aligning company resources with the needs of its future drug pipeline, which focuses on innovative drugs and biopharmaceuticals, and thereby supporting its strategy. At the same time, as part of what Teva describes as its commitment to Israel, the company is moving ahead with an investment of tens of millions of dollars to strengthen the technology infrastructure and introduce innovations at its Kfar Saba manufacturing plant.
Teva again raises guidance as branded drugs lift revenue
Teva to lay off 250 in API division in Israel

Generic drug R&D at the Kfar Saba site focuses on oral medications and liquid formulations. Teva said the scope of development projects in these areas has narrowed amid limited future demand and that it no longer sees them as drivers of growth.

Teva said it is committed to handling the process respectfully, responsibly and fairly, and to providing employees with support, career guidance, training and help finding new jobs. Some may stay at Teva in other roles. In addition to generic drug R&D, Teva operates a sterile manufacturing plant and a tablet manufacturing plant in Kfar Saba.

Teva said, "Teva’s Kfar Saba manufacturing plant is outside the scope of this move and continues to operate. Teva has begun moving ahead with a significant investment there, amounting to tens of millions of dollars, to strengthen its technology infrastructure and introduce innovations, and is also exploring various options for increasing the investment."

The company added that it employs thousands of people in Israel and conducts management, R&D and other activities at its global headquarters in Tel Aviv, its Abic innovative R&D sites in Netanya, its Kfar Saba plant and its logistics center in Shoham.

The Kfar Saba plant has seen job cuts over the past decade. In 2017, when the company ran into difficulties, more than 100 employees were laid off there, even before the major streamlining program implemented later that year. In 2021, reports said a further 200 or so employees at the site would be laid off or take early retirement. Earlier this year, layoffs were also reported to be expected at TAPI, the raw ingredients division that Teva planned to sell but has so far failed to find a buyer. The cuts there mainly affect the Teva Tech site in the Negev.

articles.title: Zoe Kleinman: Nobody is irreplaceable - unless you're Jensen Huang
articles.summary: The BBC's technology and AI editor on how Nvidia's boss made himself impossible to fire.
paragraphs: Remember the tech boss and his head of HR, both married to other people, who were caught on camera at a Coldplay concert with their arms wrapped around each other?
Their horrified reaction went viral, and the pair both resigned. Astronomer, the firm where they both worked, said their actions had fallen short of its standards.
Compared with the scandal which has engulfed Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang in recent weeks, that Coldplay kiss cam moment now feels rather tame.
Huang admitted to having had an affair, reportedly with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.
There were suggestions that she may have been involved in smuggling Nvidia chips into China, in breach of a US export ban.
Concerns about national security had reached the desk of US President Donald Trump.
There were other stories about some of Huang's relationships with female colleagues.
For most of us, that would without question amount to instant, and irreversible, dismissal.
But while Huang briefly left the company, he was just as swiftly reinstated, and welcomed back with open arms.
As I watched footage of him being greeted with cheers, applause, high fives and a big hug back at the company's HQ on Monday, I wondered how many disgraced bosses would kill to be in his shoes.
"Imagine being that Coldplay CEO reading all the comments on here about how it's OK if you're actually a good enough CEO," quipped menswear writer Derek Guy on X, external.
So, the US AI sector relies on Nvidia, Trump is determined that the American AI industry needs to be the best in the world, and Huang is the only leader the company has ever known.

He's been at the helm for 33 years and he's a computer scientist himself, renowned for being very hands-on with the development process. (Whether the boss's input is always wanted is another matter, but it's always there.)
Working for Huang isn't easy.
Long hours are normal and negative feedback is often given in front of everyone else.

When he wants something to happen, he doesn't stop until it does: one of his early ideas was to halve the chip production cycle, in order to get one step ahead of the competition with their longer lead times for orders.
Lots of experts told him it couldn't be done. Until eventually, they did it.

Not only does Huang have technical expertise, he's also a charismatic figurehead, representing Nvidia at events around the world in his trademark leather jacket, rubbing shoulders with world leaders, royalty, and fellow tech bosses.
For many, he's become something of a cult figure. Nvidia sometimes sells limited edition clothing at conference pop up stalls. A jumper featuring a cartoon image of Huang costs $178 (£137).

articles.title: What will the energy cap changes mean for my bills?
articles.summary: Regulator Ofgem is raising the cap affecting the energy bills of millions of households.
paragraphs: Image source, Getty Images
Energy bills are to soar in January, as prices governed by regulator Ofgem's cap rise at the coldest time of the year.
The cap affects millions of people in England, Scotland and Wales, and reflects higher wholesale gas costs which have been pushed up by the US-Israel war with Iran.
It means people on variable tariffs should give an accurate meter reading, ensure they are receiving all the support to which they are entitled, and take care over energy use.
What is the energy cap and how is it changing?
The energy cap fixes the maximum amount which customers on standard variable tariffs can be charged for each unit of gas and electricity used.
It covers more than 20 million households in England, Wales and Scotland and is set by the regulator Ofgem every three months, external.
It affects those paying by direct debit, by standard credit (they pay when they get a bill), or prepayment meters in slightly different ways.
Most of the increase in the energy price cap has, and will be, driven by higher gas prices.
The government's decision to temporarily remove VAT from domestic electricity bills has cut about £45 a year from a typical bill.
Meanwhile, millions of households will receive a £100 automatic payment to help cover winter costs.
Customers' actual bills depend on the amount of energy they use and how they pay for it.
From January, for those on variable tariffs:
For electricity, average unit prices will go up on 1 January from 26.32p per kilowatt-hour to 32.69p
Gas will increase from 7.97p per kilowatt-hour to 10.96p, higher than in the wake of the invasion of Ukraine
Daily standing charges will be 54.77p for electricity and 29.65p for gas
The roughly 11 million households on fixed tariffs will not see their prices change until the end of their fixed term.
Ofgem regulates the energy market in England, Scotland and Wales. Northern Ireland has a separate system.
What is a typical household?

As well as how much energy you use and how you pay for it, where you live, the type of property you have, how energy efficient it is, how many people live there, and the weather all make a difference.
The Ofgem cap is illustrated using "typical" household energy use in a year with a single bill for gas and electricity settled by direct debit.
The vast majority of people pay their bill this way to help spread payments across the year.
In July, Ofgem reduced what it believes to be a "typical" level of energy use, because many homes have cut back due to high prices in recent years while energy efficiency has improved.
Its new estimate is 9,500 kWh of gas and 2,500 kWh of electricity a year.
Should I take a meter reading when the energy cap changes?
Submitting a meter reading when the cap changes means you are not charged for estimated usage at the wrong rate.
This is especially important when prices go up.
Customers with working smart meters do not need to submit a reading as their bill is calculated automatically.
What are standing charges and how are they changing?

Ofgem also controls standing charges, which are a fixed daily fee to cover the costs of connecting households to gas and electricity supplies. These vary slightly by region, external and payment method.
Between 1 October and 31 December 2026, average standing charges for direct debit customers are 54.83p a day for electricity and 29.68p a day for gas.
From January, daily standing charges will be 54.77p for electricity and 29.65p for gas.
The electricity standing charge is lower than the amount charged over the previous three months, while the gas charge is largely unchanged.

Campaigners have long argued that standing charges are unfair because they make up a bigger proportion of the bill for low-energy households. Others say it just shifts the cost from one part of the bill to another rather than cutting it.
The government has announced plans to remove gas standing charges, although no details have been published on how that will happen
Should I fix my energy prices?
Fixed deals provide certainty for a set period – often a year, or longer – but if energy prices drop while you are on the deal, you could be stuck at a higher price.
You may also have to pay a penalty to leave a fixed deal early if you change your mind.
Experts recommend checking whole-of-market energy price comparison sites to help find the best deal and studying the details of exit fees.
What else has changed about the way energy bills are calculated?

Since 1 April, energy bill charges related to the low-income household insulation scheme - called the Energy Company Obligation - have been scrapped, and for three years, renewable energy projects will be 75%-funded by general taxation instead of a levy on energy bills.
Nearly everyone in England, Wales and Scotland will benefit from this cut, although the amounts will vary between households.
However, the cost of maintaining and strengthening energy network infrastructure like power lines, cables and gas pipes is rising.

In December 2025, Ofgem approved a £28bn investment to improve the electricity and gas grids in Great Britain to strengthen energy supplies and protect customers against volatile energy prices. It will also reduce Britain's dependence on gas.
Customers will pay part of the cost of the upgrade, through an additional £108 added to energy bills by 2031.
These charges started to appear from April 2026, adding about £6 a month to the bill for a typical household covered by the energy cap.
What help can I get with energy bills?
Suppliers must offer customers affordable payment plans or repayment holidays if they are struggling to pay their bills. Most also offer hardship grants.
Since the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022, bills have gone up by about 70% compared with the pre-crisis norm, and since then unpaid bills and charges have shot up.
Vanessa Northam, director at debt charity StepChange, has advice for people who may be struggling:
Take stock of all household money coming in and going out.
Look closely at how much energy you are using, and be alert to estimated bills, which might prove to be inaccurate.
Tell your supplier if you think you are going to struggle.
It is often best to try to talk to someone who can fully understand your situation.
Energy UK has a list of support schemes., external
What is happening to the price of heating oil?

Heating oil is not covered by the energy cap. About 1.5 million UK households use heating oil and they have already seen a sharp increase in bills since the Middle East conflict triggered a jump in oil prices. Some users have seen costs more than double.
The issue is particularly acute in Northern Ireland, where about 500,000 homes use heating all, almost two-thirds of all households.
In March, the government announced a £53m support package to help low-income households in rural communities who use heating oil.

articles.title: Desperate measures: Katzman's Norstar offers shares at huge discount
articles.summary: As Chaim Katzman tries desperately to save his real estate empire, shares of Norstar Holdings, through which he controls G City, have plummeted.
paragraphs: As Chaim Katzman tries desperately to save his real estate empire, shares of Norstar Holdings, through which he controls G City, have plummeted.

The crisis in Chaim Katzman’s real estate empire is deepening. In a desperate move following the failure of a convertible bond offering at the end of last week, Norstar Holdings (TASE: NSTR), the company through which Katzman controls income producing real estate company G City (TASE: GCT), is seeking to raise NIS 80 million at a massive 60% discount on this morning’s base share price.

The shares offered, at NIS 2 each, will represent 40% of the company. The company will allocate warrants to the investors at no cost, bringing the effective value of the share to just NIS 0.36, 93% below the share price on the eve of the announcement of the offering.

Following the announcement, Norstar’s share price has plummeted by over 50% trading, bringing the company's market cap to a low of only NIS 155 million. The company’s bonds are once again trading at double-digit junk yields: its Series 13 bonds are traded at a yield to maturity of 20% (with a duration of less than one year), while the Series 14 bonds are at a yield of about 13%.

This capital raise comes at a time when Norstar needs cash to meet its near-term obligations, and as the market prices in a debt crisis. This comes against the backdrop of a sustained decline in the share price of G City, following the collapse of a deal to transfer control from Norstar to Ari Real Estate, an income-producing real estate company owned by Tzachi Abu, which was called off last August.

The sharp drop in the share price of G City, which has lost over 40% of its value since the initial reports of a deal taking shape between Abu and Katzman, has complicated Katzman’s efforts to inject capital into Norstar. These efforts included a series of planned initiatives, such as the flotation G City’s subsidiary Noga Properties, and the issue of convertible bonds by Norstar, plans from which the company has since retreated.

"I am aware of the concern and I understand it," Katzman said in a G City investor call following the release of the company’s third quarter financials. "I understand the curiosity, as well as the market's nervousness, about asset sales and financing. We have done this before, we are doing it now, and we will continue to do so in the future. We know this business and the players; we know how to do it, and we have the right people for that."
Published by Globes, Israel business news - en.globes.co.il - on November 25, 2026.

articles.title: מפתחים Deep Tech ומחפשים משקיעים ולקוחות? זה בשבילכם
articles.summary: מסחור טכנולוגיות Deep Tech הוא תהליך מורכב. סטארטאפים רבים מתחילים את דרכם עם היכרות מוגבלת של הלקוחות והשוק הפוטנציאלי, גישה מצומצמת למקבלי החלטות בתאגידים והצעת ערך ומודל עסקי שעדיין דורשים חידוד לפני כניסה לשוק. הם לא צריכים רק צ'ק או חיבור למשקיע נוסף, אלא זקוקים לשותף אסטרטגי שמסוגל ללוות אותם לאורך הדרך, מהמעבדה אל השוק. […]
paragraphs: תוכנית עבודה מותאמת אישית לכל סטארטאפ בהתאם לצוות, לשוק ולטכנולוגיה שלו (צילום: Drive TLV)

מסחור טכנולוגיות Deep Tech הוא תהליך מורכב. סטארטאפים רבים מתחילים את דרכם עם היכרות מוגבלת של הלקוחות והשוק הפוטנציאלי, גישה מצומצמת למקבלי החלטות בתאגידים והצעת ערך ומודל עסקי שעדיין דורשים חידוד לפני כניסה לשוק. הם לא צריכים רק צ'ק או חיבור למשקיע נוסף, אלא זקוקים לשותף אסטרטגי שמסוגל ללוות אותם לאורך הדרך, מהמעבדה אל השוק.

תוכנית FastLane של Drive TLV נבנתה במענה לאתגרים האלה. היא פועלת משני צדי השוק: מצד אחד היא מסייעת לסטארטאפים למסחר טכנולוגיות, ומצד שני עובדת עם תאגידים המחפשים פתרונות לאתגרים עסקיים וטכנולוגיים. החיבור הזה מאפשר ליזמים להיחשף לצרכים אמיתיים בתעשייה, לפגוש מקבלי החלטות ולבחון את הפוטנציאל המסחרי של הטכנולוגיה שלהם. המודל הזה מסייע לגשר על "עמק המוות" של ה-Deep Tech: הפער שבין טכנולוגיה שהוכיחה את עצמה לבין פתרון שהשוק מוכן לאמץ ולשלם עבורו.

התוכנית כוללת משלחות עסקיות בינלאומיות לארה"ב ולאירופה, תוכנית פיתוח עסקי מותאמת אישית, ליווי אישי על ידי יועצים מנוסים ומפגשים ישירים עם מנהלים בכירים בתאגידים (פעילותה הבינלאומית של Drive TLV כוללת גם את יפן והודו). בנוסף, משתתפים ייחשפו למסלול השקעה פוטנציאלי באמצעות Next Gear Ventures, שהשקיעה בכמחצית מהסטארטאפים שהשתתפו ב-FastLane. הקרן מביאה לתוכנית מומחיות טכנולוגית ועסקית לצד השקעה וליווי אסטרטגי. במקביל, Drive TLV מחברת את החברות לתאגידים ולשותפים תעשייתיים גלובליים, ומאפשרת להן לבחון את הטכנולוגיות בסביבה תעשייתית אמיתית, לבצע POCs ולקדם שיתופי פעולה מסחריים.
המחזור הקרוב של FastLane יתקיים במשך שישה חודשים, מדצמבר 2026 ועד יוני 2027. ההרשמה פתוחה עד סוף נובמבר 2026. מועמדויות שיוגשו לאחר מכן ייבחנו למחזור הבא, שצפוי להיפתח במהלך השנה הקרובה.
מה כוללת תוכנית FastLane?

כדי להגיש מועמדות לתכנית FastLane, עליכם לפעול באחד או יותר מששת תחומי הטכנולוגיה המרכזיים של Drive TLV: אנרגיה וחשמול, Physical AI ורובוטיקה, Smart Mobility, שבבים ומחשוב, בינה מלאכותית ולמידת מכונה, קישוריות וסייבר. המשתתפים יעבדו על תיקוף הביקוש, חידוד המודל העסקי והצעת הערך, בניית קשרים עם לקוחות ושותפים והצגת הסיפור המסחרי בפני משקיעים. הערך הייחודי של התוכנית טמון בחמישה מרכיבים מרכזיים:

גישה ישירה למקבלי החלטות בכירים בתאגידים: באמצעות משלחות עסקיות בינלאומיות, היזמים נפגשים עם מנהלים בכירים בחברות מובילות בעולם – הן ברשת השותפים הקיימת של Drive TLV והן בעשרות תאגידים נוספים שעמם היא מקיימת קשר רציף. מפגשים אלה מאפשרים לתקף טכנולוגיות, להבין צרכים עסקיים וליצור קשרים מסחריים משמעותיים.
תובנות שוק אמיתיות: Drive TLV פועלת בממשק שבין תאגידים, יועצים ויזמים, ומספקת לחברות המשתתפות תובנות על צורכי התעשייה והביקוש בשוק.
חידוד הסיפור המסחרי של החברה: היזמים מקבלים תמיכה ממוקדת בחידוד הצעת הערך, המודל העסקי והמסרים המיועדים ללקוחות ולמשקיעים.
גישה לרשת מומחים: המשתתפים נהנים מגישה לרשת היועצים והמומחים של Drive TLV, הכוללת יזמים מנוסים ואנשי תעשייה שבנו והובילו חברות.
קהילת יזמים לטווח ארוך: FastLane מציעה גישה לקהילת יזמים, למרחב עבודה משותף, לפורומים של מנכ"לים ולרשת קשרים שממשיכה לתמוך בחברות גם לאחר סיום התוכנית.

בשונה מתוכניות האצה מסורתיות, FastLane מתמקדת במסחור ולא במנטורינג המבוסס על הרצאות, והיא בונה תוכנית עבודה מותאמת אישית לכל סטארטאפ בהתאם לצוות, לשוק ולטכנולוגיה שלו. מאז הקמתה, התוכנית ליוותה 74 סטארטאפים לאורך 11 מחזורים, מחברות בשלבים מוקדמים ועד חברות שהפכו לציבוריות. בוגריה גייסו במצטבר יותר מ-2.5 מיליארד דולר מאז שהצטרפו. התוכנית יצרה יותר מ-200 שיתופי פעולה מסחריים מתמשכים בין תאגידים לסטארטאפים, ו-13 חברות בוגרות ביצעו אקזיט. ההשתתפות אינה כרוכה בתשלום, והיא מבוססת על הקצאת אקוויטי.

"זיהוי הזדמנות כבר אינו מספיק ב-Deep Tech", אומר דניאל לוי קורי, מנכ"ל Drive TLV. "נדרשת הבנה טכנולוגית עמוקה, יכולת להעריך היתכנות מדעית והנדסית, וסבלנות להתמודד עם מחזורי פיתוח ארוכים, רגולציה ואתגרי מסחור. המודל הייחודי של התוכנית, המשלב בין קרן הון-סיכון לבין פלטפורמה פעילה לחיבור לתעשייה ולמסחור טכנולוגיות, מאפשר ליזמים לא רק לפתח טכנולוגיה – אלא גם להפחית סיכונים ולבנות את הדרך לאימוץ מסחרי".
