articles.title: Defense procurement reform underway
articles.summary: A central element is to award tenders to more than one winner, to boost competition and reduce delays in delivery.
paragraphs: A central element is to award tenders to more than one winner, to boost competition and reduce delays in delivery.

Upon assuming his position, the director general of the Ministry of Defense, Major General (Res.) Amir Baram, outlined three key reforms: expanding defense exports; turning the Rehabilitation Division into a national authority; and significantly upgrading defense procurement processes.

The first two initiatives have already been implemented, and now, with the submission of the findings of the committee led by Major General (Res.) Amir Abulafia, a former head of the Planning Directorate, substantial progress has been made on procurement programs.

In recent years, several internal committees in the Ministry of Defense have addressed the issue of defense procurement, but only within the ministry itself. The Abulafia committee therefore specifically examined the interfaces between the ministry and the IDF, where processes are led, in parallel with the ministry’s director general, by Deputy Chief of Staff Major General Tamir Yadai. Over the course of about six months, the Abulafia committee analyzed the relationship between the supplier and the purchaser. On the ministry’s side, it examined the Directorate of Procurement (Manhar) and the Directorate of Defense Research and Development (Mafat), while on the IDF side it looked at the various service branches and the general staff.

The review spanned the entire process, from the specification of the need, to the approval processes, to the suppliers, to implementation. The committee’s broad conclusions were submitted to Baram in the summer. Since then, a process of refining these conclusions has taken place-with the director general and the deputy chief of staff selecting specific recommendations and putting them into action. Within the ministry, there is a growing recognition that while defense procurement processes in the Western world tend to be cumbersome, with everyone seeking ways to streamline and shorten them, countries in the East leverage centralized leadership to move forward rapidly. It was therefore considered necessary to determine how to accelerate procurement.

The conclusions that the committee reached address, first and foremost, the problematic nature of relying on a single contract model. Instead, the Ministry of Defense intends to shift toward tenders with two or more winning bidders, an approach designed to ensure redundancy, faster delivery, and greater competition.

At the same time, the long-standing practice of procurement via tender exemptions is due to disappear. Although some matters will inevitably remain tied to a single supplier - such as the Iron Dome system, which no company other than Rafael produces - in most procurement cases, reliance on a single supplier can be avoided.

Within the IDF, the requesting units are being required to reduce over-specification. Many of the requirements originally established by the IDF to mitigate risks have, in practice, become barriers to competition. At the same time, the Ministry of Defense intends to resort much more to off-the-shelf products rather than new development, in order to avoid delays and unnecessary costs.

One particularly interesting development to watch will be the strengthening of enforcement. For years, a norm has persisted whereby certain suppliers fail to meet delivery deadlines, offering a variety of excuses that are nonetheless accepted.

Senior officials at the Ministry of Defense have become tired of this situation, and will show much less patience for such lapses. Instead, there will be a broader range of suppliers, with a more flexible, need-based evaluation process rather than a rigid, uniform approach. Furthermore, plans are in place to launch an extensive online platform that will be much more comprehensive than the current Market portal via which requesting units will be able to procure a wide range of products.
Published by Globes, Israel business news - en.globes.co.il - on November 25, 2026.
Ministry of Defense director general Amir Baram credit: Elad Malka, Ministry of Defense

articles.title: דוח ה-AI של שירות התעסוקה: 211% יותר מתכנתים דורשי עבודה
articles.summary: פעם אמרו שכלי AI לא יחליפו מתכנתים, אלא רק "יהפכו אותם ליעילים יותר" או "יחליפו את מי שלא משתמש ב-AI". ובכן, דוח חדש שמפרסם היום (ד') שירות התעסוקה מצייר תמונה קצת יותר מורכבת לעובדים בתעשיית ההייטק המקומית. לפי הנתונים, 56% מהשימוש שנבדק ב-Claude במקצוע "פיתוח התוכנה וניתוח היישומים" מוגדר כ"אוטומציה", כלומר האצלת ביצוע המשימה למערכת, […]
paragraphs: פעם אמרו שכלי AI לא יחליפו מתכנתים, אלא רק "יהפכו אותם ליעילים יותר" או "יחליפו את מי שלא משתמש ב-AI". ובכן, דוח חדש שמפרסם היום (ד') שירות התעסוקה מצייר תמונה קצת יותר מורכבת לעובדים בתעשיית ההייטק המקומית.
לפי הנתונים, 56% מהשימוש שנבדק ב-Claude במקצוע "פיתוח התוכנה וניתוח היישומים" מוגדר כ"אוטומציה", כלומר האצלת ביצוע המשימה למערכת, לעומת 44% בלבד מהשימוש שנעשה לצורך סיוע להם.

על פי הדוח, בין אוקטובר 2022 (קצת לפני הפריצה הגדולה של כלי ה-AI) לאוקטובר 2026, מספר דורשי העבודה בקרב "מפתחי תוכנה ומנתחי יישומים" זינק ב-211%, מ-2,863 ל-8,901 איש (שמהווים כ-5.5% מכלל דורשי העבודה). לשם השוואה, מספר דורשי העבודה הרשומים בשירות התעסוקה עלה באותה תקופה ב-14% בלבד. אבל לא רק אצל מפתחים: גם בקרב אנשי דאטה-בייס ורשתות נרשמה מגמה דומה. מספר דורשי העבודה בתחום כמעט שילש את עצמו, וקפץ מ-487 באוקטובר 2022 ל-1,460 בחודש שעבר. בקרב הקבוצה שמכונה בדוח "הנדסאים, טכנאים, סוכנים ובעלי משלח יד נלווה" שיעור האוטומציה, כלומר האצלת משימות למערכת, מגיע ל-43.6%; ואצל מנהלי IT הנתון נע בין 34% ל-39%.

הדוח של שירות התעסוקה נשען על המדד הכלכלי של Anthropic, מדד שמנתח באילו משימות מקצועיות נעשה שימוש ב-Claude, ומסווג אותן לשתי קטגוריות מרכזיות: "אוטומציה", כלומר העברת ביצוע המשימה למערכת במקום העובד; ו"אוגמנטציה", כלומר שימוש שרק מסייע לעובדים. עם זאת, חשוב להדגיש שהחלוקה הזו לא מעידה בהכרח על החלפת עובדים בפועל.

הנתונים חושפים פער גדול בין עולמות הפיתוח והעיצוב לבין מקצועות מסורתיים יותר. בזמן שבקרב מעצבים גרפיים ומעצבי מולטימדיה שיעור האוטומציה מגיע ל-51%, אצל המשפטנים למשל, רוב השימוש (74%) הוא לצורך סיוע, ורק 16% הוא אוטומציה. מגמה דומה נרשמה גם בקרב מקצועות "צווארון לבן" אחרים כמו יועצי אשראי והלוואות עם 85% שימוש מסייע, ויועצים פיננסיים עם 71%.

אם יוצאים רגע מהפוקוס על ההייטק, אנחנו רואים שהחשיפה ל-AI לא מוגבלת להייטק, כשמספר דורשי העבודה במקצועות עם חשיפה גבוהה ל-AI גדל ב-51.9% מאז ינואר 2022 והגיע ל-38 אלף איש באוקטובר 2026, שהם 23.4% מכלל דורשי העבודה. לשם השוואה, במקצועות שלא נצפתה בהם חשיפה ל-AI נרשמה דווקא ירידה של 23.3%. החשיפה הגבוהה ביותר ל-AI נרשמת בקרב דורשי עבודה בגיל 40 ובעיקר בקרב אקדמאים, כאשר מחוז תל אביב מוביל בפער ניכר עם שיעור חשיפה ל-AI של 46.3%, לעומת 18.3% בלבד במחוז הדרום.

עם זאת, בשירות התעסוקה מדגישים שהנתונים משקפים שינוי בהרכב המקצועי של הנרשמים, ולא בהכרח שה-AI הוא זה שגרם לעלייה. התקופה כללה נזכיר גם כמה זעזועים ביטחוניים (ועלייה בשער הדולר) שהקפיצו זמנית את מספר דורשי העבודה, אבל הפער בין הקבוצות נשמר.

articles.title: Strauss launches streamlining program
articles.summary: The food company is reallocating resources to production, expansion of operations in Brazil and Eastern Europe, and entry into additional food categories.
paragraphs: A month after presenting its business strategy for the coming years, food company Strauss Group (TASE: STRS), headed by CEO Shai Babad, is embarking on an efficiency program. The aim is to reduce management layers and achieve annual pre-tax savings of approximately NIS 100 million. The plan, approved yesterday (Tuesday) by the board of directors and disclosed alongside the company’s third quarter 2026 financial results, is set to commence in early 2027 and to be implemented over the course of the year.

The company plans to reallocate resources to investment in production capacity, its supply chain, automation, and expansion into international markets. The report provides no detail on how many positions will be cut, but it emphasizes that the cuts will affect operations both in Israel and abroad.

This marks the third wave of layoffs at Strauss within four years. In November 2022, following the salmonella crisis and ahead of Babad’s appointment as CEO, the group approved an efficiency plan that called for the dismissal of about 150 employees, mostly in head office roles, aimed at generating annual savings of up to NIS 80 million. In January 2024, Strauss announced the layoff of another 150 employees, primarily in the management ranks, as part of a move designed to save NIS 50 million annually. The current efficiency plan is intended to yield even greater savings for the company than the previous two. Strauss has over 13,000 employees in Israel, and several thousand more in its international operations.

The strategic plan for 2027-2030 unveiled last month includes investment of over NIS 2 billion in Israel, primarily in manufacturing plants and production infrastructure, and the expansion of operations in Brazil and Eastern Europe, and entry into additional food categories. The company targeted average growth of 7-9% in annual net profit.

Meanwhile, Strauss has concluded another quarter in which a decline in raw material costs has translated into improved profitability, despite a drop in sales. The group’s revenue totaled NIS 3 billion, 8.4% less than in in the corresponding quarter of quarter last year.
Selling fewer snacks and sweets, yet earning more

Strauss’s food and beverage operations in Israel saw a 2.9% decline in revenue, to NIS 1.37 billion, with all three business segments reporting a drop in sales. Nevertheless, operating profit from local operations rose by 21.2% to NIS 177 million.

This shift is particularly notable in the snacks and sweets category, in which Strauss’s sales fell by 4.2% to NIS 350 million, primarily due to a decline in sales volume. Nevertheless, the segment's operating profit surged by 140% to NIS 35 million. This is partly attributable to price increases implemented by the company last year in response to rising raw material costs (in the past quarter, the average global market price of cocoa was 21% lower than in the corresponding quarter of 2025).

A similar trend was observed in the coffee business in Israel, in which sales fell by 1.5%, yet operating profit climbed by 54% to NIS 46 million, thanks to strengthening of the shekel and efficiency measures. Meanwhile, as recently reported in "Globes", supermarket chain Shufersal is expanding its independent coffee imports, a market in which Strauss currently holds a dominant position through its Elite brands.

Conversely, in the Health and Wellness segment, which includes the dairy business, Strauss recorded a 2.6% decline in sales and a 6.2% drop in operating profit. Strauss attributes this decline to the discontinuation of the distribution of certain chilled products, as well as reduced production volumes resulting from ongoing quality control and assurance processes.
Price reductions in Brazil erode revenue

In contrast to the coffee business in Israel, in the Brazilian market the decline in prices of raw materials is reflected in lower selling prices. Revenue from Strauss’s International Coffee segment fell by 15.1% to NIS 1.39 billion, impacted by price reductions and the strengthening of the shekel against the currencies of the countries in which the company operates. Operating profit declined by 6.2% to NIS 152 million, even though the operating profit margin improved.

Strauss continues to expand its operations in Brazil beyond the coffee market. In September, the company, through its Três Corações joint venture, completed the acquisition of food company Yoki, which makes the snacks, dry foods, and cooking and seasoning products. At the time the deal was announced, the annual sales of the acquired company were estimated at NIS 1.2 billion.

The financial statements indicate that, following adjustments, the acquisition consideration was revised to NIS 467 million, and that the transaction yielded a one-time gain for Strauss of NIS 101 million that is not included in the management results.

The water division was the only one of the group’s segments to post sales growth for the quarter. Its revenue rose by 5.7% to NIS 247 million, primarily thanks to an increase in the customer base and the specific product mix sold. Operating profit totaled NIS 24 million.

The company's board of directors has approved a share buyback program of up to NIS 50 million, as part of a framework that allows for additional share repurchases (up to NIS 200 million) until the end of 2030. Since the beginning of the year, the company has distributed dividends totaling NIS 430 million.
Published by Globes, Israel business news - en.globes.co.il - on November 25, 2026.

articles.title: פיצ'ר האפליקציות החדש של אנת'רופיק הוא איום ישיר על אפל וגוגל
articles.summary: בשנה האחרונה נדמה שבכל פעם ש-Anthropic משיקה פיצ'ר חדש ל-Claude, האינטרנט ממהר כבר להספיד תעשיות שלמות ולהכניס את הבורסות ברחבי העולם לסחרור. אבל הפעם, אנת'רופיק מכוונת את התותחים שלה למקום אחר לגמרי, עם פיצ'ר חדש שיסייע אולי למשתמשים, אבל עשוי גם לאיים על חנויות האפליקציות של אפל וגוגל. כל אחד יכול ליצור ולפרסם אפליקציה אם […]
paragraphs: בשנה האחרונה נדמה שבכל פעם ש-Anthropic משיקה פיצ'ר חדש ל-Claude, האינטרנט ממהר כבר להספיד תעשיות שלמות ולהכניס את הבורסות ברחבי העולם לסחרור. אבל הפעם, אנת'רופיק מכוונת את התותחים שלה למקום אחר לגמרי, עם פיצ'ר חדש שיסייע אולי למשתמשים, אבל עשוי גם לאיים על חנויות האפליקציות של אפל וגוגל.
כל אחד יכול ליצור ולפרסם אפליקציה

אם אתם משתמשים ב-Claude, סביר להניח שאתם מכירים את Artifacts. אותה יכולת של קלוד לענות לכם לא רק בטקסט, אלא באמצעות סוג של מסמך או כלי חיצוני שהוא בונה עבורכם. ממסמכים, דרך מצגות, דאשבורדים, אנימציות, דפי נחיתה או מיני-אפליקציות. אתם יכולים לשתף את ה-Artifacts שלכם עם חברים, עובדים ובני משפחה, אבל עד כה, האלמנטים האלה חיו בתוך אפליקציית Claude.

עכשיו, כל זה משתנה עם פיצ'ר Install as app, שמאפשר לכם להפוך את ה-Artifacts שלכם לאפליקציות דסקטופ ב-Windows או ב-Mac. זה אומר של-Artifact שלכם יהיה אייקון משל עצמו כמו כל אפליקציה אחרת במחשב שלכם, וכשתלחצו עליו, הוא ייפתח בחלון משלו. כל אפליקציה שכזאת מתעדכנת באופן אוטומטי בכל פעם שתערכו את ה-Artifact המקורי, והיא יכולה לשלוח לכם התראות. לכל אפליקציה יש גם 3 רמות של הרשאות: הראשונה מאפשרת לה לעשות כל מה שהיא הייתה יכולה לעשות בדפדפן; השנייה מאפשרת לה לבקש הרשאות נוספות כמו שליחת התראות, יצירת חלונות וכו'; והאחרונה מאפשרת לאפליקציה לקרוא, לשנות או למחוק קבצים על המחשב שלכם מבלי לשאול בכל פעולה. לאחר עדכון האפליקציה תתבקשו לאשר מחדש את ההרשאות, גם אם אתם עצמכם ערכתם אותה. עם זאת, רכיבים באפליקציה שמגיעים מאתר חיצוני יכולים להשתנות בלי בקשת אישור נוספת. אם זה נשמע לכם כמו מתכון לאסון ולהפצה מהירה של נוזקות, באנת'רופיק מסבירים שאתם יכולים לתת את אם-כל-ההרשאות הזו רק לאפליקציה שיצרתם בעצמכם, או במסלולי Team ו-Enterprise, לאפליקציה שיצרו אנשים בארגון שלכם.

מה שכן כדאי לקחת בחשבון, זה שכל בקשה של האפליקציה לקלוד תגרע לכם כמובן מהמכסה של המינוי שלכם, ושבאנת'רופיק מבהירים שהם לא מבצעים כל תהליך של אישור אפליקציות. זה אומר שאתם צריכים לחשוב פעמיים לפני שאתם נותנים גישה מלאה לאפליקציות שכאלו. בנוסף, לא כל סוגי ה-Artifacts ניתנים להתקנה: מסמכים, מצגות וגיליונות של Claude אינם נתמכים.

בשביל להפוך Artifact לאפליקציה אתם רק צריכים ללחוץ על "Install as app" בתפריט השיתוף. אין שום שימוש ב-API Key, אין שום צורך בהרשמה מיוחדת. פשוט להתקין ברגע. כדי לפתוח את האפליקציה צריך להיות מחוברים לרשת ולחשבון ה-Claude שלכם, כך שלא כולם סתם יכולים להתחיל להשתמש בה.
מי יצטרך אפליקציות?

הצעד החדש הוא איום פוטנציאלי על הקונספט של חנויות האפליקציות כמו App Store של אפל ו-Google Play של גוגל. כרגע מדובר באפליקציות ל-Mac ול-Windows, ולא בחלופה להתקנת אפליקציות באייפון או באנדרואיד, אבל עדיין – תשאלו כל מפתח כמה מעצבנים תהליכי הבקרה והאישור של גוגל ואפל, ואתם כנראה תבינו למה אנת'רופיק מביאה כאן בשורה מאוד מעניינת שעשויה לבנות סביבה תעשייה חדשה. בנוסף, אם אתם יכולים לבנות לעצמכם אפליקציה מותאמת אישית, לא בטוח שתצטרכו ללכת להוריד ולשלם על אפליקציה חיצונית. האם אנחנו בדרך לאפסטור של אנת'רופיק? ימים יגידו.

הפיצ'ר החדש מופץ בהדרגה בבטא בכל המסלולים. אם אתם בתוכנית Team, הוא כבר מופעל כברירת מחדל, אך הגישה המלאה למחשב כבויה כברירת מחדל. אם אתם בתוכנית Enterprise, הוא כבוי כברירת מחדל, כך שתצטרכו לבקש מהאדמין שלכם להפעיל אותו.

articles.title: Colombia’s president arrives at scene of supermarket hostage siege in tourist city
articles.summary: Abelardo de la Espriella to take control of operation trying to free at least 20 hostages Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, a popular tourist city. Abelardo de la Espriella’s motorcade arrived in Cartagena on Tuesday night, Agence France-Presse reported, where he will ostensibly take control of an operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces. Continue reading...
paragraphs: Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, a popular tourist city.

Abelardo de la Espriella’s motorcade arrived in Cartagena on Tuesday night, Agence France-Presse reported, where he will ostensibly take control of an operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces.
About 30 people were initially seized by the armed men early on Tuesday morning, but by nightfall, 10 hostages – five of them elderly women – had been released, police said.
There have been no reports of injuries so far.

Before arriving in Cartagena, the rightwing president said that, despite the context of growing violence perpetrated by criminal groups involved in the country’s decades-long armed conflict, the hostage-taking appeared to have stemmed from a botched robbery carried out by “common criminals”.
The past few days have been particularly challenging in the South American country, with a car bomb and a drone attack killing one person and leaving nearly 30 injured.

The supermarket where the hostages are being held is just six miles from the old city and its 500-year-old fortress walls overlooking the Caribbean. Hundreds of thousands of visitors are drawn to Cartagena every year.

The gunmen reportedly arrived at about 8.30am local time at an Éxito supermarket in La Castellana neighbourhood and, according to Colombia’s president, the group planned to rob an armoured cash-in-transit vehicle that was due to collect the previous day’s takings from the store.
After spotting the movement on security cameras, employees reportedly alerted the national police, who surrounded the supermarket.

“My son is there,” Jacob Pérez, the father of one of the workers reportedly held hostage, told Agence France-Presse. “He didn’t leave work and he’s not answering his phone. I think they took it from him,” he said.
Customers were also believed to be among the hostages. The five people initially released were “older women”, according to De la Espriella.

Footage shared on social media showed dozens of people rushing out of the supermarket, while local media outlets showed snipers positioned on nearby buildings in what appeared to be a standoff between the armed men and police.

De la Espriella, known for his populist rhetoric and an “iron fist” approach to crime – he sometimes wears a gun on his waist and has posed beside the bodies of people killed by police – has been in office for just over three months, and said the hours-long standoff at the supermarket “will turn out well for the hostages, but I’m not so sure it will turn out quite so well for the hostage-takers”.

He addressed the case at a press conference in Villavicencio, about 684 miles inland, where he was dealing with the aftermath of an attack on Monday night in which a car bomb was detonated outside the headquarters of the Meta departmental government.
More than 20 people were injured, and the president attributed the attack to a dissident faction of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc).

“Narco-terrorism is desperate because we are confronting it decisively. It intends to intimidate us and force us to retreat in search of another false peace process,” the president said, referring to the landmark 2016 peace deal between the government and the Farc – the 10th anniversary of whose signing was on Tuesday.

Internationally recognised for substantially reducing violence, the deal alone could not bring the decades-long armed conflict to a definitive end. Subsequent administrations were slow to implement the agreement, which was rejected by Farc dissidents and other rebel factions.

In the early hours of Monday, in another part of the country, gunmen believed to belong to the ELN, an armed group that never signed a peace deal, used drones to drop bombs on the local police command in the city of Cúcuta. Instead they hit homes and injured three civilians, including an 18-month-old baby.
Although drone attacks by criminal groups have become increasingly common, it was the first time they had targeted a departmental capital.

articles.title: US attorney general dodges questions about Nvidia investigation
articles.summary: Nvidia's share price have fallen 7% as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's reinstatement.
paragraphs: US Attorney General Todd Blanche has backed Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while refusing to comment on whether the AI chipmaker was under federal investigation.
Blanche said he had no information about newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers demand answers about US President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's comeback.
Huang was given his job back less than two weeks after being forced to resign over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
Asked several times on Tuesday whether the justice department or FBI had investigated Huang, Blanche responded: "I don't know what you're talking about."

Huang is still set to appear before Congress next week, where he will be questioned about national security concerns over his relationship with an alleged spy who previously ran Megaspeed, a Singapore-based corporate customer of Nvidia.
Trump has said he would consider pardoning Huang for any potential criminal activity, though he does not think it will come to that.
"It's always an option, I guess, but I don't think it'll be necessary," Trump told the New York Post in an interview published on Tuesday.
The US commerce department has also announced it was preparing to blacklist the tech company Megaspeed, which has been suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China.
The commerce and justice departments said last week that they began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 "for potential export control violations".
But Blanche told reporters on Tuesday that the latter had "hundreds, if not more" export investigations occurring at any one time.
"So when you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don't know what you're talking about," he said.

Asked if he was satisfied Nvidia had been co-operative with inquiries into whether it or Huang knew about chips being diverted to China, Blanche said: "I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.

"Obviously, if Nvidia was the target or was subject to some criminal investigation or they were obstructing or thwarting our investigation, then that wouldn't be the message that the president is saying to the American people.
"It shouldn't be what my message would be either."
While Nvidia's stock market value surged on the announcement of Huang's reappointment, some of the gains were reversed in volatile Tuesday trading.
The company's share price closed down nearly 6% - still well above where it ended last week. On Monday, Nvidia stock rocketed more than 31% following news of Huang's return.

Huang reportedly apologised to Nvidia employees on Tuesday, the day after returning to the company as chief executive, saying he had made "terrible mistakes" and was now receiving daily 90-minute therapy sessions.
The company's board reinstated Huang on Monday in a shock U-turn. Harvey Jones, its chairman, said Huang's return was in the "best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers".
The board said it had received input from senior levels of the US government and was confident that Huang's reinstatement posed no national security risk.
On Monday, Trump said he had spoken to the company's directors and convinced them to bring back Huang.
Huang's reinstatement provoked bipartisan anger.
Republican Congressman Don Bacon said Nvidia should have "ignored the administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang".
Republican Senator Pete Ricketts said Huang's behaviour "doesn't absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips".

Democratic Congressman Robert Garcia, the incoming chairman of the House Oversight Committee, said Trump's "direct involvement" with Nvidia's decision "raises serious national security and corruption questions".
Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego said Congress needed to "investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement".

articles.title: Trump's rescue of Nvidia's Huang brings political risks
articles.summary: The US president's intercession to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang has inextricably linked their fates.
paragraphs: After the AI chipmaker Nvidia announced it was bringing back embattled former head Jensen Huang and the company's stock shot up like a bullet, President Donald Trump took a very public victory lap.
"I made the deal," he said during a lengthy phone interview with cable business news channel CNBC.

Trump followed that with an AI-generated image posted to his social media platform that riffed on the famous photograph taken moments after the 2024 attempt on his life in Pennsylvania. But instead of Trump in the image, Huang was the one surrounded by Secret Service guards. It depicted him in front of an Nvidia banner - with a raised fist clenching a red bra.
The post was classic Trump – potentially offensive, yet still a bit opaque.

Was Trump suggesting Huang survived a scandal – one that includes allegations of recklessly jeopardising US national security by consorting with a suspected Chinese spy – the way he had survived an assassin's bullet?

Was the bra a celebration Huang's reported extramarital affairs? By replacing the US flag with an Nvidia standard, was he claiming that America and one of its largest, most powerful companies are one and the same?
At the very least, the image underscores how inextricably linked Huang and Trump now are, with the fate of the former hinging on the successes and failures of the latter.
And with that comes significant risks for the American president and for Republicans, including Vice-President JD Vance, who played a key part in his efforts to rescue Huang.

While Trump has said that a "very thorough investigation" by federal officials "exonerated" Huang and his reinstatement poses no national security threat, that is far from the final word on the matter.
"Every time you have a Chinese woman that's good looking or beautiful, they say she's a spy," Trump told CNBC, adding that "with Jensen, I don't believe that's true".
Democrats and some concerned Republicans in Congress have a different view.

They are promising to launch their own oversight of Huang and Nvidia, with subpoenas and compelled witness testimony, in order to assess whether they violated laws by allowing China to access sophisticated microchip technology.
State governments could also launch their own investigations.
Any new revelations could further damage the company's standing – and, by association, Trump himself.
"I have warned the administration from the start about Communist China obtaining our most advanced chips through both smuggling and remote access," Republican Senator Tom Cotton posted on X.
"Congress has much to investigate," he said.
While Huang has a long record of success at Nvidia, there is no guarantee that he can recapture past glory now that has star his dimmed.
Even if he is free from any criminal liability, the tech mogul is about to be in a much harsher spotlight than he has ever experienced.
Trump also appears to be on the wrong side of public opinion when it comes to AI writ large.

In the recent US midterm elections, candidates on both the left and right campaigned on imposing new restrictions on data centre construction, with many calling for new legal guardrails to prevent AI-fuelled economic and social disruption.

"Rather than addressing the American people's growing concerns about AI, this administration remains asleep at the wheel or willfully ignorant as our most advanced technologies fall into the hands of our greatest competitors," congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove, a California Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told the BBC.

The president's own political base is also suspicious of the new technology, with rural conservatives often rebelling at the demands that big tech companies have placed on their local resources and civic infrastructure.

The Nvidia story has also exposed rifts in Trump's own administration, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, a China hawk, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, a vocal proponent of AI, publicly feuding over whether to impose new restrictions on AI chip exports.

Both Bessent and Lutnick travelled with Trump on his recent trip to China, although it was the commerce secretary who hitched a ride back to the White House on the Marine One helicopter when Trump returned to Washington last Thursday.
Polling also indicated that political corruption was a top issue for voters this year.
The president's willingness to intervene in the deliberations of a major private company in which he owns millions of dollars of stock could further fuel those concerns.

Trump's decision to help save Huang – noting on Monday that "we have to protect our geniuses, and he certainly is a genius" – could further inflame the public's sense that the rich and powerful, genius or not, play by a different set of rules.

"It almost feels like they've bent the rule, the regulation, to allow this to happen because it's such an important part of our economy right now," Steve Bannon, a former top Trump adviser, said on his podcast on Monday.
"Even in the crash of 2008... I never saw the government step in and take over a board of directors."
For this American president, however, these risks appear to be worth taking because of the stakes involved.
Trump has long viewed the success of the US economy as a key part of his political legacy.
He boasted of the historic growth and low unemployment during his first presidential term (while glossing over the disruptions caused by the Covid pandemic).
And since returning to office, he has celebrated as major US stock indices posted new record highs.
Recent US economic expansion has been fuelled largely by investment in AI technology, and Trump has become one of the industry's biggest boosters.

He scolded states and local governments for blocking data centre construction and predicted that the nation that wins the race for supremacy in AI – which he has tried to rebrand as "super intelligence" – will control the fate of the world.

If Trump views the economy as the key to his political success and AI as instrumental to the health of the US economy, then his dramatic, precedent-shattering actions to try to rescue Nvidia, the company at the centre of America's AI industry, make more sense.
In the weeks since concerns over Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy first surfaced, Nvidia's stock price tumbled more than 32%.
Last Friday alone, it fell 14%.
US stock indices tumbled as well, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq down 10% last week and the larger S&P 500 dropping 8.6%.

The recent financial turmoil may have given Trump a glimpse into a future where AI growth is just the latest financial bubble – like the housing market in 2008 and internet companies in 2001 – that is due for a resounding pop, with similarly dire economic consequences to follow.
Trump's intervention on behalf of Huang arrested that drop, at least for a day.

On Tuesday, Nvidia's stock price gave back much of the bounce it had enjoyed, and larger stock indices were mixed. The fate of the America economy and the AI juggernaut that has powered it is still undetermined.
Trump's intervention may not be a crisis fully averted, but only a crisis delayed.
And if an AI reckoning does come, the US president will be hard-pressed to avoid being caught in the maelstrom.

articles.title: Why tiny cars are taking off across Europe
articles.summary: Once seen as a car for elderly, rural people, tiny cars are being embraced by a younger demographic.
paragraphs: Selena Buse, 16, reverses her Citroën Ami out of a parking space and heads off past the school playground. Heads turn. The Ami looks pretty remarkable. Futurist or like-a-toaster depending on your point of view. But it's changed her life.
"I got it because I really needed it to get to school. And I use it to visit friends on the weekends. It's indispensable in rural areas like where I live," she says.
In France, you can drive a car like this from the age of 14 with a road safety certificate and eight hours training. In Italy too.
In Germany and Spain it's 15, in the UK 16, external. Because they are classed as motorised quadri-cycles. Four-wheel mopeds in other words.
Registrations have risen from about 13,000 in 2019 to around 25,000 last year in France.

In Europe, sales have gone from 30,000 to 60,000 in the past five years. And the Ami, launched in 2020, has really changed the image, with teenagers who now account for a quarter of all mini-car sales.
In Selena's very small Citroën, we are soon rolling along at the top speed of 45km/h (28mph). For other road users, no-licence cars like this can seem like mobile traffic calming.
"When I'm on faster roads and there's a lot of traffic the cars behind me sometimes honk their horns but I can't go any quicker!" Selena says.
Another local Daniel Laprès, who drives a micro-car made by French firm and market-leader Aixam, tells me he actually pulls over to let the cars behind pass.

He and his wife moved from Paris to this country village two years ago. Of Canadian nationality, he didn't swap his foreign licence for a French one in time and lost the right to drive. That didn't matter much when he was in Paris. Like many Parisians he didn't need a car. He used public transport. But that's not possible here.

"We tried living off of taxis and it was in the end a disaster. Then we heard about how you could drive without having to have a licence, and it was the exact solution to our problem. Cheap, inexpensive to operate, basically no administrative formalities, you get insurance."
However, Laprès feels less safe in his small car. "They're little more than tin cans on wheels, right? I mean, you're not going to be driving fast, but someone else could be."
These cars are forbidden on motorways. But even on medium-fast roads, being considerably slower than the average vehicle can be a problem.

"You go on national highways at your risk and peril. I did it once and I will never, ever do it again. On those roads (speed limit 110km/h), everybody is passing you, including the biggest trucks. And they come at you very fast from the rear, so it's scary," Laprès says.
Daniel is 77 so fits in with the long-established market for these cars: older people living in the countryside.

Traditionally the market also included quite a few people who'd lost their licences, often because of drink-driving offences. But the launch of the electric Citroën Ami in 2020 changed the customer profile and the product.

"The launch of the Ami was the beginning of the transformation of the sector, with more and more electric models coming on to the market. In 2026, more than 67% of new licence-free cars are electric," says Marie-Laure Nivot, market analyst at AAA Data.
This tendency was encouraged by stricter EU regulations on motorised two-wheelers that had been the vehicles of choice for European teenagers until then.

"It proved too costly for manufacturers to apply the new EU rules, so mopeds and small scooters have almost disappeared from the market since 2020 and licence-free cars have taken their place," Marie-Laure Nivot says.
Tiny car sales rose strongly till 2024 although they have flattened since in France with the withdrawal of subsidies for electric models.
Curiously, the arrival in this niche market of a giant competitor in the shape of Stellantis brand Citroën was actually good news for existing French manufacturers like Aixam and Ligier.

"We're specialised in this niche market and we're very good at what we do, but of course, we didn't have the communication strength of a multinational like Stellantis. They helped us to make people understand that it was possible in France to drive this product from 14-years-old, in Germany from 15-years-old. They gave a lot of visibility to our market," says Aixam sales and marketing director Tom Faget.
Aixam has invested €30m (£25m; $33m) in expanding its production capacity in France. And its sales are growing in other European countries, even as the French market slows.

Meanwhile, the competition is producing increasingly sophisticated minicars - some costing as much as a small conventional car. At Ligier, marketing director Romain Illegems says the biggest change is in who's buying them.

"We've gone from mobility that was imposed on people to mobility that people choose. Before, these vehicles were something you used because you absolutely needed to get around, because there was no public transport, or because you didn't have a licence.
"Today, teenagers are choosing them instead of scooters or mopeds, because they're safer and offer better protection from the weather. Young people now account for 40% of our customers."

There are limitations, of course. Just two seats, a maximum speed of 45km/h and no motorways. But for Selena, who rents her Ami for €60 a month, plus insurance, it's a small price to pay for independence.

articles.title: Kilmar Ábrego García, man at center of Trump deportation battle, leaves US
articles.summary: Salvadorian man, who was deported in March 2025 and returned to US after supreme court ruling, leaving of own volition for Spain Kilmar Ábrego García has left the United States of his own volition, his lawyers confirmed on Tuesday, with the Department of Homeland Security confirming that he was travelling to Spain. A source close to Ábrego said Madrid was his first stop but that it would not be his final destination. Continue reading...
paragraphs: Kilmar Ábrego García has left the United States of his own volition, his lawyers confirmed on Tuesday, with the Department of Homeland Security confirming that he was travelling to Spain.
A source close to Ábrego said Madrid was his first stop but that it would not be his final destination.

The Salvadorian immigrant was at the center of a months-long legal battle since he was deported to El Salvador in March 2025 by the Trump administration, in defiance of a court’s protection. He was held in Cecot, a notorious mega-prison.

He was ultimately returned to the US after a decision by the supreme court three months later. Since then, Ábrego has been fighting a second deportation to a series of African countries proposed by Department of Homeland Security (DHS) officials.
The Washington Post reported earlier on Tuesday that he negotiated a deal with federal authorities to depart the US voluntarily in order to avoid being forcibly removed.

In a statement, the US senator Chris Van Hollen, who has advocated for Maryland resident Ábrego and who met with him in El Salvador last year, described him as a “free man” and referenced Ábrego’s agreement with the Trump administration.

“While the Trump Administration had been pursuing their vindictive prosecution against Kilmar and desperately trying to ship him against his will to countries known for human rights abuses, the Administration was forced to come to this agreement that respects Kilmar’s will and the due process rights guaranteed to him and to all in our nation,” Van Hollen said. “I am relieved that he will be safe, in a country of his choosing, and free – including from this Administration’s constant persecution.”

The 31-year-old has an American wife and child and has lived in Maryland for years, but he immigrated to the US illegally as a teenager. In 2019, an immigration judge ruled that he could not be deported to El Salvador because he faced danger there from a gang that had threatened his family. The judge allowed him to live and work in the US under Immigration and Customs Enforcement supervision, but he was not given residency status.

He was arrested in Baltimore in March 2025 and deported to a Salvadorian prison in what an official later called an “administrative error”. Facing public pressure and a court order, the Trump administration brought him back in June 2025, but only after securing an indictment charging him with human smuggling in Tennessee. A federal judge dismissed that case in May, finding that the justice department’s pursuit of criminal charges was designed to punish Ábrego for challenging his deportation. The government is appealing.
The Trump administration vowed to deport him to a third country, threatening to send him to Uganda, Eswatini, Ghana and, most recently, Liberia.

“We will always admire his remarkable courage in staring down and defeating a vindictive prosecution instigated by the highest reaches of the Justice Department,” one of Ábrego’s attorneys, Sean Hecker, said in a statement provided to the Washington Post. “He, in turn, is grateful to those who stood by him.”
Additional reporting by Ashifa Kassam in Madrid and the Associated Press

articles.title: Canada says it ‘does not report to the US’ after Pentagon criticizes military spending
articles.summary: Scathing US document memo supposedly ‘atrophied’ defence capabilities of its northern neighbour Canada is a “sovereign nation” that does not “report” to the United States, the country’s defense minister said after the Pentagon released a scathing memo that criticized the supposedly “atrophied” defence capabilities of its northern neighbour. The document, released on Tuesday, said Canada had “yet to make the hard decisions and tradeoffs” necessary to meet previous defence spending pledges and become a “credible partner in the defense of our shared continent”. Continue reading...
paragraphs: Canada is a “sovereign nation” that does not “report” to the United States, the country’s defense minister said after the Pentagon released a scathing memo that criticized the supposedly “atrophied” defence capabilities of its northern neighbour.

The document, released on Tuesday, said Canada had “yet to make the hard decisions and tradeoffs” necessary to meet previous defence spending pledges and become a “credible partner in the defense of our shared continent”.

The Pentagon memo said it took Canada nearly two decades to finally reach spending promises made in 2006 “despite Canada’s role as a major G7 economy as well as one of the largest and wealthiest members of the NATO alliance”.

Historically, Nato members have fallen short of meeting the security organization’s funding goals. When Russia annexed Crimea in 2014, only three Nato members – the US, the UK and Greece – were meeting the alliance’s guideline of spending 2% of GDP on defence. By 2025, all 31 members with armed forces, including Canada, had reached the goal.

The document also suggested Canada faces significant operational hurdles in its air, land and sea operations, blaming political leaders for pursuing “parochial economic and commercial interests over military optimization”.

The Pentagon document said the US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, was “laser focused” on modernizing Canada’s military, suggesting American taxpayers had been “footing the bill for its defense” for decades.
The defense minister, David McGuinty, told reporters he could not “divine” the thinking behind the Pentagon’s decision to criticise Canada’s defence spending now.

“The amount of cooperation we are pushing under Norad [North American Aerospace Defense Command] has not changed. What we’re doing together at Nato has not changed. Our military-to-military cooperation has not changed. Our work on integrated air missile defence has not changed,” he said.
McGuinty also bristled at the suggestion from a reporter that the memo implied Canada required approval from the US when it came to its spending plans.
“Canada is a sovereign nation. I’ll be very direct. We don’t report to the United States,” he said.
The memo came as a Canadian official travelled to Europe to pitch a new defence bank championed by the prime minister, Mark Carney.

Isabelle Hudon, Canada’s lead negotiator for establishing the Defence, Security and Resilience Bank, is looking to cajole more countries into joining a global initiative that would lend to governments and contractors at low cost to support defense projects.

Ten countries have pledged their support but no others from the G7 have done so yet, with both the UK and Germany so far declining to join. Hudon says the €4bn in commitments secured so far is enough to start the bank up but she is aiming for up to €100bn.

Carney has made significantly increased spending commitments in defence. The country spent $63.4bn on national defence in 2025, meeting its Nato pledge to spend 2% of gross domestic product for the first time.
Last year, Nato members agreed to raise the goal to the equivalent of 5% of GDP by 2035.

Canada’s federal budget this month laid out a plan to spend about 4% of Canada’s GDP on defence and security annually by the end of the decade, and 5% by 2035, including the purchase of submarines and early warning aircraft.

Canada’s air power is a key point of friction with Washington. Carney’s government has yet to make a final decision on its order of F-35 fighter jets from the US firm Lockheed Martin and is weighing the possibility of purchasing Swedish-made Gripen aircraft instead. The multibillion-dollar purchase has been the subject of a political review for more than a year. The Pentagon memo warned that operating a “mixed fleet” of aircraft would “compound existing personnel shortfalls”.

articles.title: World Chess Championship 2026 Game 1: Gukesh Dommaraju and Javokhir Sindarov play to 38-move draw – as it happened
articles.summary: Sindarov and Gukesh play to 38-move draw in Game 1 Explainer: all your pre-match questions, answered Sindarov interview: ‘I can’t play games just for fun’ Play through 22 famous world championship games The players have shaken hands and we’re off! We have a Berlin defense of the Ruy Lopez (1 e4 e5 2 Nf3 Nc6 3 Bb5 Nf6), one of the most thoroughly analyzed openings in modern chess. The Berlin famously helped Vladimir Kramnik dethrone Garry Kasparov in their 2000 world title match in London and has been a staple of elite chess ever since, earning a reputation as one of black’s most reliable…
paragraphs: Everything you need to know about the World Chess Championship

India’s Gukesh Dommaraju is defending the world chess championship against fast-rising Uzbek grandmaster Javokhir Sindarov in the youngest title match in the competition’s 140-year history. The best-of-14-games contest is scheduled to take place from 24 November to 12 December at the Fondation Martin Bodmer outside Geneva, with an overall prize fund of $2.5m (£1.9m).
Game 1 starts at 3pm in Geneva, 2pm in London, 9am in New York and 7.30pm in India
Sindarov will have the white pieces for Game 1 and make the first move
Gukesh and Sindarov are both 20 years old, making this the youngest matchup in world championship’s 140-year history
Read the Guardian’s comprehensive watch guide for the Gukesh v Sindarov showdown
Go move by move through 22 of the most famous games in world championship history
Gukesh: 'I never felt like I was too much in trouble'
Game 1 ends in a draw!
Game 1 is under way!
How do Gukesh and Sindarov match up?
That’s all for today. Thanks as always for following along with us and be sure to read the full report from Game 1 here.

An interesting question at the press conference about the players’ contrasting body language. Sindarov was seen repeatedly shaking his leg during the early stages of the game, while Gukesh sat with his eyes closed in apparent meditation. But it seems neither player is reading much into the other’s behavior.

“I don’t know, maybe it was a little bit of nerves also,” Gukesh says. “But I think both of our habits are similar in a sense. I think in general he taps his foot or shakes his leg and I close my eyes in any tournament, not just the match. So I think it’s just how we behave at the board.”
Sindarov concurs: “I do it in every tournament, not just here. And I saw all the players from India are always meditating. Whenever we meet, he’s also meditating, so I think nothing special here.”

Both players give their approval to the unusually intimate playing conditions at the Fondation Martin Bodmer, where Fide has dispensed with the traditional soundproof glass enclosure that separated the players from spectators at previous world championship matches.

“Some people go out, some people come in, sometimes there’s some creaks on the floor,” Gukesh says. “But nothing too distracting. I was quite OK with it. And also I think it’s quite nice that spectators get to experience the world championship with actually seeing the players up close. I’m completely fine with it.”

Asked how it compares with playing inside purpose-built “fishbowl” in Singapore two years ago, the defending champion says with a laugh: “In the glass box, I’m used to seeing even less people in the room, so maybe it’s a welcome change.”
Gukesh adds: “As a sportsperson, you need to just adapt to different conditions and find a way to perform at your best.”
Sindarov, who has spoken of the peculiar loneliness of playing a tournament with only one other competitor, is similarly enthusiastic.
“As a professional, first of all, you need to be ready to play in any conditions,” he says. “It’s nice to have more people in the playing hall, otherwise it would be too boring.”

Sindarov singles out Gukesh’s adventurous king move (27 ... Kf6) as one of the most impressive moments of the game, admitting he had underestimated the safety of the black king in what appeared to be an exposed position.
“Kf6 was super strong,” the challenger says. “I didn’t give a good evaluation for this one. And the king is really pretty safe on f6.”

Gukesh, for his part, suggests he was entertaining thoughts of playing for a win at that stage. Asked by moderator Maurice Ashley whether he had calculated in advance that his king would be safe on f6, the champion replies: “I thought I’m more than safe.”
“More than safe even?” Ashley asks. “You started thinking maybe more?”
“Yeah, maybe more,” Gukesh says.
Sindarov also addresses the unusual denouement to the game, when his incorrect claim of a draw by threefold repetition resulted in Gukesh being awarded an additional two minutes.
“I was thinking we already did it two times,” he says. “But then, yeah, you need to offer it on the right move.”
“Then I just played two more moves and I offered the draw correctly. I was thinking we already did it three or four times.”

Gukesh sounds less concerned about the time trouble he faces than those of us watching. “Obviously, in the opening I started thinking quite a bit and had some little problems to solve,” he says. “But I knew that overall I didn’t really make any unsound moves. I thought I should be fine. I think overall it was a pretty good game. Maybe around when I went [31 … Bc3], I was getting a little optimistic.”
The Indian credits the time he spent earlier in the game with helping him find his moves quickly once the clock became a factor.

“I thought I was always under control, at least not in a place where I really needed to be worried. When I got into the time trouble, I’d already thought about the next few moves, what I was going to play. So I was happy that I managed to spend some time and find a good solution. And then the moves after that were pretty easy.”
Sindarov, meanwhile, makes no secret of his desire to exploit the disparity on the clock.

“Of course, I’m trying to push every moment because of the clock,” he says. “But in general, I understand my position is very close to equal. I’m trying to keep finding some interesting ideas, but then he defended very well.”

“It’s the easiest thing to actually go and play the game because there’s so much thinking, so much work to do before that,” Gukesh says at the post-game press conference, admitting the anticipation surrounding the match was more difficult to handle than the game itself. “Once you get to the game, it’s like your home. It’s a game you’ve been playing for a lot of years. It feels safe. Before that, with all the nerves and all the hype, I think it’s a little tougher to handle all that.”
Sindarov, making his world championship debut, expressed similar sentiments.
“Before the start of the tournament, I was very nervous, thinking a lot about the game and everything,” he said. “But today I’m just trying to enjoy the game.”

Asked whether he approached the opener as a feeling-out game, the Uzbek said: “In general, if you get a chance, you will always try to win. It doesn’t matter which game. But in the first game, I think mostly you try to learn about your opponent and play safe.”
Both players seem satisfied with the quality of the opening game in a brief walk-and-talk interview with Fide presenter Charlize van Zyl en route to the post-game press conference.
“It felt like a really high-level game,” Gukesh says. “It just looked equal the whole time. As usual, some little problems to solve, but I think both of us played just a very good game.”

The defending champion admitted his mounting time trouble had become a concern. “There were some opening problems to solve, so I took my time. But I never felt like I was too much in trouble. Obviously, the time was getting a little scary.”
Sindarov acknowledged he had been looking to exploit his considerable advantage on the clock but ultimately decided the risks of playing on outweighed the potential rewards.

The players have shaken hands after 38 moves (37 ... Kh7 38 Rh5 Kg8), bringing a tense opening game of the world chess championship to a close by threefold repetition. Gukesh has survived considerable time pressure to emerge with a half-point from his first outing with the black pieces, while Sindarov will have to wait at least another day for his first win on the world championship stage.

A curious bit of drama! Sindarov has incorrectly claimed a draw by threefold repetition and, in accordance with Fide’s by-laws, Gukesh has been awarded an additional two minutes on his clock. A welcome reprieve for the time-strapped defending champion, even if the game still appears headed for a draw.

Sindarov has picked off the h6 pawn to restore material equality (31 Rh5 Bc3 32 Bxh6+ Kg8). And now we have a repetition of moves (33 Rg5+ Kh7 34 Rh5 Kg8 35 Rg5+ Kh7 36 Rh5 Kg8 37 Rg5+), with Gukesh’s king shuttling between g8 and h7. The opening game appears destined for a draw by threefold repetition, which is permitted even before the 40th move under the match regulations.

A couple more moves (28 Rf2 Rgd8) and Gukesh is offering an exchange of rooks on the d-file. Surely any simplification would come as a relief to the champion. But Sindarov declines to accommodate, instead bringing his other knight into the action (29 Nd3) and attacking Gukesh’s bishop on b4.

The ensuing sequence (29 ... Bxf5 30 Rxf5+ Kg7 31 Rh5) sees the players exchange a bishop for a knight, with Sindarov turning his attention to black’s vulnerable h6 pawn. That leaves Gukesh with barely seven minutes to make his next 10 moves, but he appears to have escaped from danger.
Gukesh marches his king further up the board (27 ... Kf6) rather than retreating. The champion is down to 8min 39sec for his next 13 moves, while Sindarov still has more than 25 minutes.
Things are heating up (25 ... Nc6 26 f5 gxf5 27 Nxf5+). Sindarov has recovered the pawn he lost and given check to Gukesh’s king.

And we have our first material imbalance of the game (23 ... Nxe5 24 f4). Gukesh has won a pawn but Sindarov has immediately attacked the knight that captured it. The champion responds by threatening Sindarov’s own knight on the kingside (24 ... g6 25 Ng3).
The challenger has retreated and now Gukesh must navigate a delicate position with barely 10 minutes to make his next 16 moves.

A flurry of activity on the board (22 Ne1 axb3 23 axb3). Gukesh has initiated an exchange of pawns on the queenside, opening up the a-file for his rook. The game is becoming more dynamic at a moment when the champion can least afford to spend time calculating variations.
Sindarov has been in the think tank for 15 minutes and counting, but his overwhelming time advantage affords him that luxury.

Meanwhile, over on the Chess.com broadcast, Judit Polgar is telling war stories. Sindarov’s decision to play 21 g4 rather than Stockfish’s preferred 21 Ne1 has reminded the Hungarian grandmaster of a painful defeat to Veselin Topalov in a similar Berlin endgame during the 2005 Fide world championship tournament in San Luis, Argentina.
“At some point I played g4,” Polgar recalls. “Not because I wanted to play for a win desperately, but because I thought that was the best move I could make in that position.

“And after the game people came to me: ‘Why did you play for a win in that position? It was not better anymore.’ I said: ‘I was not playing for a win in that position. I just thought that was the best move.’”
Two more moves (21 g4 Ke7) and Gukesh is putting his king to work in the center of the board. For all the Berlin’s reputation as a drawish opening, this is shaping up to be a three-result game.

Gukesh has pushed another pawn forward (19 ... c5), reinforcing his bishop on b4 and restricting the movement of white’s pieces. Sindarov quickly moves his knight to the edge of the board, prompting Gukesh to bring his rook across to defend his g7 pawn (20 Nh5 Rg8).

The champion has reached the halfway point to the first time control with barely 16 minutes to spare, while Sindarov still has more than 55 minutes at his disposal. The defending champion is effectively going to have to play rapid chess against an in-form opponent who has the luxury of thinking things through.
That said, despite Gukesh’s visible suffering, the Hungarian grandmaster Peter Leko is beginning to warm to black’s position on the official Fide broadcast.

“Nh5 was played clearly out of ambition,” Leko says. “I don’t know how much this choice was influenced by the clock situation, whether Sindarov wants to keep the game going because of the time situation. And I was praising the move Ng3 because of the clock factor. Looking at the position now, with the knight on h5 stuck and black having a clear b7-b5 push in the air, I already kind of wonder if I would not be much happier with black now.”

Sindarov takes more than 18 minutes before repositioning one of his knights (19 Ng3), keeping his options open and maintaining the tension on the board. The Uzbek challenger still has 57min 11sec on his clock compared with less than 24 minutes for Gukesh.

Gukesh has finally nudged his h-pawn forward (18 … h6), denying a square from Sindarov’s bishop and knights. Even if the position remains objectively equal, the clock is giving Sindarov a significant practical advantage.

Latvian grandmaster Arturs Neiksans has entered the chat, suggesting that Gukesh’s struggles today could have implications well beyond the opening game. If the Berlin defense was intended to be a mainstay of the champion’s opening repertoire for this match, Sindarov may already have given him reason to rethink his preparations.

“It’s probably too early to draw any firm conclusions, but Gukesh’s opening choice is already looking concerning,” Neiksans writes on X. “If you’re facing this much discomfort in Game 1 with what could be one of the cornerstones of your repertoire against 1.e4 for the match, it’s hard to see how you can confidently rely on it in the games to come. Hopefully, Gukesh has a solid backup plan.”
Gukesh has been on the clock for nearly five minutes as he considers his response to Sindarov’s 18 Re2. That’s left him with 24 minutes to make his next 23 moves.

And finally Gukesh has made his move (17 ... Bb4), bringing his bishop forward to attack one of Sindarov’s rooks. But the champion has burned through 36min 14sec of precious time in the process. He now has less than 29 minutes to make his next 23 moves, an average of roughly 75 seconds per turn.

Sindarov thinks for just three minutes before moving his threatened rook out of harm’s way (18 Re2). The position remains finely balanced, but the disparity on the clock is becoming one of the major storylines of this opening game. Gukesh has put himself in a situation where even relatively straightforward decisions will need to be made quickly.

Gukesh has been pondering his response to 17 b3 for more than half an hour. That’s a considerable investment of time given he still has 24 moves to make before receiving another 30 minutes on his clock.

The clock is becoming a factor for Gukesh, who is below 50 minutes remaining with another 23 moves to make before he receives any additional time. Grandmasters Judit Polgar and David Howell, commenting on the Chess.com broadcast, have identified a tempting rook move (17 ... Ra5), but one that would land the champion in trouble if Sindarov answered with 18 Bg5. An important decision awaits Gukesh, and he can ill afford to spend too much time making it.
Two more moves in Geneva (16 ... Be6 17 b3). Gukesh has moved his bishop out of the path of Sindarov’s rooks, while the challenger has reinforced his position on the queenside.

A few more moves to bring us up to date (15 Rd2 a4 16 Rad1). Sindarov has brought both of his rooks into the center of the board, while Gukesh has been steadily advancing a pawn down the left-hand side. Neither player has lost any material since the eighth move, with both looking to build up incremental advantages rather than force the issue. All of the popular engines and supercomputers continue to assess the position as dead even (0.00).
An excellent question from Justin Horton, writing in from Aragón, Spain, about the decor in the playing hall:

double quotation markWhat are the books in the players’ lounge? They look like chess books but you wouldn’t have thought players would be allowed to consult chess books during a game. Nor would they be wise to do so given the cameras are there, but I can’t believe they’d put the players on an honour system not to open them. So are they real, or are they facsimiles, Potemkin books as it were?

Given the decidedly bibliothecal setting, it’s a particularly fitting question. The Fondation Martin Bodmer is one of the world’s great repositories of rare books and manuscripts, its 160,000 treasures including a Gutenberg Bible, Shakespeare’s First Folio and a copy of Isaac Newton’s Principia Mathematica once owned by his great rival Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz.

The subject of the books came up at Sunday’s opening press conference. Gukesh said he had inspected the chairs, lighting and even the floor of the playing hall to ensure he would be comfortable during games that could last four or five hours, but admitted he had barely glanced at the books. “I don’t think I’ll be reading in between the games,” he joked.

A nugget of arcana from the Macedonian grandmaster Alex Colovic that may bode well for Gukesh. Of the four players who have deployed the Berlin defense in a world championship match, three of them (Vladimir Kramnik, Magnus Carlsen and Ding Liren) went on to win their matches. The lone exception? Vishy Anand against Carlsen.

Sindarov has expanded on the queenside and Gukesh has responded by pushing his a-pawn (14 c4 a5). The battle lines are becoming clearer: Sindarov has the more active pieces in the center, while Gukesh is looking for counterplay on the queenside to offset white’s long-term structural advantage.

“I think there were a lot of small surprises at first,” the Dutch grandmaster Anish Giri says on the Take Take Take stream. “I think on move one, maybe 1 d4 was a little more expected than 1 e4. Then from black, I think within the Spanish, maybe the Marshall was a little more expected than the Berlin.

“But then within the Berlin, I think finally the actual surprise is coming from Javokhir. I think this particular Ne4 move, we are in very rare territory. It is not something that I or many of my colleagues have studied deeply. I can imagine it’s a little bit of an obscure position.

articles.title: El Al buys back frequent flyer club stake at NIS 4.2b valuation
articles.summary: In 2022, when El Al was in severe financial distress, it sold 20% of the club to The Phoenix at a NIS 1.3 billion company valuation.
paragraphs: In 2022, when El Al was in severe financial distress, it sold 20% of the club to The Phoenix at a NIS 1.3 billion company valuation.

Four years after selling a 25% stake in its frequent flyers club to institutional investor Phoenix Finance (TASE: PHOE), El Al Israel Airlines Ltd. (TASE: ELAL ) is buying back Phoenix’s holding for NIS 1.05 billion, at a NIS 4.2 billion valuation. Remarkably, the deal sees El Al’s frequent flyer club as more valuable than the entire credit card company Isracard, which has a market cap of NIS 3.4 billion.

In 2022, when El Al was in severe financial distress, it sold 20% of the club at a NIS 1.3 billion valuation. At the start of this year, Phoenix exercised an option to buy a further 5%. El Al is now a very different company, with large cash reserves and listed on the TA-35 Index, which it joined in the latest index reshuffle in early November.

El Al currently holds 75% of the shares in the frequent flyer club. El Al’s own financial reports show how profitable the frequent flyer club has become for the airline. El Al began publishing the club’s results because Phoenix reports them through its subsidiary Phoenix Gamma. According to the third-quarter reports, the club posted a profit of NIS 160 million ($50 million) in the first nine months of the year. Revenue jumped 61% from the same period last year to $117 million.

The club has 3.8 million members, and at the end of the quarter 570,000 people held its Fly Card credit card, which earns points for El Al flights. The figures were up 9% and 14%, respectively, from last year.
The club is in the process of transferring its cards from ICC-Cal to rival Isracard, which has already reported that it has 390,000 cards in the program.
Who gains and who loses?

For the frequent flyer club, headed by Moshe Morgenstern, moving the cards to Isracard will boost profitability. Under the agreement, El Al and the club will gain more than NIS 100 million in additional annual profit, for a total of NIS 1 billion to NIS 1.3 billion over the 10-year agreement.

For Isracard, the agreement will reduce profit by NIS 70 million to NIS 100 million in the coming year. The company estimates that in subsequent years it will contribute an average of NIS 120 million to NIS 160 million annually over the 10-year term.
El Al has a market cap of NIS 12.5 billion, with its shares up 684% over the past three years.

Frequent flyer club and Fly Card CEO Moshe Morgenstern said, "The frequent flyer club and Fly Card have experienced exceptional growth in recent years, strengthening the club’s position as Israel’s strongest and leading loyalty program. This move builds on our business momentum and follows our 10-year strategic agreement with Isracard, which is expected to generate about NIS 1 billion over its term. The club is an integral part of El Al, and the return to full ownership will allow us to keep expanding our travel, consumer and financial offerings and deliver the best value to the club’s millions of members."
Published by Globes, Israel business news - en.globes.co.il - on November 24, 2026.

articles.title: Faisal Islam: Fears over the AI boom haven't gone away
articles.summary: There were legitimate fears before Huang's abrupt exit from Nvidia - and his return won't fix it
paragraphs: As the market bell rang out at the Nasdaq today, the Nvidia super-bounce faded.
Its shares slid and are down almost 30% over the past six months, well before the scandal involving Jensen Huang emerged earlier this month.
The legitimate fears about the staying power of the tech boom pre-dated Huang's exit. They have not gone away with his return.

Investors are jittery. Already Anthropic is now trading notably lower than last week's stock market flotation. The firm is the first purely AI company to be publicly listed, and is being seen as a big test for continued investor appetite for the technology.

President Trump's extraordinary phone call to CNBC taking credit for telling the board to reinstate Huang showed the extent of the operation - of some in Silicon Valley and within the US administration - to get him back at the helm.
Among the truly astonishing reflections from President Trump was a suggestion that a two-day investigation of allegations was done and had cleared Huang of national security concerns.
The President said his remarkable move to intervene was because Huang is a "national treasure" who has the next generation of AI chips "in his head". Trump says this is why he needed to act.

In markets, those sceptical about the AI boom say they have never seen an operation to prop up a stock market boom like this. The bond vigilantes and short sellers are now up against Silicon Valley and the White House.
Investors are trading not revenue numbers but levels of political support at a time when US voters have just delivered a backlash against AI data centres.
Against this backdrop, the recovery of the central cash-generating foundation of the tech boom - Nvidia and its $400bn (£304bn) annual sales of advanced chips - looks politically fragile.
This worsens other uncertainties and risks, such as Nvidia's central role in the web of financing, borrowing and cross-ownership to support every corner of the build out of data centres.
The brief interim Nvidia chief executive Colette Kress had already signalled a rowing back from elements of this strategy last week. Where is that now?
The fall back in Anthropic's share price also raises questions about OpenAI's planned listing on the stock exchange. Ultimately these two companies might be the most critical part of all this.

They remain valuable companies with phenomenal technology relied on by the world's biggest companies. The real question is whether that reliance eases, as corporations eschew expensive frontier models for cheaper generic models offered by China.
In turn, all this could be affected by the political backlash, to which the Nvidia psychodrama now contributes.
It is simply not normal to have trillion dollar swings in the value of individual companies.
The extraordinary volatility shows the fragile mood of investors.

articles.title: גוגל רוצה ליצור לכם ערוץ טלוויזיה. והכוכבים? אתם
articles.summary: ראיתם ביוטיוב את תקציר המשחק של דני אבדיה מהלילה, כשהוא ניצח את לברון ג'יימס? מעולה. כי אם החלום של גוגל יתגשם, הסרטון הבא שיצוף לכם כשתפתחו את אפליקציות יוטיוב בטלוויזיה יהיה בכלל סרטון AI על משחק אחר של הכדורסלן הישראלי הגדול בכל הזמנים, שבו אתם פוגשים את אבדיה על הפרקט במדיסון סקוור גארדן. נשמע מוטרף? […]
paragraphs: ראיתם ביוטיוב את תקציר המשחק של דני אבדיה מהלילה, כשהוא ניצח את לברון ג'יימס? מעולה. כי אם החלום של גוגל יתגשם, הסרטון הבא שיצוף לכם כשתפתחו את אפליקציות יוטיוב בטלוויזיה יהיה בכלל סרטון AI על משחק אחר של הכדורסלן הישראלי הגדול בכל הזמנים, שבו אתם פוגשים את אבדיה על הפרקט במדיסון סקוור גארדן. נשמע מוטרף? זה בדיוק מה שעולה מבקשת פטנט חדשה של גוגל שנחשפה בימים האחרונים ובה ה-AI יפיק ערוץ שלם עם תוכניות שבהן אתם הדמות הראשית. וכן, ברור שיהיו פרסומות.
מהיסטוריית הצפייה לפרומפט

בקשת הפטנט של גוגל שנחשפה על ידי 404Media פורסמה רשמית לפני שבוע. הבקשה מתארת לשונית בשם My Channel באפליקציית יוטיוב בטלוויזיה, ובה סרטונים שנוצרו עבורכם. באחד האיורים מופיע הערוץ של צופה בשם ג'ון. בתפריט שלו יש קומדיה רומנטית, הרפתקת מדע בדיוני ומותחן אקשן. וכן, אתם תככבו בכולם.

כדי לייצר את הסרטונים, המערכת תחבר בין היסטוריית הצפייה שלכם לבין נתונים כמו קבוצת גיל, שפת המכשיר והמיקום שלו. משם היא תנסח פרומפט שינחה את המודל באיזה ז'אנר לעבוד ואיזה סגנון ופורמט לאמץ מהסרטונים שבהם אתם צופים הכי הרבה. העלילה תיכתב עבורכם, ואם תבחרו לככב בה, המערכת תוכל להשתמש בתמונות שלכם כדי ליצור דמות ולשחזר את הקול שלכם לדיאלוגים. הסרטונים יוכלו להיווצר לפי בקשה או להתווסף לערוץ אוטומטית במועדים קבועים. לפי המסמך, תוכלו לשלוט במידע שהמערכת אוספת, וככל שתשתפו פחות היא תישען יותר על ברירות מחדל.
לא רק קרינג' של עצמכם, קחו גם פרסומות

בקשת הפטנט של גוגל לא עוצרת רק ביצירת תכנים שמבוססים על המראה שלכם ושכנראה יגרמו לכם להתכווץ בכיסא. לא לא, גוגל צריכה גם לראות מזה כסף. הבקשה מתארת כלי פרסום שיוכל להכניס לפחות מודעה אחת לסרטון שנוצר בשבילכם, עוד לפני שהוא מגיע למסך.

הרעיון הזה משתלב במה שכבר קורה אצל חברות אחרות. מטא למשל מאפשרת למפרסמים ליצור בעזרת AI כמה גרסאות של אותה מודעה, ואז בוחרת איזו מהן להציג לפי הסיכוי שכל משתמש יגיב אליה; יצרנית הטלוויזיות TCL כבר התנסתה בהפצת תוכן שנוצר ב-AI בשירות הסטרימינג החינמי שלה; ואצל גוגל, לפי הבקשה, גם מה שתראו בין הפרסומות יכול להיות שונה מצופה לצופה. כל הרעיון כרגע, כמובן, קיים על הנייר בלבד.

במקביל, האתר Patentlyze מדווח כי בוחן הפטנטים האמריקאי דחה את הבקשה של גוגל יותר מפעם אחת לקבלת פטנט. עם זאת, באתר מצוין במקביל כי גוגל עדיין יכולה לתקן את הבקשה ולהגיש אותה מחדש או לערער על הדחייה. אם אכן תצליח ותוציא לפועל את My Channel, השאלה "ראיתם את הפרק אתמול?" תגיע עם לא מעט תשובות אם כל אחד יקבל פרק משלו.

articles.title: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
articles.summary: Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard.
