paragraphs: When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted.

“Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.”

The Kremlin-controlled forces and their Malian allies were facing a coordinated surprise assault by the al-Qaida-linked JNIM and the Tuareg-led Azawad Liberation Front (FLA), whose fighters used suicide car bombs and drones to break through the city’s defences.

Leaked Russian state records suggest the losses were heavy that day. Death certificates of Russian fighters killed in Mali, held by Rosstat, Russia’s state statistics agency, were obtained by the hacker groups Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow and analysed by the Guardian.

The records show that 43 Russians died in Mali on 25 April, including six in Kidal and one in nearby Aguelhok. Others were recorded as dying in the capital, Bamako, and in Gao, where rebels shot down a Russian military helicopter that day.

By the following morning, the Russians had abandoned Kidal, which Russian mercenaries had helped capture in November 2023 and which Moscow had since held up as a showcase of its growing influence in Africa.
In all, the records list 349 Russian deaths in Mali between September 2023 and September 2026, most of which the Guardian was able to link to known battles with rebel groups.
The figures offer a previously unseen glimpse into the human cost of Moscow’s efforts to prop up Mali’s military junta, in what has become Russia’s largest military deployment in Africa.
Two western officials who have travelled to Mali and were shown the data said the death toll was higher than previously estimated.
“That’s over 10% of Russia’s forces killed in action,” said one of the officials, speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly.
Moscow does not publish its losses in Africa, and its foreign ministry did not respond to a request for comment.

The Wagner private military group, led by the warlord Yevgeny Prigozhin, first arrived in Mali in late 2021, a year after a military coup had toppled President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta. French forces were ordered to leave the country as relations with the junta deteriorated, bringing an end to France’s decade-long counter-terrorism operation and leaving Russia as the regime’s main foreign protector.

Wagner handed over its operations in Mali to the Africa Corps in June 2025, two years after Prigozhin led a failed mutiny on Moscow that discredited the group in the eyes of the Kremlin. By that summer, British intelligence estimated that about 2,000 Africa Corps personnel were deployed in the country.

The Africa Corps, closely overseen by Russian military intelligence, currently provides backing to several African governments in return for payment or lucrative contracts granting access to natural resources.

Despite the Russian presence, Mali’s security situation has continued to deteriorate. In late July 2024, Russian and Malian forces fought Tuareg separatists for several days near Tinzaouaten, on the Algerian border.
Wagner at the time issued a rare statement admitting losses, including the death of a commander, but gave no figure. Estimates from Russian sources ranged from about 20 to more than 80 dead.

The Rosstat records list 70 Russians who died on 27 July 2024, all but one of them in the Kidal region. The figures make the battle of Tinzaouaten the deadliest single day for Russian forces in Africa since Wagner mercenaries first deployed to the continent in 2017.

The toll in Mali may have been driven up by Ukraine, which has extended its war against Russia to the Sahel. Kyiv has been assisting Tuareg rebels there, according to two people with knowledge of the operations. CNN has reported that about 15 Ukrainian specialists were deployed to Mali to help local rebel forces fighting Russian troops.

The records are probably an undercount. Registration often lags, and no Russian deaths in Mali are recorded for March 2026 although at least three Africa Corps fighters were reported killed in an ambush near Nampala that month.

The leaked data also sheds light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa. Central African Republic, where Wagner fighters guard the president, Faustin-Archange Touadéra, accounts for 30 deaths. While not all could be linked to known incidents, three men died on the night drones struck Wagner camps in Kaga-Bandoro in December 2023.

In Libya, where Russian forces back the eastern commander Khalifa Haftar and use his airbases as a supply route to their deployments in the Sahel, some of the recorded deaths were probably linked to a helicopter crash at the Maaten al-Sarra base in February 2026. On Sunday, Ukrainian drones sunk a Russian warship off the coast of Libya; it is unclear whether there were any casualties.

In Niger, where Russia’s Africa Corps moved in after the military junta expelled French and US troops, a Russian fighter died two days after Islamic State militants attacked Niamey airport in January, a previously unreported casualty.

Moscow has in recent months stepped up its effort to show it is back in control in Mali. On 6 October, Malian troops and the Africa Corps recaptured Kidal after what the army called an air and ground campaign.

A report this month by the US-based Conflict Insights Group (CIG) found that the Africa Corps had sharply increased its use of drones in Mali, including Lancet suicide drones, amid an intensifying air campaign.

The group wrote that the drone campaign had also targeted civilians, boostering support for the rebels. “Civilian deaths in the intensified air campaign, which the Africa Corps leads, are likely to aid insurgent recruitment,” it said.
A western diplomat who works in the region said the attacks in late April had punctured the image of Russian military invincibility that Moscow and the junta had cultivated among Malians.
“Russia still wields considerable influence in Mali, but patience with its military performance is wearing thin.”

articles.title: Home investors in Israel count their losses
articles.summary: Many investors who sold apartments in 2025 saw a loss in real terms, Finance Ministry deputy chief economist Galit Ben Naim reports. “Globes” looks at which regions were hit hardest.
paragraphs: The housing slowdown in Israel is affecting investors too, and those who bought apartments in recent years can find themselves selling at a substantial loss. After years of steadily rising home prices, some investors are finding they have to cut their asking price to attract a buyer, sometimes selling for less in real terms than they paid. That at least exempts them from betterment tax. Transaction costs, particularly the high purchase tax levied on investors deepens the overall loss.

How widespread is the trend, and where have investors been hit hardest? Figures published by Ministry of Finance deputy chief economist Galit Ben Naim, show that a substantial share of investors who sold apartments in 2025 after holding them for five years took a loss in real terms. The figures vary widely across the country, both in the share of investors who sold at a loss and in how long they held their apartments.
The south saw 62% of investors take a loss

A nationwide analysis of about 12,000 sales by investors in 2025 covered by finalized real estate betterment tax assessments found that 47.5% of investors who sold an apartment within five years of buying it took a loss in real terms.

The share of investors who sold at a loss fell sharply the longer they held their apartments. It was 17.2% among those who held them for six to 10 years and 1.9% among those who held them for more than 30 years.

In the south, the share was well above the national average. Some 62% of investors who sold an apartment within five years took a loss in real terms, and some sold for less than they had paid even before adjusting for inflation. Nearly 25% of investors who sold apartments in the south in 2025 had held them for less than five years, compared with just 9.7% nationwide. Investors made nearly 2,000 sales in the south, the most of any region examined.

One possible explanation is oversupply. Construction began on about 50,000 apartments in Beersheva, Ofakim, Netivot, Ashkelon, Dimona and Kiryat Gat over the past five years, some in subsidized housing programs. Some of those apartments entered the rental market, increasing competition. This may lead investors who are struggling to find tenants to accept a lower sale price as well.

Ben Naim recalls that the picture was almost the reverse in 2009, when investors in the south sold apartments after particularly short holding periods and made handsome profits. She suggests that some sellers may now be trying to cut their losses, much like investors placing a stop-loss order in the capital market.
Developers rent unsold homes to avoid price cuts
Israeli home sales suffer summer slowdown
Home deal cancellations proliferate in Israel
Tel Aviv investors can afford to wait

The Tel Aviv region also had a high share of loss-making sales. Some 57% of investors who sold an apartment within five years took a loss in real terms, and most of the sales took place in Tel Aviv itself. A substantial share of the apartments were bought in 2021, which Ben Naim calls "The year of euphoria in the real estate market," just before interest rates began to rise.

To illustrate the point, Ben Naim cited several deals, including a luxury apartment that sold in 2025 for just over NIS 10 million after being bought about two years earlier at a considerably higher price. The seller had bought the apartment shortly before construction was completed, from buyers who had purchased it directly from the contractor. The original buyers used the proceeds from the sale to make the final payment to the builder and assigned the purchase contract to the new buyer. Ben Naim said this may have allowed the original buyers to avoid paying a cancellation fee on a deal they could not or did not want to complete. "They found someone to step into their shoes. In hindsight, it seems the shoes were too big for him," she wrote.

In another deal, a buyer paid just under NIS 3 million for a Tel Aviv apartment in 2022 in an "apartment under construction" arrangement, intending it to replace his existing home. By then, the Bank of Israel had raised its interest rate twice, by a cumulative 0.65 percentage points. Three years later, the buyer sold the new apartment at a loss after failing to sell his previous home within the time allowed by law. As a result, he was classified as an investor for tax purposes, even though he had originally bought the apartment as a replacement home. Because he sold at a loss, he owed no tax.

In Bat Yam, a second-hand apartment was bought for about NIS 1.5 million shortly after the outbreak of the war in October 2023, partly because of the potential for an urban renewal project in the building. About a year after the purchase, the residents reached an agreement with a developer, but the anticipated rise in value failed to materialize. In mid-2025, the apartment sold for exactly what the buyer had paid. Ben Naim estimates that the potential for urban renewal was already reflected in the purchase price. The buyer made no nominal gain and paid more than NIS 100,000 in purchase tax, on top of other transaction costs.

Ben Naim notes that only a minority of investors in the Tel Aviv region rushed to sell after a relatively short holding period. "Those who don’t have to sell probably aren’t selling," she says. Investors with deep pockets may be able to afford to wait, she adds, and that may partly explain the low number of deals in the region’s resale market. She also puts the question to contractors in Tel Aviv and Bat Yam, who hold some 15,000 unsold new apartments.
Most Jerusalem sellers held their apartments for decades
The Jerusalem region, which also includes Beit Shemesh, had the lowest share of investors who took a loss when selling a home within five years of buying it. Just 27% sold at a loss in real terms.

Less than 7% of investor sales in the Jerusalem region in 2025 involved apartments held for up to five years. Meanwhile, 63% of investors who sold apartments had held them for at least 20 years, the highest share in the country. Of those who sold, 44.4% had held their apartments for more than 30 years and another 18.5% for 21 to 30 years.

The figures show that long-term investment is particularly common in the Jerusalem region, where many investors hold properties for decades. Those long ownership periods allowed them to ride out price declines without realizing losses.

Ben Naim stresses that Jerusalem investors did see property values fall. She says some saw declines in real terms from the second half of the 1990s until just before the 2008 global financial crisis, after which interest rates fell to near zero.

The figures come amid a decline in investor activity. According to the Ministry of Finance, investors bought just 849 apartments in September 2026, down 29% from September 2025, and their share of all deals fell to 13.6%. The decline was steep in Netanya and Tel Aviv, where investor purchases fell by 47% and 43%, respectively. Investors sold 1,080 apartments, down 10% from a year earlier, and still sold more homes than they bought.
Published by Globes, Israel business news - en.globes.co.il - on November 24, 2026.

articles.title: Cloud backup co Eon raising funds at $6b valuation
articles.summary: The round, expected to total several hundred million dollars, is being led by existing Canadian investor Georgian, “Globes” has learned.
paragraphs: The round, expected to total several hundred million dollars, is being led by existing Canadian investor Georgian, “Globes” has learned.

Israeli cloud backup company Eon , founded by serial entrepreneur Ofir Ehrlich, is in talks to raise another funding round that could value the company at $6 billion, "Globes" has learned. The round, expected to total several hundred million dollars, is being led by existing investor Georgian, a Canadian venture capital firm that was once among the most active investors in Israeli tech. Georgian has invested in growing Israeli cybersecurity companies such as Cyera and Island and has backed Eon since late last year, when the company raised $300 million at a $4 billion valuation, according to PitchBook.

It is rare for an existing investor in a growing company to seek to lead a new funding round, as companies usually bring in new, larger funds to help lead the round. The move appears to reflect Georgian’s confidence that it can make a return on its investment in Eon.

Eon is considered one of the most sought-after investments by Israeli venture capital firms, partly because its founders, Ofir Ehrlich, Ron Kimchi and Gonen Stein, are serial entrepreneurs with a strong track record. Eon tackles one of the biggest and most complex problems facing large corporations, backing up cloud data, with a fresh approach that uses new code to support AI data. The platform promises executives that their databases will survive even ransomware attacks or natural disasters, using an algorithm that is "attached" to the data and prevents it from being deleted under any circumstances. Last year, investors ranked Eon among Globes’ 10 most promising startups.
Fierce market competition

Eon’s popularity with investors enabled it to raise $200 million across three funding rounds in 2024. Its valuation rose in stages from $200 million at the start of the year to $1.4 billion by year-end, while it brought in only a few million dollars. In late 2025, Eon raised $300 million in a round led by serial investor Elad Gil. At the time, its annual recurring revenue (ARR) was just $10 million to $20 million, and it primarily served one large US bank. In 2026, ARR is estimated at about $60 million.

The company’s ARR is still considered low for its stage of development and the high valuation it is seeking. Market sources report fierce competition from companies including Rubrik, Veeam, Druva and Cohesity, which already have backup contracts, seasoned sales teams and technology adapted for ransomware recovery. Large customers are also hard to persuade to switch from major backup platforms. Meanwhile, cloud giants such as Microsoft, Google and Amazon are improving their backup and attack recovery tools.
Eon in startup rankings despite $1.4b valuation

Ehrlich, Kimchi and Stein founded Eon after spending four years at Amazon Web Services (AWS), the largest cloud provider. They joined AWS after selling it their previous company, CloudEndure, which had achieved the reverse, allowing companies to move data to Amazon’s cloud at the click of a button. That business was already doing $1 billion in turnover by the time they left. After seeing firsthand how much customers wanted reliable backups, they founded a company to back up data itself for Amazon customers. Along the way, they recruited their former bosses, including several senior AWS backup and storage executives.
No response to this report has been forthcoming from Eon.
Published by Globes, Israel business news - en.globes.co.il - on November 24, 2026.

articles.title: "הסוכן הוא רק הצינור": יוצאי אימפרבה מגייסים 10 מיליון דולר כדי לשמור על סוכני ה-AI שלכם
articles.summary: לא. אף אחד במשרד לא רוצה לשמוע על האייג'נט שבנית שמכין רשימת קניות בסופר ומתאם לך דייטים עם בן או בת הזוג. הבנו את הקטע. אבל אם בניתם כבר סוכנים שמשמשים אתכם במקום העבודה שלכם, זה כבר יותר מעניין. זה כנראה מספיק מעניין כדי שבכירי אימפרבה לשעבר יציעו פלטפורמה שלמה שתשגיח על הסוכנים שלכם, ויגייסו […]
paragraphs: הצוות של דאנטה ו-Nero, הכלב המשרדי. צילום: ויקטור לוי

לא. אף אחד במשרד לא רוצה לשמוע על האייג'נט שבנית שמכין רשימת קניות בסופר ומתאם לך דייטים עם בן או בת הזוג. הבנו את הקטע. אבל אם בניתם כבר סוכנים שמשמשים אתכם במקום העבודה שלכם, זה כבר יותר מעניין. זה כנראה מספיק מעניין כדי שבכירי אימפרבה לשעבר יציעו פלטפורמה שלמה שתשגיח על הסוכנים שלכם, ויגייסו בשביל זה 10 מיליון דולר לסטארטאפ שנחשף רק עכשיו. אה, ואתם חייבים לראות את האתר שלו.
של מי הסוכן הזה בכלל?

בשיחה עם גיקטיים מספר משה ליפסקר, מנכ"ל ומייסד שותף ב-Dante Security, כי ארגונים כבר משתמשים בסוכני AI ביום-יום, ואלו כבר מבצעים פעולות במערכות הליבה של הארגון, אולם ברוב המקרים אין לאף אחד תשובה לשאלה הכי פשוטה: מי אחראי על הסוכן הזה? "אנחנו מביאים אחריות אנושית לעולם של סוכני AI: כל פעולה של כל סוכן מול מערכות ארגוניות קריטיות – מתועדת; סוכן שחורג מהגבולות שלו נעצר, וכל החלטה שדורשת שיקול דעת מנותבת לאדם שאחראי עליה", אומר ליפסקר. לדבריו, הפלטפורמה נעזרת במערכת ניהול הזהויות הקיימת של הארגון כדי למפות כל סוכן לאדם שהפעיל אותו, כך שלכל אחד יש בעלים.

בשלב הבא, כל פעולה של הסוכן מסווגת כרגילה, אפורה או מסוכנת. אם הפעולות הן רגילות, הן ממשיכות כרגיל. במקרה של פעולה אפורה או מסוכנת, היא נעצרת ומחכה לאישור של הגורם האחראי. במקביל, המערכת מבצעת מעקב אחרי כל פעולה של הסוכנים, כך שאתם יכולים לדעת מי נגע במה, מתי, למה ומי אישר את זה. "מהצד של העובדים, החוויה כמעט שקופה. הסוכנים ממשיכים לעבוד והעבודה לא נעצרת", אומר ליפסקר. "מהצד של צוות האבטחה, יש סוף-סוף תמונה מלאה: אילו כלי AI וסוכנים פועלים בארגון, מול אילו מערכות קריטיות הם עובדים ותיעוד מלא של מה כל סוכן שינה ובסמכות של מי. במקום לרדוף אחרי סוכנים, צוות האבטחה יודע בכל רגע מי אחראי על כל אחד מהם".

לדברי ליפסקר, ההבדל המשמעותי בין Dante לשאר המערכות להגנה מפני סוכנים הוא שהפלטפורמה שלה עובדת על המידע בזמן שהוא בתנועה, ובזמן שהפעולה מתרחשת: "לא מספיק לנסות לחזות מראש מה סוכן עלול לעשות, או לנסות לתת לו הרשאות המגדירות מה מותר ומה אסור לו, ולא מספיק לגלות בדיעבד מה הוא כבר עשה. סוכנים פועלים במהירות של מכונה, ולכן גם השליטה צריכה לפעול בזמן אמת: לזהות את הפעולה החריגה בזמן שהיא מתרחשת, ולעצור אותה לפני שהנזק נעשה". זאת לדבריו בניגוד לפתרונות אחרים שבודקים מה נכנס למודל, מה יוצא ממנו ואיך הוא מתנהג. "זו רק חצי מהתמונה. אנחנו מסתכלים על כל המערכות שהסוכן מחובר אליהן ולעומק הנדרש, כי שם נוצר הנזק בפועל. הסוכן הוא רק הצינור. המידע והפעולות במערכות הליבה הם מה שהארגון באמת צריך להגן עליהם".
גם גיגי לוי-וייס כבר בפנים

ליפסקר היה המנהל של אימפרבה ישראל, וכיהן גם בתפקיד מנהל המו"פ העולמי. הוא מספר שהניסיון הזה לימד אותו "להסתכל על המידע עצמו ועל המערכות שבהן הוא יושב, כי שם נמצא מה שהארגון באמת צריך להגן עליו". הוא מוסיף, "כמומחים לאבטחת מידע, אנחנו יודעים לזהות מתי פעולה על מערכת קריטית ומידע חורגת מהשגרה. זו בדיוק היכולת הנדרשת היום מול סוכני AI, שמבצעים כמות עצומה של פעולות, כשרק חלק קטן מהן באמת דורש עצירה ושיקול דעת אנושי". כיום, החברה מעסיקה 24 עובדים בשני מוקדים, כאשר בישראל מתבצעים פיתוח המוצר והמחקר, בעוד בארצות הברית נמצאים צוותי המכירות והתמיכה. היום (ג') מודיעה דאנטה על השלמת סבב גיוס Seed בהיקף של 10 מיליון דולר בהובלת קרן NFX של גיגי לוי-וייס, ובהשתתפות הקרנות Alpha Drive ו-Inovia, לצד משקיעים פרטיים נוספים. החברה נוסדה על ידי ליפסקר, גבי ביו (מנהל הפיתוח של מחלקת החדשנות באימפרבה), ושי פיינברג. ליפסקר ופיינברג הכירו עוד בשירותם בצבא – אבל לא ב-8200 כפי שאתם אולי מצפים – אלא בסיירת גולני.
לאתר של Dante Security שאתם באמת צריכים לראות

articles.title: Israeli institutional investors return to US office market
articles.summary: US real estate capital markets conference jointly hosted by global real estate services firm JLL and international law firm Greenberg Traurig at its office in Tel Aviv was told there had been a 186% surge in deals.
paragraphs: US real estate capital markets conference jointly hosted by global real estate services firm JLL and international law firm Greenberg Traurig at its office in Tel Aviv was told there had been a 186% surge in deals.

The number of lenders offering financing for office transactions through JLL's US operations rose from 43 at the market low to 123 today, up 186%. The figure was presented at a US real estate capital markets conference jointly hosted by global real estate services firm JLL and international law firm Greenberg Traurig, held at Greenberg Traurig's offices in Tel Aviv’s Azrieli Center. Industry leaders described improved access to financing and investment opportunities, alongside growing caution in deal selection amid interest rate movements and market volatility.

JLL senior managing director and capital markets office head in Los Angeles Jeffrey Bramson said the increase in the number of lenders reflects a recovery in the credit market. Bramson stressed that even large deals that previously struggled to secure financing are now benefiting from improved credit availability. The event brought together senior US investment executives and representatives of Israeli institutional investors, banks and other investors.

Bramson also emphasized that interest rate stability is no less important to investors than the level of interest rates. Sharp fluctuations in bond yields and borrowing costs make it difficult to determine an asset's value and close a transaction on the terms that formed the basis of the original investment decision.

The presentation also featured JLL senior managing director and capital markets equity placement platform leader Doug Bond, and highlighted that despite improving liquidity, investors continue to carefully assess asset quality and financing structures.
Israeli perspective: Beyond equity investments, financing deals

Greenberg Traurig's Tel Aviv office shareholder Lawrence Sternthal highlighted a shift in Israeli investment activity in the US. He said that Israeli institutional investors and banks are now also active as lenders, investors in real estate debt funds and partners in providing financing for transactions. Due to adjustments in property values and the gap between existing debt obligations and current financing capacity, he identified opportunities in mezzanine financing, preferred equity and capital injections into existing transactions.

He continued, "One of the questions occupying Israeli investors today is no longer whether to invest in US real estate, but where, how and with whom. After years of uncertainty, the US real estate market is entering a new phase of opportunities, but also complexity. In such a market, familiarity with the US business and regulatory environment, combined with a deep understanding of the needs of Israeli investors, becomes a significant advantage."

JLL head of international capital coverage Mor Ziv stressed the resilience of Israeli investors: "Regardless of what the headlines say or which way the political winds are blowing, we keep working, flying, building and investing. According to JLL's latest research, Israel ranks eighth among foreign investors in US real estate. At JLL Israel, we are pleased to guide Israeli investors as they navigate global investment opportunities and carefully select those best suited to their needs and objectives."

JLL is one of the world's largest real estate services firms, operating in more than 80 countries and maintaining one of the industry's largest research divisions, alongside its consulting, investment and property management activities. The company has operated in Israel since 1997 and employs some 300 people in the country.
Investors are more selective, but still see opportunities

During a panel moderated by JLL senior managing director and capital markets equity placement platform leader Michael Joseph, David Warshawsky of Corebridge Real Estate Investors illustrated the caution prevailing in the rental housing market. He said the company evaluated about 400 investment opportunities over the past year but completed only one deal. Nevertheless, he identified opportunities to buy assets at appropriate prices and create value through active management and property improvements.

Crow Holdings CEO Michael Levy highlighted the contrast between strong demand for industrial and logistics development and greater caution regarding residential development. He also suggested that the decline in construction starts could improve market conditions in the coming years. Christoph Donner of Cityview Real Estate Partners presented strategies for improving operational efficiency in residential properties, including the use of technology and artificial intelligence to reduce management costs.

Improved access to financing and adjustments in property values are opening up new opportunities in the US market. Successful investment today requires careful asset selection, appropriate financing structures and a genuine ability to enhance and manage properties over the long term.

articles.title: גייסו 53 מיליון דולר כדי שהאייג'נטים יפסיקו לנפח לכם את החשבון
articles.summary: סוכני AI כבר כותבים ומריצים קוד בארגונים בקצב מסחרר, אבל מישהו צריך לנהל את כל עומס המחשוב הזה בלי לשרוף את התקציב. סטארטאפ ישראלי חדש בשם Zipher (זייפר), שנחשף היום (ג') עם גיוס משמעותי, רוצה לתת לסוכנים שלו לנהל את העבודה מאחורי הקלעים – ולחתוך בעלויות הענן. אותה משימה, חשבון אחר "ב-Zipher הלקוח מגדיר יעדי […]
paragraphs: מייסדי זייפר | צילום: עומר הכהן

סוכני AI כבר כותבים ומריצים קוד בארגונים בקצב מסחרר, אבל מישהו צריך לנהל את כל עומס המחשוב הזה בלי לשרוף את התקציב. סטארטאפ ישראלי חדש בשם Zipher (זייפר), שנחשף היום (ג') עם גיוס משמעותי, רוצה לתת לסוכנים שלו לנהל את העבודה מאחורי הקלעים – ולחתוך בעלויות הענן.

"ב-Zipher הלקוח מגדיר יעדי ביצועים ותקציב, והסוכנים שלנו מחליטים אוטומטית איך כל workload ירוץ", אומר בשיחה עם גיקטיים דן קוסטר, מנכ"ל זייפר ואחד ממייסדי הסטארטאפ. לדבריו, הסוכנים לומדים מה כל משימה צריכה ובאילו משימות אחרות היא תלויה. הם בוחרים מנוע עיבוד לפי העומס והקיבולת הזמינה בזמן אמת, מקצים משאבים, קובעים מתי להריץ את המשימה ומריצים אותה בעצמם. בעת הצורך הם גם משכתבים את הקוד ומתאימים אותו ל-framework של המנוע שנבחר.

המערכת עובדת עם AWS, Azure ו-Google Cloud ומתחברת בין היתר ל-dbt, ל-Databricks Workflows ול-Airflow. לדברי קוסטר, אחד היתרונות המרכזיים של הפלטפורמה הוא שהיא פועלת ולא רק ממליצה. כך היא מבטלת את הטרייד-אוף המוכר של חיסכון בעלויות compute על חשבון רמת השירות או האמינות, ומספקת ללקוחות תוצאות בתוך כשבועיים מתחילת העבודה עם המוצר.

את זייפר הקימו ב-2024 קוסטר ויואב גיל בן אפרים, ה-CTO של החברה, שניהם יוצאי 8200. אחת הלקוחות היא Hertz, שמריצה אלפי משימות דאטה, בין היתר סביב הזמנות וניהול צי הרכב שלה. לפי קוסטר, Hertz הפחיתה את עלויות המחשוב ב-25% עד 40% ושמרה על ביצועים עקביים גם בעונות השיא. במקביל, בסטארטאפ כבר מדווחים כי בקרב לקוחות שלהם מרשימת ה-Fortune 500 נרשם חיסכון של 40% עד 60% בעלויות, ושיפור של עד 80% בעמידה ביעדי רמת השירות, וכי ההשקעה במערכת מחזירה את עצמה בממוצע בתוך שבועיים.
הצוות של Zipher | צילום: עומר הכהן

היום כאמור נחשף הסטארטאפ עם גיוסי הון בסך כולל של 53 מיליון דולר, כולל סבב סיד של 8 מיליון דולר בהובלת TLV Partners, ועכשיו 45 מיליון דולר בסבב A חדש, בהובלה משותפת של Maor Investments עם Glilot Capital ובהשתתפות המשקיעים הקיימים TLV Partners. בין האנג'לים והיועצים של הסטארטאפ נמצאים תומר שירן מ-Dremio, בר מוזס וליאור גביש מ-Monte Carlo וקלינט שארפ מ-Cribl.

שחר צפריר, שותף מנהל ב-TLV Partners, אמר עם חשיפת הסטארטאפ והגיוסים החדשים: "סוכני AI הופכים למקור הגדול ביותר לעומסי עבודה של נתונים בארגונים, ובעולם שבו סוכנים אוטונומיים פועלים בהיקף הולך וגדל, ארגונים זקוקים לפלטפורמה שתקבע היכן ואיך להריץ כל משימה. הצוות של Zipher כבר הוכיח את היכולות של הפלטפורמה בסביבות ייצור אצל לקוחות Fortune 500, שממשיכים להרחיב את השימוש בה".

articles.title: AI agents data infrastructure co Zipher raises $53m
articles.summary: The Israeli company says its AI agents automatically decide how data workload runs, from resource allocation to framework selection and scheduling, according to the performance targets that each customer sets.
paragraphs: The Israeli company says its AI agents automatically decide how data workload runs, from resource allocation to framework selection and scheduling, according to the performance targets that each customer sets.
Israeli AI agents enterprise data infrastructure company Zipher today announced it has raised $53 million in seed and Series A rounds from TLV Partners, Maor Investments and Glilot Capital.

Zipher says its AI agents automatically decide how data workload runs, from resource allocation to framework selection and scheduling, according to the performance targets that each customer sets. Zipher works with several Fortune 500 companies, including Hertz, which see 40-60% cost-efficiency gains, up to 80% better service level agreement adherence and a sharp drop in infrastructure-related incidents.

Zipher says customers typically see results within two weeks. Zipher runs on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud and integrates with dbt, Databricks Workflows, Apache Airflow, Azure Data Factory and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools such as Databricks Asset Bundles or Terraform.

Zipher was founded by CEO Dan Coster and CTO Yoav Gill Ben Ephraim. Coster said, "The next generation of data platforms can’t depend on a person deciding how every workload should run. That dependence on manual work is becoming a barrier to AI adoption at scale. As agents create more workloads, the infrastructure needs to make its own decisions. We built Zipher to be that brain, learning each workload and deciding how to run it within the customer’s performance targets and budget."

As our AI and agentic workloads grow, Zipher helps us optimize how those workloads run. Depending on the workload, we’ve seen compute cost reductions in the range of 25% to 40%, while supporting consistent performance through seasonal peaks," says Gaurav Rastogi, Senior Director, Enterprise Data Analytics & BI Platforms, Hertz.
The latest funding will be used for R&D and worldwide marketing. The company will build out US enterprise sales and expand across Europe, Asia, Africa and Latin America.

articles.title: Elbit Systems wins German naval electronic warfare deal
articles.summary: Under the contract, Elbit Systems Deutschland will supply its Aqua Marine system to Thyssenkrupp Marine Systems (TKMS).
paragraphs: Under the contract, Elbit Systems Deutschland will supply its Aqua Marine system to Thyssenkrupp Marine Systems (TKMS).

Israeli defense electronics company Elbit Systems Ltd. (Nasdaq: ESLT; TASE:ESLT) German subsidiary, Elbit Systems Deutschland GmbH, has won a contract to supply naval electronic warfare (EW) systems, which will be performed over five years.

Under the contract, Elbit Systems Deutschland will supply its Aqua Marine system to Thyssenkrupp Marine Systems (TKMS). The system is an integrated naval self-protection suite against electronic warfare and will be supplied for the German Navy’s F-128 frigates.

The modular suite combines passive and active EW capabilities to detect, identify and analyze threats, and provides advanced electronic self-protection and electronic attack capabilities. Designed to operate in complex, dense maritime environments, the system provides enhanced situational awareness, rapid response, electronic intelligence and interoperability between naval platforms.

The deal has been concluded about a month after Elbit expanded its presence in the naval market by acquiring Canadian company ISE (International Submarine Engineering Ltd.), which specializes in autonomous and remotely operated underwater systems.

Although the purchase price is immaterial to Elbit, the deal reflects growing interest in unmanned underwater vehicles by naval forces. ISE, a technology company based in the Vancouver area of Canada, develops and manufactures underwater vehicles, including autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) and remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), as well as computerized control systems and robotics. With more than 50 years of experience in underwater robotics, ISE has supplied more than 250 underwater vehicles to customers in more than 20 countries worldwide.

Elbit Systems’ naval portfolio already includes unmanned vessels, underwater systems, integrated command and control (C2) systems, electro-optical and sonar systems, and communications and electronic warfare technologies. Through its subsidiaries and global centers of excellence, Elbit Systems provides operationally proven naval capabilities for missions ranging from coastal security to deep-water operations.

Elbit’s unmanned surface vessels have a major reputation in the international market. Thew company’s Seagull, for example, took part in the international Digital Horizon exercise in December 2022. The exercise, held in the Persian Gulf close to Iran, tested cooperation among 17 unmanned vessel manufacturers from around the world. It was hosted by the US Fifth Fleet, whose home base is in the Bahrain capital Manama. Seagull is an unmanned surface vessel designed for anti-ship warfare.

articles.title: נפתחה ההרשמה לתוכנית ה-Deep Tech MBA של אוניברסיטת תל אביב
articles.summary: אם אתם קוראים את זה, כנראה שיש לכם מומחיות טכנולוגית בעולמות הפיתוח והמחקר. אבל האם אתם יודעים להפוך אותה ליכולת לנהל עסק או יחידה עסקית, או להוביל מיזם המתבסס על טכנולוגיה עמוקה? פיתוח טכנולוגיה פורצת דרך הוא רק חלק מהדרך להפוך רעיון לחברה מצליחה. בתחומים כמו AI, סייבר, רובוטיקה, ביוטכנולוגיה, טכנולוגיות רפואיות, אקלים ו-Deep Tech, […]
paragraphs: תוכנית Coller Deep Tech MBA לא נשארת ברמת התיאוריה (צילום: Dreamstime)
אם אתם קוראים את זה, כנראה שיש לכם מומחיות טכנולוגית בעולמות הפיתוח והמחקר. אבל האם אתם יודעים להפוך אותה ליכולת לנהל עסק או יחידה עסקית, או להוביל מיזם המתבסס על טכנולוגיה עמוקה?

פיתוח טכנולוגיה פורצת דרך הוא רק חלק מהדרך להפוך רעיון לחברה מצליחה. בתחומים כמו AI, סייבר, רובוטיקה, ביוטכנולוגיה, טכנולוגיות רפואיות, אקלים ו-Deep Tech, האתגר אינו רק לפתח פתרון מבריק, אלא גם להפוך אותו לחברה מצליחה או למוצר מסחרי.

בין המעבדה לשוק, אתם עומדים להיתקל בלא מעט אתגרים ושאלות: איך בונים מודל עסקי סביב פתרון טכנולוגי? איך מגייסים השקעה, מזהים שוק פוטנציאלי ומקבלים החלטות אסטרטגיות? וכיצד מובילים צוות וארגון כשהמוצר מבוסס על טכנולוגיה עמוקה שעדיין לא בשלה לכדי מוצר מסחרי?

אלה בדיוק האתגרים שעומדים במרכז תוכנית Coller Deep-Tech MBA הבינלאומית באוניברסיטת תל אביב. בניגוד לתוכניות הכשרה קצרות, מדובר בתואר MBA אקדמי מלא שנבנה במיוחד עבור נשות ואנשי טכנולוגיה, הנדסה, מדעים, מחקר, יזמות וניהול פיתוח ומוצר, שרוצים להרחיב את ארגז הכלים המקצועי שלהם ולהשתלב גם בצד העסקי של תעשיית הדיפטק הישראלית והבינלאומית.
תיאוריה לצד התנסות מעשית ובניית קשרים מקצועיים
התוכנית, שנמשכת שנתיים ונלמדת באנגלית, מתמקדת בחיבור בין דיפטק למצוינות עסקית וניהולית. תלמדו על:
יזמות טכנולוגית ופיתוח מודלים עסקיים
מסחור טכנולוגיות והעברת ידע מהמחקר לתעשייה
אסטרטגיה עסקית וניהול חברות טכנולוגיה
מימון, הון-סיכון והערכת השקעות
ניהול חדשנות, מוצר וצמיחה
מנהיגות, משא ומתן וקבלת החלטות במצבי אי-ודאות
ניהול ארגונים וצוותים טכנולוגיים
היכרות עם שווקים גלובליים ועם האקוסיסטם של תחום הדיפטק

הלימודים לא נשארים ברמת התיאוריה: במסגרת Venture Builder תוכלו להתנסות בפיתוח רעיון טכנולוגי לכדי מיזם עסקי, לנתח הזדמנויות השקעה, להשתתף בסימולציות של ועדות השקעה ודירקטוריונים ולהתמודד עם תרחישים של משא ומתן ופתרון קונפליקטים, ניתוח אתגרים עסקיים אמיתיים וקבלת החלטות אסטרטגיות.

הייחוד של התוכנית טמון גם בחיבור לאנשים ולחברות שפועלים באקוסיסטם הדיפטק בישראל ובעולם. המשתתפים יפגשו יזמים, משקיעים ומנהלים בכירים, וייחשפו לאתגרים עסקיים וטכנולוגיים מהשטח. המחזור מתוכנן לכלול עד 25 משתתפים, כדי לאפשר עבודה בקבוצות קטנות ובניית קשרים מקצועיים משמעותיים.

הלימודים ההיברידיים מתאימים במיוחד עבור מי שכבר נמצאים בעיצומה של הקריירה – הם משלבים למידה מקוונת עם שישה שבועות לימוד מלא, הנפרסים לאורך התואר ובמשך שנתיים בקמפוס אוניברסיטת תל אביב. כך תוכלו להמשיך לעבוד במקביל ללימודים, בלי לוותר על מפגש פנים אל פנים ועל קהילה מקצועית בינלאומית.

ההרשמה למחזור השני של התוכנית פתוחה עד 15 בדצמבר 2026. תנאי הקבלה כוללים תואר ראשון בתחומי המדעים, ההנדסה, הטכנולוגיה או המחשבים, ניסיון מקצועי של שלוש שנים לפחות ויכולת לימוד באנגלית. הליך המיון כולל בחינת הרקע האקדמי והמקצועי וריאיון אישי.

articles.title: From fighting cancer to targeting aging: The science driving Dr. Sharon Shacham
articles.summary: WATCH: Dr. Sharon Shacham, CEO and co-founder of Regenimo Biosciences, in conversation with Jake Laznik, Senior Breaking News Desk Manager, The Jerusalem Post.
paragraphs: WATCH: Dr. Sharon Shacham, CEO and co-founder of Regenimo Biosciences, in conversation with Jake Laznik, Senior Breaking News Desk Manager, The Jerusalem Post.

“We are living in an amazing age, when some of the most devastating cancers, which once left patients with only a few months to live, are becoming chronic, manageable diseases,” says Dr. Sharon Shacham, an Israeli scientist and biotech entrepreneur whose work has helped lead the development of a new approach to treating cancer. Dr. Shacham's background spans chemistry, biochemistry, computational physics, protein modeling, and business.

Shacham, who co-founded Karyopharm Therapeutics, is today the CEO and co-founder of Regenimo Biosciences, a company developing new drugs aimed at extending the human health span by targeting biological mechanisms linked to aging.
She received all of her academic degrees at Tel Aviv University, including a Bachelor of Science in Chemistry, a Ph.D. in Biophysical Chemistry, and an MBA with a focus on information systems.

Shacham says that she was inspired to pursue a career in science by the lives of two women – Marie Curie, the first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the only person to win a Nobel Prize in two different scientific fields, and her grandmother, who was a member of the Haganah.

Of Madam Curie, she says, “I read her biography when I was 10 years old and was fascinated by her life and by the courage and curiosity she had in her scientific efforts. So I knew I wanted to be a scientist.”

When Shacham was fifteen, her grandmother was stricken with Alzheimer’s disease. “Since then,” says Shacham, “I have had the passion to fight some of these terrible diseases. We have made much progress, but we still have a way to go to help people who are suffering from these devastating diseases have a better life.”

What has given Dr. Shacham the confidence to pursue her scientific dreams? “A little bit has to do with Tel Aviv University,” she says, “and a lot has to do with being Israeli, knowing there is a way, and being a dreamer. Being Israeli is very important, because we see the light, we dream about the light, and we can feel the fire.”

Shacham says that Tel Aviv University has an amazing entrepreneurial spirit and an excellent network. “I was always encouraged: ‘Don’t stay in your lab. Look at the world and think about what more you can do.’ In my undergraduate work, I didn’t just learn chemistry. I learned to think. In my Ph.D. program, I learned how to use these tools and apply them to big problems. It's very unique to Tel Aviv University. Today, as an alumna, I work with fellow graduates to strengthen our network and explore how we can support the university—and how it can help us achieve our goals.”
This article was written in collaboration with Tel Aviv University.

articles.title: Should CrowdStrike-Zscaler merger alarm Israel’s cyber firms?
articles.summary: While the growing dominance of cybersecurity giants may pose challenges for independent companies, it could also make startups with unique technologies highly sought-after acquisition.
paragraphs: While the growing dominance of cybersecurity giants may pose challenges for independent companies, it could also make startups with unique technologies highly sought-after acquisition.

CrowdStrike’s $44 billion acquisition of Zscaler represents the peak of a massive wave of acquisitions in the cybersecurity sector over the past few years with many of the deals involving Israeli companies.

Notable transactions include Google’s acquisition of Israeli firm Wiz for $32 billion, Cisco’s acquisition of Splunk ($28 billion), and Palo Alto Networks’ acquisition of Israel’s CyberArk ($25 billion). Also included are ServiceNow’s acquisition of Israeli company Armis for $7.75 billion, and Proofpoint’s acquisition of Israeli-founded data security firm Varonis, announced last month, for about $6.3 billion.
700 CyberArk employees to lose jobs after $25b exit

These five deals, alongside the acquisition involving Zscaler, reach a cumulative value of roughly $144 billion. This figure underscores the intensity of consolidation within the industry, as technology and cybersecurity giants invest vast sums to acquire companies and technologies, all in an effort to expand their operations and strengthen their standing in a highly competitive market.

And how will this impact Israel? CrowdStrike employs over 500 people in Israel, following its acquisition of several Israeli companies, including Bionic, Flow Security, and Adaptive Shield. Zscaler has also expanded its local operations through acquisitions; and according to media reports, it employs about 200 people in Israel.

However, the implications may extend well beyond the merger’s impact on local employees. Technology investment fund Lucid Capital founder and CEO Shahar Cohen suggests that the deal could actually harm the Israeli cybersecurity industry, as it reinforces a trend where organizations prefer to procure a range of security services from a single large provider, rather than integrating solutions from smaller, specialized firms.

That said, this remains speculative. While the growing dominance of cybersecurity giants may pose challenges for independent companies, it could also make startups with unique technologies highly sought-after acquisition targets. The broader question now is not merely which firm will emerge as the largest cybersecurity company, but whether organizations will continue to source security solutions from a diverse array of vendors or instead choose to entrust the bulk of their defensive infrastructure to a handful of industry giants. With its $44 billion deal, CrowdStrike is betting on the latter scenario.

articles.title: BoI governor: We're seeing inflationary pressures
articles.summary: Explaining the Bank of Israel's decision not to cut interest rates, Governor of the Bank of Israel Amir Yaron points to depreciation of the shekel and expected global interest rate hikes.
paragraphs: The annual rate of inflation in Israel has dropped to just 1.1%, near the lower bound of the Bank of Israel’s 1-3% target range, yet the interest rate remains unchanged. The Monetary Committee decided yesterday to hold the rate at 3.25% for the second consecutive time, citing the sharp depreciation of the shekel, global expectations of interest rate hikes, and both local and global uncertainty. Since the previous interest rate decision, the shekel has lost 7.6% of its value against the US dollar and 5.1% against the euro, a development that could reignite inflationary pressures within the economy.

Talking to "Globes" following the announcement, Governor of the Bank of Israel Amir Yaron explained why the Bank decided not to continue a trend of interest rate cuts, despite the sharp decline in inflation.

"First of all, we have lowered the interest rate; we have already implemented five cuts, three of them consecutive," said Yaron. "We are in an environment shrouded in uncertainty, uncertainties that are both global and local, spanning a wide range of areas."

Yaron says that the bank does not limit itself to examining current inflation. "We no longer look solely at one recent data point or another. Looking ahead, inflation is expected to rise toward the middle of the target range in 2027, and forecasters are already projecting that, a year from now, it will be above the midpoint of the range.

"The depreciation of the currency coupled with a high probability of further interest rate hikes globally will continue to exert inflationary pressure. Furthermore, we see an economy with a high level of activity and low unemployment. Taking all of this into account, it is crucial that we continue to act with responsibility and caution."
"The exchange rate is volatile, but the direction is clear"

One of the primary factors behind the decision is the sharp depreciation of the shekel. Since the previous interest rate decision, the Israeli currency has weakened by 7.6% against the US dollar, partly because of the turmoil in global stock markets. This depreciation could drive up the cost of imported goods and push inflation back upward.

Asked to what extent the foreign exchange market influenced the decision, Yaron noted that some of the impact of the depreciation was already factored into inflation forecasts. "We know that appreciation generally leads to a moderation in inflation, while depreciation works in the opposite direction. We have various historical estimates. It should be understood that since the Covid-19 pandemic, the exchange rate’s transmission mechanism has been volatile, though the general direction is clear to us."
Shekel depreciation continues amid global market selloff
Israel’s economy grew at 8% in Q3

Yaron warned that the anticipated interest rate differentials between Israel and the rest of the world could intensify pressure on prices. "The fact that significant depreciation has already occurred, compounded by the likelihood that interest rate gaps will widen further, will exert even greater inflationary pressure."
The institutions and the Shekel: "We’ve taken steps to mitigate the impact"

In the interview, Yaron also addressed the growing impact of investment institutions on the exchange rate. In recent years, the institutions have expanded their exposure to foreign stock markets, primarily in the US, and their hedging activities have emerged as a key factor in dollar-shekel trading.

Asked how the Bank of Israel is dealing with the exchange rate’s increasing sensitivity to fluctuations in US stock markets, Yaron replied: "First of all, let me put it this way: the foreign exchange market is one of the deepest markets in Israel, if not the deepest. Generally speaking, we want to see it as a free market driven by its own participants."

Nevertheless, the governor noted that the Bank of Israel had already taken measures designed to mitigate the possible impact of investment institutions’ activities on the exchange rate. "Following the events of the Covid-19 pandemic and other incidents, we took action regarding institutional investors, which manage trillions of shekels in assets and allocate a significant portion to overseas markets, primarily in the US. In coordination with the Capital Markets Authority, we initiated a requirement for them to hold at least a portion of these investments through 'spot' or direct holdings rather than through futures contracts," he said, explaining that the object of this move was to mitigate market pressure during sharp downturns, drawing lessons from past events.
"We’ll decide whether to act on developers’ financing offers"

Another topic that arose in the interview was the future of the Bank of Israel’s restrictions on financing schemes offered by real estate developers, which are set to expire at the end of the year. These restrictions were originally imposed out of concern over transactions in which homebuyers pay only a small fraction of the purchase price upon signing, deferring the remainder to a later date.

"These restrictions were implemented primarily from a consumer-protection perspective," Yaron explained. "The goal is, first and foremost, to ensure that buyers fully understand the nature of the transaction they are entering into, and, hopefully, that they also undergo a full underwriting process."

Yaron noted that a shift in market behavior had been observed since the restrictions were introduced. "Over a period of time, we have indeed seen an improvement in this situation, as well as a reduction in the prevalence of these transactions."

However, Yaron acknowledged that developers have developed new financing models. "Naturally, there is creativity in the sector, and other types of transactions have emerged," he said, adding that this "facilitates continued purchases in the market, which in itself is a positive thing."

As to whether the Bank of Israel will extend existing restrictions or impose new ones, the governor said, "We are, of course, monitoring the situation. We will decide exactly what course of action to take, whether to extend the current measures or make slight adjustments in the near future. As always, we will handle this in an orderly fashion, through our internal staff work."

Yaron also addressed the future of the correspondent banking arrangements that facilitate banking ties between Israel and the Palestinian Authority. The current arrangement is set to expire at the end of the year, and the Ministry of Finance is examining alternatives.

"As you know, the existing banking arrangements are slated to remain in place until the end of the year. It is important to find an alternative solution, and there are several possible paths," Yaron said. "We are, of course, assisting the accountant general as much as we can in this matter; it is clearly vital that correspondent banking operations should continue."
Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia: "It fosters stability"

Towards the end of the interview, Yaron was asked about Jensen Huang’s return to the role of Nvidia CEO, following the turbulence the company has experienced in recent weeks, and what this development might mean for the Israeli economy.

"Naturally, I won’t go into specific details," Yaron replied. "Nvidia is, of course, a company of global significance, and it is certainly highly consequential for the Israeli economy. I believe Israel possesses excellent human capital. The company’s presence here is not arbitrary; it likely fosters greater stability from Israel’s perspective. Furthermore, there are compelling reasons for the expansion of their campus here and for Israel’s continued appeal to Nvidia."

Asked about Huang’s personal role in driving investment in Israel, Yaron emphasized that it was more than a matter of a decision by a single individual. "It is clear that he has a significant role in this respect, but I would say that there is also the fundamental aspect of human capital, the employees and what they offer the company. There’s a reason for them being in Israel."
Published by Globes, Israel business news - en.globes.co.il - on November 24, 2026.

articles.title: עוד 320 מיליון דולר להשקעות בסטארטאפים ישראלים
articles.summary: מתוך כ-200 קרנות הון סיכון בישראל, פחות מעשר מתמקדות בשלבי צמיחה מאוחרים, זאת למרות שהיקף ההשקעות בתחום זינק לכ-10 מיליארד דולר בשנה שעברה. למגרש הזה נכנסת קרן Key1 Capital, שהודיעה על סגירה ראשונה של 320 מיליון דולר לקרן השנייה שלה. על פי הודעת הקרן, כ-95% מההתחייבויות להשקעה הגיעו מגופים מוסדיים, פאמילי אופיסס ויזמים שכבר השקיעו […]
paragraphs: מתוך כ-200 קרנות הון סיכון בישראל, פחות מעשר מתמקדות בשלבי צמיחה מאוחרים, זאת למרות שהיקף ההשקעות בתחום זינק לכ-10 מיליארד דולר בשנה שעברה. למגרש הזה נכנסת קרן Key1 Capital, שהודיעה על סגירה ראשונה של 320 מיליון דולר לקרן השנייה שלה.

על פי הודעת הקרן, כ-95% מההתחייבויות להשקעה הגיעו מגופים מוסדיים, פאמילי אופיסס ויזמים שכבר השקיעו בקרן הראשונה, שהוקמה ב-2022 על ידי בכירי גולדמן זאקס לשעבר דני אקרמן, שראל אלדור ועמית פילובסקי. הקרן הראשונה רשמה שני אקזיטים בולטים: SuperPlay ו-DustPhotonics, והציגה, על פי נתוני הקרן, תשואה פנימית נטו (או Net IRR) של 20.6%.
לא משקיעים במודלים אלא בטכנולוגיות שמאפשרות אותם

בפורטפוליו הקיים של הקרן נמצאות חברות כמו WEKA, Xsight Labs ו-Sentra של מפקד 8200 לשעבר שגייסה 150 מיליון דולר בתחילת החודש. "אנחנו לא משקיעים במודלי AI. אנחנו מתמקדים בטכנולוגיות ובתשתיות שמאפשרות את הפיתוח שלהם: שבבים, תקשורת, דאטה, אבטחת מידע ואפליקציות ייחודיות", מסביר שראל אלדור, שותף מייסד בקרן. "ישראל צברה לאורך עשרות שנים מומחיות בתחומים האלה".

עמית פילובסקי, שותף מייסד בקרן, מוסיף: "השאיפה כיום היא להקים חברות גלובליות עם מובילות תחום ברורה. לפני עשור היו בישראל פחות מעשר חברות שהגיעו לשווי של מיליארד דולר כל אחת, והיום יש יותר ממאה". דני אקרמן, השותף המייסד השלישי, מסכם כי "התפקיד שלנו הוא להביא לשולחן את הניסיון העסקי והפיננסי שנדרש בצמתים האלה".

articles.title: Gideon Tadmor's Numerios raises capital at NIS 1.2b valuation
articles.summary: The money raised, in equity and debt, will be used to acquire a data center in Kansas.
paragraphs: The money raised, in equity and debt, will be used to acquire a data center in Kansas.

The Numerios partnership, which is active in data centers and controlled by Gideon Tadmor, has completed raising an estimated NIS 400 million at a valuation of NIS 1.2 billion. The participants in the raise were Poalim Equity, Discount Capital, the Goren family, and other major investors, and Tadmor Grup, which invested a substantial portion of the total.

In addition, the partnership raised debt of some $375 million, mostly from a consortium led by Morgan Stanley in the US and with the participation of the four largest Israeli banks: Hapoalim, Discount, Leumi, and Mizrahi Tefahot. The remainder, 20%, was raised from Israeli investment management firm Cogito Capital Fund.
The money raised will be used for, among other things, financing the equity in a deal for the purchase of a data center in Kansas.
